Switch off unused appliances, use LED lights, and choose inverter appliances that use less electricity.
statements.tl:
Ano ang ilang paraan upang makatipid ng energy sa bahay?

Patayin ang mga hindi ginagamit na appliances, gumamit ng LED lights, at pumili ng mga inverter appliances na mas kaunti ang gamit na kuryente.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17S8pbolvIjWyrC4nk0KN_I74ri7B4tqC), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Can we lower the electric bill without buying a new appliance?

Yes! Simply reducing the hours of use of high-power appliances like the electric iron or water heater lowers the total kilowatt-hours consumed.
statements.tl:
Pwede ba nating mapababa ang electric bill nang hindi bumibili ng bagong appliance?

Oo! Ang pagbawas lang ng oras ng paggamit ng mga high-power na appliance tulad ng plantsa o water heater ay nagpapababa sa kabuuang kilowatt-hour na nakokonsumo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1AH3VYawMvIcfxJCk5j7pSBX-Fx7nz373), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Is renewable energy too expensive for homes?

The initial installation, like for solar panels, can be costly, but in the long run it reduces your electricity bill by powering your appliances for free.
statements.tl:
Masyado bang mahal ang renewable energy para sa mga bahay?

Ang paunang pag-install, tulad ng solar panels, ay maaaring magastos, pero sa katagalan, binabawasan nito ang iyong electric bill sa pamamagitan ng libreng pagpapaandar ng iyong mga appliances.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GeBNfUkD7aIxwv_GZTGzoieGpq-GInAn), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Earth Hour is a worldwide movement organized by the World Wildlife Fund to encourage people to turn off lights for one hour to save energy.
statements.tl: Ang Earth Hour ay isang pandaigdigang kilusan na inorganisa ng World Wildlife Fund upang hikayatin ang mga tao na patayin ang mga ilaw sa loob ng isang oras upang makatipid ng enerhiya.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1gLlsocYxWQJOAqTxRTsyzzM4srvXGHaO), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: We help the environment and save money when we simply turn off the lights and appliances we are not using!
statements.tl: Nakakatulong tayo sa kapaligiran at nakakatipid ng pera kapag pinapatay natin ang mga ilaw at gamit na hindi ginagamit!

statements.text:
Are your appliances secretly drinking power?

Many appliances keep drawing a little electricity even when switched off, as long as they stay plugged in!
statements.tl:
Lihim bang kumukuha ng kuryente ang mga aparato?

Maraming aparato ang patuloy na kumukuha ng kaunting kuryente kahit naka-off, basta naka-plug pa rin sila!

statements.text:
Is your empty charger still working?

A charger left plugged in still pulls some electricity even when no phone is attached!
statements.tl:
Gumagana pa ba ang walang cell phone na charger?

Ang charger na naka-saksak ay sumisipsip pa rin ng kuryente kahit walang nakakabit na cellphone!

statements.text: An LED bulb gives the same brightness but uses much less electricity than an old incandescent bulb!
statements.tl: Ang LED na bombilya ay nagbibigay ng parehong liwanag pero gumagamit ng mas kaunting kuryente kaysa lumang incandescent na bombilya!

statements.text:
Which home appliance is the biggest power eater?

An air conditioner is one of the home appliances that uses the most electricity.
statements.tl:
Aling aparato sa bahay ang pinakamalakas kumain ng kuryente?

Ang aircon ay isa sa mga aparato sa bahay na pinakamaraming kuryenteng ginagamit.
statements.source: U.S. DOE home energy use; encyclopedia-stable

statements.text: An electric fan uses much less electricity than an air conditioner, so it is cheaper to run!
statements.tl: Ang electric fan ay gumagamit ng mas kaunting kuryente kaysa aircon, kaya mas mura itong patakbuhin!

statements.text:
How can you save electricity when doing laundry?

Load the washing machine to its rated capacity! Running one full load saves more electricity than doing many small loads.
statements.tl:
Paano ka makakatipid ng kuryente kapag naglalaba?

Lagyan ang washing machine hanggang sa nakatakdang kapasidad nito! Mas nakakatipid ng kuryente ang isang punong laba kaysa sa madalas na maliit na laba.

statements.text:
How do you know which appliance is more energy-efficient?

Check the energy labels! They tell you exactly how little electricity an appliance uses, helping you pick the best one.
statements.tl:
Paano mo malalaman kung aling aparato ang mas matipid sa kuryente?

Tignan ang energy labels! Sinasabi nila kung gaano katipid ang aparato sa kuryente, para makapili ka ng mas matipid.
statements.source: Energy efficiency labeling (PH DOE / Energy Star); stable

statements.text:
What should you do with your TV and computer at bedtime?

Fully turn them off! Don't just leave them on standby when it's time to sleep.
statements.tl:
Ano ang dapat mong gawin sa TV at computer mo kapag tutulog ka na?

Patayin nang husto! Huwag lang iwanang naka-standby ang TV at computer kapag oras na ng tulog.

statements.text: Watch out! Electricity wasted by things left plugged in but unused is still paid for on your bill.
statements.tl: Mag-ingat! Ang kuryenteng nasasayang sa mga gamit na naka-plug pero hindi ginagamit ay binabayaran pa rin sa bill.

statements.text:
Why is a power strip with a switch so helpful?

It lets you turn off many devices at once! This stops them from wasting standby power.
statements.tl:
Bakit nakakatulong ang isang extension na may switch?

Pwede mong patayin ang maraming aparato nang sabay-sabay! Ito ang pumipigil sa pagsasayang ng standby power.
statements.source: U.S. DOE smart power strip tip; stable

statements.text: Shear stress happens when two plates rub against each other in opposite directions at transform fault boundaries.
statements.tl: Ang shear stress ay nangyayari kapag ang dalawang plate ay nagkikiskisan sa magkasalungat na direksyon sa transform fault boundaries.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The force of separation at a divergent boundary creates a tension zone, where shallow earthquakes may happen.
statements.tl: Ang lakas ng paghihiwalay sa divergent boundary ay lumilikha ng tension zone, kung saan maaaring maganap ang mababaw na lindol.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1cqlpmCutye6Nrn93DzHR-JoS-MKBrsre), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: There are three plate boundaries: convergent — plates collide and one subducts or land crunches up; divergent — plates move apart and new crust forms; transform — plates slide horizontally past each other with no crust created or destroyed.
statements.tl: May tatlong plate boundaries: convergent — nagtatagpo ang mga plato at isa ang nagsa-subduct o kumukulubot ang lupa; divergent — lumalayò ang mga plato at nabubuo ang bagong crust; transform — pahalang na dumudulas ang mga plato nang walang crust na nabubuo o nawawala.

statements.text:
What happens when plates crash into each other?

At a convergent boundary, plates push and collide! This creates tall mountains, deep trenches, and lots of earthquakes and volcanoes.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagbanggaan ang mga plato?

Sa convergent boundary, nagtutulak at nagbabanggaan ang mga plato! Dito nabubuo ang matataas na kabundukan, malalalim na trench, lindol, at bulkan.

statements.text: Compression is the stress that squeezes rocks together at convergent boundaries, and it is the force that builds mountains.
statements.tl: Ang compression ay ang stress na pumipiga sa mga bato sa convergent boundaries, at ito ang puwersa na bumubuo ng mga bundok.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When spreading continues at a divergent boundary, the crust may break into segments and form a rift valley, which can grow into a linear sea like the Red Sea.
statements.tl: Kapag nagpapatuloy ang pagkalat sa divergent boundary, ang crust ay maaaring mabasag sa mga segment at bumuo ng rift valley, na maaaring lumaki at maging linear sea tulad ng Red Sea.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The East Pacific Rise is another example of a divergent boundary where new oceanic crust forms as plates move apart.
statements.tl: Ang East Pacific Rise ay isa pang halimbawa ng divergent boundary kung saan nabubuo ang bagong oceanic crust habang naghihiwalay ang mga plate.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Convergent boundaries are called destructive because crust is recycled into the mantle when one plate subducts beneath another.
statements.tl: Ang convergent boundaries ay tinatawag na destructive dahil ang crust ay bumabalik sa mantle kapag ang isang plate ay sumusubduct sa ilalim ng isa pa.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Harry Hess proposed seafloor spreading, where new oceanic crust forms at mid-ocean ridges and moves away on each side.
statements.tl: Iminungkahi ni Harry Hess ang seafloor spreading, kung saan nabubuo ang bagong oceanic crust sa mid-ocean ridges at gumagalaw palayo sa bawat panig.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1CC-09Q5LWQPrHRoQx1Ofzr4JXiruUTAW), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Volcanic activity is common at divergent boundaries because magma easily moves to the surface through the thin, fractured rock as the plates separate.
statements.tl: Karaniwan ang volcanic activity sa divergent boundaries dahil madaling umaakyat ang magma sa manipis at bitak-bitak na bato habang naghihiwalay ang mga plates.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1FaGu3pfCjb26gKmYQIUlCd2tCKLca8Uj), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Tectonic plates push each other, slide past each other, and drift away from each other along their boundaries.
statements.tl: Ang mga tectonic plate ay nagtutulakan, dumudulas sa isa't isa, at naghihiwalay sa isa't isa sa kanilang mga boundary.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1LXHXazR3p9VcbEDCB1uxc9rZES5YOwVx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Different plate boundaries create different landforms: divergent boundaries make ridges, convergent boundaries make mountains and volcanoes, and transform boundaries make fault lines.
statements.tl: Iba't ibang plate boundary ang bumubuo ng iba't ibang anyong lupa: ang divergent boundaries ay gumagawa ng ridges, ang convergent boundaries ay bumubuo ng mga bundok at bulkan, at ang transform boundaries ay gumagawa ng fault lines.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1RUuL2GI3TdzhKiNZ94TeHeUBGrpiLs9n), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A convergent boundary forms where two plates move toward each other, causing one plate to bend downward or both plates to crumple.
statements.tl: Nabubuo ang convergent boundary kung saan naglalapit ang dalawang plate, na nagiging sanhi ng pagyuko pababa ng isang plate o pagkunot ng dalawang plate.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1VHHZVuic8Wx0_ZbypEXpvvNB6x6wBl2Q), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A continental volcanic arc is a chain of volcanoes on a continent that forms parallel to a trench at an oceanic-continental convergent boundary.
statements.tl: Ang continental volcanic arc ay isang hanay ng mga bulkan sa isang kontinente na nabubuo kahanay ng trench sa oceanic-continental convergent boundary.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1VHHZVuic8Wx0_ZbypEXpvvNB6x6wBl2Q), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: As plates pull away from each other, a long depression called a rift valley is created.
statements.tl: Habang naghihiwalay ang mga plate, nabubuo ang isang mahabang mababang lupain na tinatawag na rift valley.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1cqlpmCutye6Nrn93DzHR-JoS-MKBrsre), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A convergent boundary is where two tectonic plates move toward each other and collide, causing one plate to bend or sink.
statements.tl: Ang convergent boundary ay kung saan ang dalawang tectonic plates ay gumagalaw papunta sa isa't isa at nagbanggaan, kaya ang isang plate ay nababaluktot o lumulubog.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1fPGla1FN3DHCh2rLsSH4BmifaHcv_FZw), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A convergent plate boundary happens when two tectonic plates move toward each other, and this powerful collision is called a destructive boundary.
statements.tl: Ang convergent plate boundary ay nangyayari kapag ang dalawang tectonic plates ay gumagalaw palapit sa isa't isa, at ang malakas na banggaang ito ay tinatawag na destructive boundary.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-17998), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A rift valley is a gap formed between two plates moving apart at a divergent boundary, like the African Rift Valley.
statements.tl: Ang rift valley ay isang puwang na nabubuo sa pagitan ng dalawang plates na lumalayo sa divergent boundary, tulad ng African Rift Valley.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-17998), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Oil and coal are fossil fuels! They took millions of years to form, so they run out and can't be replaced quickly.
statements.tl: Ang langis at karbon ay fossil fuels! Milyon-milyong taon ang kinailangan upang mabuo sila, kaya nauubos sila at hindi agad napapalitan.

statements.text: Examples of renewable energy are solar (Sun), wind, hydro (water), geothermal (Earth's heat), and biomass!
statements.tl: Ang mga halimbawa ng renewable energy ay solar (araw), wind (hangin), hydro (tubig), geothermal (init ng lupa), at biomass!

statements.text:
Where does the pollution from electricity come from?

It comes from power plants that burn fossil fuels like coal and crude oil, releasing harmful gases into the air.
statements.tl:
Saan nagmumula ang polusyon mula sa kuryente?

Nagmumula ito sa mga power plant na nagsusunog ng fossil fuels tulad ng coal at crude oil, na naglalabas ng mga mapanganib na gas sa hangin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17S8pbolvIjWyrC4nk0KN_I74ri7B4tqC), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Most renewable energy is clean! It doesn't release much smoke or harmful gas into the air, making it way better for our planet than burning coal or oil.
statements.tl: Karamihan sa renewable energy ay malinis! Hindi ito naglalabas ng maraming usok o nakakalasong gas, kaya mas maganda ito para sa kalikasan kaysa pagsunog ng karbon o langis.

statements.text: The ocean's power makes renewable energy! Rising and falling tides and big waves have the force to spin a turbine and make electricity.
statements.tl: Ang lakas ng dagat ay pwedeng gawing renewable energy! Ang pagtaas at pagbaba ng tides at malalaking alon ay puwedeng magpaikot ng turbine para sa kuryente.

statements.text: A hydroelectric plant burns no fuel or coal, so it gives off no smoke or air pollution while it makes electricity!
statements.tl: Ang hydroelectric plant ay hindi nagsusunog ng gasolina o karbon, kaya hindi ito naglalabas ng usok o polusyon sa hangin habang gumagawa ng kuryente!

statements.text: Run-of-river hydro plants use a river's natural flow without a large storage lake. This means they flood much less land around them!
statements.tl: Ang run-of-river hydro plants ay gumagamit ng natural na daloy ng ilog nang walang malaking storage lake. Kaya mas kaunti ang nababahaing lupa sa paligid!

statements.text: Tiny micro-hydro plants use small streams to bring electricity to remote mountain villages that big power lines haven't reached yet!
statements.tl: Ang maliliit na micro-hydro plants ay gumagamit ng maliliit na sapa para magdala ng kuryente sa mga liblib na nayong nasa kabundukan na hindi pa naaabot ng malalaking linya ng kuryente!

statements.text: Even though hydro power is clean, building a big reservoir floods land and sometimes forces people living there to move away.
statements.tl: Kahit malinis ang hydro power, ang paggawa ng malaking reservoir ay nagbabaha ng lupa at minsan ay pinipilit ang mga tao na lumipat.

statements.text:
Why do fossil fuels run out so fast?

We use them way faster than they form! We burn in just a few decades what took millions of years to make.
statements.tl:
Bakit mabilis maubos ang fossil fuels?

Ginagamit natin sila nang napakabilis! Sa loob lang ng ilang dekada, nauubos natin ang pinangailangan ng milyun-milyong taon para mabuo ulit.

statements.text:
What is biomass energy made from?

Biomass energy comes from things that were once alive, like wood or crop leftovers. It is renewable if we keep growing new plants to replace them!
statements.tl:
Saan galing ang enerhiya ng biomass?

Ang enerhiya ng biomass ay mula sa mga bagay na buhay dati, tulad ng kahoy o tira ng pananim. Renewable ito kung patuloy tayong nagtatanim ng kapalit!

statements.text:
Why do we need batteries for renewable energy?

Renewable energy never runs out, but it's not always available! There is no solar at night and no wind when calm, so we need batteries to store it.
statements.tl:
Bakit kailangan natin ng baterya para sa renewable energy?

Hindi nauubos ang renewable energy, pero hindi rin ito palaging available! Walang solar sa gabi at walang hangin kapag kalmado, kaya kailangan ng baterya para mag-imbak.

statements.text:
What do we use different fossil fuels for?

Coal is burned in power plants for electricity, oil is made into gasoline for vehicles, and natural gas is used for cooking and heating!
statements.tl:
Ano ang mga gamit ng iba't ibang fossil fuels?

Ang karbon ay sinusunog sa power plant para sa kuryente, ang langis ay ginagawang gasolina para sa sasakyan, at ang natural gas ay para sa pagluluto at pag-init!

statements.text:
Where in the Philippines can we find a big geothermal field?

In Tongonan, Leyte, there's a huge geothermal field that powers many homes across the Visayas! It's a real-life example of how the Philippines uses the Earth's heat for electricity.
statements.tl:
Saan sa Pilipinas makikita ang malaking geothermal field?

Sa Tongonan, Leyte, may malaking geothermal field na nagbibigay ng kuryente sa maraming bahay sa Visayas! Ito ay tunay na halimbawa kung paano ginagamit ng Pilipinas ang init ng lupa para sa kuryente.

statements.text: Geothermal energy is renewable because the Earth's heat never runs out—it's always there! It's also cleaner than coal since it releases much less smoke into the air.
statements.tl: Ang geothermal energy ay renewable dahil hindi nauubos ang init ng Mundo—palaging naroon ito! Mas malinis din ito kaysa sa karbon dahil mas kaunting usok ang nilalabas nito sa hangin.

statements.text:
Why is geothermal cleaner than a coal plant?

Coal plants burn fuel that runs out and makes lots of smoke! Geothermal burns nothing, just using Earth's heat, so it’s cleaner.
statements.tl:
Bakit mas malinis ang geothermal kaysa sa planta ng karbon?

Nagsusunog ang planta ng karbon ng fuel na nauubos at maraming usok! Ang geothermal ay hindi nagsusunog, gumagamit lang ng init ng lupa kaya mas malinis.

statements.text: The Philippines is a top producer of geothermal electricity! Underground heat from our many volcanoes provides a huge share of our national electricity supply.
statements.tl: Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa mga top producer ng geothermal electricity! Ang underground na init mula sa marami nating bulkan ay nagbibigay ng malaking bahagi ng kuryente.

statements.text: Biogas is renewable energy made from digesting pig or carabao dung in a sealed tank! The methane gas it produces is great for cooking and lighting on farms.
statements.tl: Ang biogas ay renewable energy mula sa pag-digest ng dumi ng baboy o kalabaw sa sealed tank! Ang methane gas na nagagawa ay pwedeng gamitin sa pagluluto at ilaw sa bukid.

statements.text:
What is an ocean trench?

It's like a super long, narrow valley carved right into the seafloor!
statements.tl:
Ano ang isang ocean trench?

Ito ay parang napakahaba at makitid na lambak na nakaukit sa sahig ng karagatan!

statements.text: You can find the Philippine Trench on the eastern side of our country, right inside the Pacific Ocean!
statements.tl: Makikita mo ang Philippine Trench sa silangang bahagi ng ating bansa, mismo sa Karagatang Pasipiko!

statements.text: Convergent boundaries create different landforms depending on the plates: trenches and volcanic arcs for oceanic collisions, and mountain ranges for continental collisions.
statements.tl: Ang convergent boundaries ay lumilikha ng iba't ibang anyong lupa depende sa mga plate: trenches at volcanic arcs para sa oceanic collisions, at bulubundukin para sa continental collisions.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 121-uDtX-5IqzkiXeWEKqkzlKaCideMpg), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The Philippines is surrounded by deep ocean trenches like the Philippine Trench! Down in these deep waters, heavy tectonic plates sink down.
statements.tl: Napapaligiran ang Pilipinas ng malalalim na ocean trenches tulad ng Philippine Trench! Sa ilalim ng dagat, naglulubog ang mga plaka.

statements.text: When a plate sinks, very deep ocean trenches form! A great example near us is the Philippine Trench.
statements.tl: Kapag lumulubog ang isang plaka, nabubuo ang napakalalim na ocean trench! Halimbawa dito ay ang Philippine Trench.

statements.text:
Why does the Philippines have so many mountains?

It sits where large tectonic plates meet! The land is constantly pushed up, creating lots of mountains.
statements.tl:
Bakit kaya maraming bundok sa Pilipinas?

Nasa pagtatagpo ito ng malalaking tectonic plates! Patuloy itong itinutulak pataas, kaya lumilikha ng maraming bundok.

statements.text: Fault-block mountains form when huge blocks of rock are lifted up along a crack, called a fault, in the ground!
statements.tl: Ang fault-block mountains ay nabubuo kapag malalaking tipak ng bato ay naitataas sa tabi ng isang biyak, o fault, sa lupa!

statements.text: The ocean floor isn't flat! It has tall mountains, volcanoes, and deep trenches formed by the movement of Earth's plates.
statements.tl: Hindi patag ang ilalim ng dagat! May mga matataas na bundok, bulkan, at malalalim na trench na nabuo dahil sa paggalaw ng Earth's plates.

statements.text: The Philippines is on the "Ring of Fire" with many quakes, volcanoes, and deep ocean trenches, making tsunamis possible here!
statements.tl: Nasa "Ring of Fire" ang Pilipinas na may maraming lindol, bulkan, at malalalim na ocean trench, kaya posibleng magkaroon ng tsunami!

statements.text: The Emden Deep of the Philippine Trench is the third deepest spot in the world! Only the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench and Horizon Deep in the Tonga Trench are deeper.
statements.tl: Ang Emden Deep ng Philippine Trench ay pangatlo sa pinakamalalim na lugar sa buong mundo! Mas malalim lang ang Challenger Deep sa Mariana Trench at ang Horizon Deep sa Tonga Trench.

statements.text: The Philippine Trench is on the east, while the Manila Trench is on the west near the South China Sea. They are in different places and connect to different plates!
statements.tl: Ang Philippine Trench ay nasa silangan ng bansa, habang ang Manila Trench ay nasa kanluran malapit sa South China Sea. Magkaiba sila ng lokasyon at kung saang plate naka-ugnay!

statements.text:
How are the Philippine Trench and Philippine Fault connected?

They are part of the same big plate movement system! Together, the sea trench and land fault cause many earthquakes in our country.
statements.tl:
Paano nagkakaugnay ang Philippine Trench at Philippine Fault?

Pareho silang bahagi ng malaking sistema ng paggalaw ng plate! Magkasama, ang trench sa dagat at fault sa lupa ang nagdudulot ng maraming lindol.

statements.text:
What connects to the Philippine Trench up north near Luzon?

The East Luzon Trough! Together, they form a long line of deep water on the east of our country.
statements.tl:
Ano ang kumokonekta sa Philippine Trench sa hilaga malapit sa Luzon?

Ang East Luzon Trough! Magkasama silang bumubuo ng mahabang guhit ng malalim na tubig sa silangan ng ating bansa.

statements.text: Scientists study the Philippine Trench to understand how earthquakes and tsunamis happen on the east of the country. This knowledge helps us prepare better for disasters!
statements.tl: Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang Philippine Trench para maintindihan kung paano nangyayari ang mga lindol at tsunami sa silangan ng bansa. Mas mapaghahandaan natin ang mga sakuna!

statements.text: Along the eastern edge of the Philippines lies the Philippine Trench—a super deep crack in the sea floor where one plate slides under another. That same motion builds the earthquakes, volcanoes, and islands!
statements.tl: Sa silangang gilid ng Pilipinas ay ang Philippine Trench—isang napakalalim na biyak sa sahig ng dagat kung saan dahan-dahang sumusuot ang isang plaka sa ilalim ng isa. Iyon ang gumagawa ng mga lindol, bulkan, at mga isla!

statements.text:
Why are earthquakes common on our eastern coast?

East of us is the deep Philippine Trench! Here, the Philippine Sea Plate dives down, causing those frequent quakes.
statements.tl:
Bakit malimit magkaroon ng lindol sa silangang baybayin natin?

Sa silangan natin ay ang malalim na Philippine Trench! Dito sumusubsob ang Philippine Sea Plate, kaya malimit ang lindol.

statements.text: More than one plate affects us! The Philippines is squeezed between the large Philippine Sea Plate in the east and the Sunda Plate in the west, causing many quakes and volcanoes.
statements.tl: Hindi lang isa ang plate na may kinalaman sa atin! Naipit ang Pilipinas sa pagitan ng Philippine Sea Plate sa silangan at Sunda Plate sa kanluran, kaya maraming lindol at bulkan.

statements.text: The Manila Trench is a subduction zone west of the Philippines where the South China Sea floor dives under Luzon! It is a potential source of large earthquakes and tsunamis affecting the Luzon coastline!
statements.tl: Ang Manila Trench ay subduction zone sa kanluran ng Pilipinas kung saan ang South China Sea floor ay nagsasalid sa ilalim ng Luzon! Ito potensyal na pinagmumulan ng malalaking lindol at tsunami na maaaring makaapekto sa Luzon!

statements.text: Always write 'in 50 million years' on your sketch — this is geologic time, not a weather forecast for next century!
statements.tl: Laging isulat ang 'pagkalipas ng 50 milyong taon' sa sketch mo — geologic time ito, hindi weather forecast para sa susunod na siglo!

statements.text: The 50-million-year map is called a model! It uses today's measurements and stated assumptions, not a guaranteed future.
statements.tl: Ang 50-million-year map ay tinatawag na model! Ginagamit nito ang mga sukat ngayon at mga ipinahayag na palagay, hindi isang garantisadong hinaharap.

statements.text: At divergent ridges, new seafloor spreads outward at a slow but steady rate of about 2 to 20 centimeters per year.
statements.tl: Sa divergent ridges, ang bagong seafloor ay kumakalat palayo sa bilis na mga 2 hanggang 20 sentimetro kada taon.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The Philippine archipelago may change its position and appearance after 50 million years because the tectonic plates beneath it keep moving.
statements.tl: Maaaring magbago ang posisyon at hitsura ng kapuluan ng Pilipinas pagkatapos ng 50 milyong taon dahil patuloy ang paggalaw ng tectonic plates sa ilalim nito.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1HvWwxZKTNk_tTXlKDRjHV_WJbT8lM5BC), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How fast do the plates at the Philippine Trench move?

Very slowly! Only a few centimeters a year, about as fast as your fingernails grow. But over millions of years, this shapes the sea!
statements.tl:
Gaano kabilis gumagalaw ang mga plate sa Philippine Trench?

Napakabagal! Mga ilang sentimetro lang kada taon, halos kasingbilis ng paglaki ng kuko mo. Pero sa milyong taon, malaki ang epekto nito sa dagat!

statements.text: To predict the archipelago in 50 million years, first measure today's plate velocity from GNSS! Then, assume it stays roughly similar.
statements.tl: Para mahulaan ang arkipelago sa loob ng 50 milyong taon, sukatin muna ang bilis ng plate ngayon mula sa GNSS! Tapos, ipagpalagay na mananatili itong halos pareho.

statements.text: A first sketch multiplies current speed by 50 million years! It converts centimeters per year into kilometers of future displacement.
statements.tl: Ang unang sketch ay minu-multiply ang kasalukuyang bilis sa 50 milyong taon! Gini-convert nito ang sentimetro bawat taon sa kilometro ng magiging paggalaw.

statements.text: The archipelago's future shape depends on more than one plate! The method applies each nearby plate's velocity, not just one number.
statements.tl: Ang magiging hugis ng arkipelago ay nakasalalay sa higit sa isang plate! Ang paraan ay nag-a-apply ng bilis ng bawat kalapit na plate, hindi lang isang numero.

statements.text: When crust dives into a trench, it can actually disappear! So some seafloor may vanish instead of just sliding sideways.
statements.tl: Kapag sumisid ang crust sa trench, pwede itong mawala! Kaya ang ilang seafloor ay maaaring maglaho imbes na dumulas lang.

statements.text:
Can plates change their speed and direction?

Yes! Plate speed and direction can shift over millions of years, so a 50-million-year sketch is just a model, not a promise.
statements.tl:
Pwede bang magbago ang bilis at direksyon ng plate?

Oo! Ang bilis at direksyon ng plate ay pwedeng magbago sa loob ng milyong taon, kaya ang 50-milyong-taong sketch ay modelo lang, hindi pangako.

statements.text: Some methods move the map in small steps, redrawing trenches as they go, instead of one giant 50-million-year jump!
statements.tl: Ang ilang paraan ay inaabante ang mapa sa maliliit na hakbang, muling iginuguhit ang mga trench habang gumagalaw, imbes na isang higanteng talon ng 50 milyong taon.

statements.text:
How can classrooms predict plate movement?

They can use a plate-velocity calculator! Enter today's vector, pick 50 million years, and plot the predicted point.
statements.tl:
Paano hulaan ng classroom ang galaw ng plate?

Pwede silang gumamit ng plate-velocity calculator! Ilagay ang vector ngayon, piliin ang 50 milyong taon, at i-plot ang predicted point.

statements.text:
Do islands only move, or do they change shape too?

Both! Blocks may spread or squeeze, so the archipelago's outline can change even if its center just translates.
statements.tl:
Gumagalaw lang ba ang mga isla, o nagbabago rin ang hugis?

Pareho! Ang mga bloke ay pwedeng kumalat o mapiga, kaya ang outline ng archipelago ay pwedeng magbago kahit ang gitna ay gumagalaw lang.

statements.text:
What does the Philippine Trench do to the seafloor?

It's a boundary that can consume seafloor! This step keeps the future map from being just islands sliding like a rigid sticker.
statements.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng Philippine Trench sa seafloor?

Ito ay boundary na kayang kumain ng seafloor! Step ito para ang future map ay hindi lang mga isla na dumudulas bilang rigid sticker.

statements.text: About two centimeters per year times 50 million years equals about 1,000 kilometers—if that rate truly stayed constant!
statements.tl: Mga dalawang sentimetro bawat taon times 50 milyong taon ay mga 1,000 kilometers—kung talagang nanatiling constant ang rate na iyon!

statements.text: Coastlines erode and grow! So the method predicts the tectonic position of crustal blocks, not today's exact beach outline.
statements.tl: Ang mga coastline ay maaagnas at lalaki! Kaya ang method ay humuhula ng tectonic position ng crustal blocks, hindi ang eksaktong beach outline ngayon.

statements.text: Instead of sliding plates in a straight line, smart methods spin them around an Euler pole — a much better geometric prediction for 50 million years!
statements.tl: Sa halip na idausdos ang plate nang tuwid, iniikot ito ng smart methods sa paligid ng Euler pole — mas magandang geometric prediction para sa 50 milyong taon!

statements.text: When a nearby ridge creates new seafloor, the method must add new area on that side — not just shuffle today's pieces around like furniture!
statements.tl: Kapag gumagawa ng bagong seafloor ang kalapit na ridge, dapat dagdagan ng method ang area roon — hindi lang galawin ang mga piraso ngayon parang furniture!

statements.text:
What pushes and pulls tectonic plates besides convection?

Two forces! 'Slab pull' — a sinking plate's weight drags it down. 'Ridge push' — a raised ridge pushes the plate away!
statements.tl:
Ano ang tumutulak at humihila sa tectonic plates bukod sa convection?

Dalawang puwersa! 'Slab pull' — hinihila ng bigat ng lumulubog na plate pababa. 'Ridge push' — itinutulak ng nakataas na ridge ang plate palayo!

statements.text:
What lies beneath the lithosphere?

The asthenosphere! It is a hotter, softer part of the mantle where the tectonic plates above slowly slide.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nasa ilalim ng lithosphere?

Ang asthenosphere! Ito ay mas mainit at malambot na bahagi ng mantle kung saan dahan-dahang umuusad ang mga plate sa ibabaw.

statements.text: Rheology is the study of how materials flow and deform, and it helps explain how the rigid lithosphere moves over the flowing asthenosphere.
statements.tl: Ang rheology ay ang pag-aaral kung paano dumadaloy at nagde-deform ang mga material, at nakakatulong itong ipaliwanag kung paano gumagalaw ang matigas na lithosphere sa dumadaloy na asthenosphere.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1g5VFVVe8xglsBVQhO8165Rm5JoVm0-li), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Deep inside Earth, very hot, mostly solid rock that flows slowly in the mantle slowly rises and sinks through convection. This slow flow helps move tectonic plates, causing earthquakes and volcanoes!
statements.tl: Sa loob ng Earth, ang napakainit at halos solidong batong mabagal dumaloy sa mantle ay dahan-dahang umaakyat at bumababa sa convection. Tumutulong ang pagdaloy na ito sa paggalaw ng tectonic plates, nagdudulot ng lindol at bulkan!

statements.text:
What moves the ground beneath our feet?

Deep inside Earth, hot rock in the mantle circulates by convection! These currents push tectonic plates, causing earthquakes and volcanoes in the Philippines.
statements.tl:
Ano ang gumagalaw sa ilalim ng ating mga paa?

Sa loob ng Mundo, sobrang init na bato sa mantle ay umiikot sa pamamagitan ng convection! Itinutulak nito ang mga tectonic plate, kaya nagkakaroon ng lindol at bulkan sa Pilipinas.
statements.source: NRC ESS2.B; PHIVOLCS; AAAS BSL Ch.4C

statements.text: Convection happens deep inside the Earth! The very hot mantle slowly circulates as hotter rock rises and cooler rock sinks, pushing the plates that PHIVOLCS studies.
statements.tl: May convection din sa loob ng mundo! Mabagal na umiikot ang napakainit na mantle habang umaakyat ang mainit na bato at bumababa ang malamig, tumutulak sa mga plato na pinag-aaralan ng PHIVOLCS.
statements.source: AAAS BSL Ch.4C; PHIVOLCS; NRC ESS2.B

statements.text:
What helps move tectonic plates on Earth's surface?

Convection currents in the mantle! Heat from the core makes hot rock rise and cooler rock sink, helping drive the movement of tectonic plates!
statements.tl:
Ano ang tumutulong magpagalaw sa mga tectonic plates sa ibabaw ng Earth?

Ang convection currents sa mantle! Ang init mula sa core ay nagpapataas ng mainit na bato at nagpababa ng malamig, tumutulong magpagalaw sa tectonic plates!

statements.text: In the mantle, hot rock rises, cools, and sinks in a slow churn called convection. This pushes Earth's tectonic plates to move!
statements.tl: Sa mantle, ang mainit na bato ay umaakyat, lumalamig, at bumababa sa mabagal na convection. Ito ang nagtutulak sa tectonic plates na gumalaw!

statements.text: Tectonic plates float on the hot, soft part of the mantle beneath them!
statements.tl: Ang mga tectonic plate ay lumulutang sa mainit at malambot na bahagi ng manto sa ilalim nila!

statements.text: Deep inside Earth, hot rock in the mantle loops up and down in a motion called convection — and that pushes the tectonic plates!
statements.tl: Sa loob ng Daigdig, ang mainit na bato sa manto ay umiikot pataas at pababa sa galaw na tinatawag na convection — at iyan ang nagtutulak sa mga plaka!

statements.text: A mantle convection cell has three parts in a loop: hot rock rises (upwelling), moves sideways at the top, then cooler rock sinks (downwelling). This loop repeats over and over!
statements.tl: Ang convection cell sa mantle ay may tatlong bahagi: umaakyat ang mainit na bato (upwelling), gumagalaw nang patagilid sa itaas, pagkatapos lumulubog ang mas malamig na bato (downwelling). Paulit-ulit ang loop na ito!

statements.text: Mantle convection is like a lava lamp! Heat from the core warms the rock, making it rise, cool at the top, and sink back down in a big loop.
statements.tl: Ang mantle convection ay parang lava lamp! Init mula sa core ang nagpapainit sa bato, kaya umaakyat ito, lumalamig sa itaas, at bumababa muli.

statements.text:
Why does part of the mantle rise?

When heated, rock expands and becomes lighter (lower density), so it floats up! Cooler, denser rock sinks — and this starts convection.
statements.tl:
Bakit umaakyat ang ilang bahagi ng mantle?

Kapag pinainit, lumalawak ang bato at nagiging mas magaan (lower density), kaya lumulutang ito! Ang mas malamig at siksik na bato ay lumulubog — dito nagsisimula ang convection.

statements.text:
What heats the mantle?

Two things! (1) Leftover heat from when Earth first formed, and (2) heat from radioactive decay of atoms deep inside our planet.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nagpapainit sa mantle?

Dalawa! (1) Natitirang init mula noong nabuo ang Earth, at (2) init mula sa radioactive decay ng mga atom sa loob ng Earth.

statements.text: Mantle convection works like a heat elevator! It carries heat from deep inside up to the surface, where it escapes. Over millions of years, Earth's interior slowly cools down.
statements.tl: Ang mantle convection ay parang heat elevator! Dadalhin nito ang init mula sa malalim papunta sa ibabaw, kung saan ito lalabas. Sa loob ng milyong-milyong taon, dahan-dahang lumalamig ang loob ng Earth.

statements.text: Mantle convection won't stop! As long as the bottom of the mantle (near the core) stays hotter than the top (near the crust), the rock keeps cycling. It only stops when Earth fully cools — millions of years away!
statements.tl: Hindi titigil ang mantle convection! Hangga't mas mainit ang ilalim ng mantle (malapit sa core) kaysa sa itaas (malapit sa crust), patuloy ang pag-ikot ng bato. Titigil lang ito kapag ganap nang lumamig ang Earth — milyong-milyong taon pa!

statements.text:
How do we know the mantle moves?

Rising rock from convection carries deep mantle pieces up through volcanoes! Scientists collect these real rocks from far below to study.
statements.tl:
Paano natin alam na gumagalaw ang mantle?

Ang umaakyat na bato mula sa convection ay nagdadala ng mga piraso ng mantle pataas sa mga bulkan para pag-aralan ng mga siyentista!

statements.text: The mantle's heat is like an engine! It drives Earth's surface activity, including earthquakes, volcanoes, and the building of mountains.
statements.tl: Ang init ng mantle ay parang makina! Pinapatakbo nito ang aktibidad sa ibabaw ng Earth, tulad ng lindol, bulkan, at pagbuo ng bundok.

statements.text:
What happens when one tectonic plate slides under another?

Deep ocean trenches form below, and volcanoes form above!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag ang isang plate ay sumusubsob sa ilalim ng isa pa?

Nabubuo ang malalim na ocean trench sa ilalim, at mga bulkan sa ibabaw!

statements.text:
What happens as the plate sinks at the Philippine Trench?

It produces earthquakes! These are the earthquakes that PHIVOLCS carefully monitors.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari habang lumulubog ang plato sa Philippine Trench?

Nagkakaroon ng mga lindol! Ito ang mga lindol na binabantayan ng PHIVOLCS.

statements.text: Along the Ring of Fire, one tectonic plate sinks under another in subduction, melting rock into magma to feed volcanoes!
statements.tl: Sa Ring of Fire, isang tectonic plate ang lumulubog sa ilalim ng isa pa sa subduction, natutunaw ang bato sa magma para sa bulkan!

statements.text:
How does subduction create volcanoes?

When a plate sinks beneath another, water from it helps melt mantle rock into magma that rises up and builds volcanoes on the surface!
statements.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng bulkan ang subduction?

Kapag lumubog ang isang plaka sa ilalim ng iba, ang tubig mula rito ay tumutulong tumunaw ng bato sa mantle at bumuo ng magmang umaakyat para gumawa ng mga bulkan!

statements.text: When one plate sinks beneath another, water from it helps melt mantle rock and form new magma that can feed a volcano!
statements.tl: Kapag ang isang plaka ay lumulubog sa ilalim ng iba, ang tubig mula rito ay tumutulong tunawin ang bato sa mantle at bumuo ng bagong magma!

statements.text:
How do volcanoes get their magma?

When a plate sinks, rock deep underground melts into magma that feeds the volcanoes above!
statements.tl:
Paano nakakakuha ng magma ang mga bulkan?

Kapag lumulubog ang isang plaka, natutunaw ang bato sa ilalim ng lupa at nagiging magma na nagpapakain sa mga bulkan!

statements.text: The Philippines has many volcanoes like Mayon and Taal! Water released by a sinking plate helps mantle rock melt into magma that can erupt.
statements.tl: Maraming bulkan sa Pilipinas tulad ng Mayon at Taal! Ang tubig na inilalabas ng lumulubog na plate ay tumutulong sa pagkatunaw ng bato sa mantle para maging magma na maaaring pumutok.

statements.text:
How is the trench connected to our volcanoes?

As a plate sinks into Earth's hot interior, water it releases helps mantle rock melt into magma! This magma rises up to build volcanoes nearby.
statements.tl:
Paano konektado ang trench sa mga bulkan natin?

Habang lumulubog ang plate sa mainit na loob ng Earth, tumutulong ang tubig na inilalabas nito na tunawin ang bato sa mantle para maging magma! Umaakyat ito para bumuo ng mga bulkan sa malapit.

statements.text:
Why do the Philippine islands curve like a smile on the map?

They sit above a curved boundary where one plate dives under another. This curved row of volcanic islands is called an island arc!
statements.tl:
Bakit nakabaluktot ang mga isla ng Pilipinas sa mapa?

Nabuo sila sa itaas ng kurbadong hangganan kung saan sumusuot ang isang plaka sa ilalim ng isa. Ang ganitong hilera ng bulkanikong isla ay tinatawag na island arc!

statements.text: When denser oceanic crust meets continental crust, it can sink because it's denser. Water released from the sinking plate helps mantle rock melt into magma that rises to form volcanoes!
statements.tl: Kapag ang mas siksik na oceanic crust ay nakasalubong ng continental crust, maaari itong lumubog dahil mas siksik ito. Tumutulong ang tubig na inilalabas ng lumulubog na plate na tunawin ang bato sa mantle para maging magmang bumubuo ng bulkan!

statements.text:
How does the angle of a diving plate change where volcanoes pop up?

The angle at which a plate subducts affects the volcanic arc's position! A steeper subduction angle places the volcanic arc closer to the trench, shifting where volcanoes appear in the Philippine subduction system!
statements.tl:
Paano nababago ng anggulo ng pagsalubong ng plato ang paglitaw ng mga bulkan?

Ang anggulo ng pagsasalid ng plato ay nakakaapekto sa posisyon ng volcanic arc! Ang mas matarik na subduction angle naglalagay ng volcanic arc mas malapit sa trench, nagpapabago ng posisyon ng mga bulkan sa Pilipinas!

statements.text:
Why do Philippine island arc volcanoes form at a specific distance from the subduction trench?

At about 100 km deep, the sinking plate releases water that helps the mantle above it melt into magma! The distance between the trench and volcanic arc is called the 'arc-trench gap'.
statements.tl:
Bakit nabubuo ang mga bulkan ng Philippine island arc sa tiyak na distansya mula sa subduction trench?

Sa lalim na mga 100 km, naglalabas ng tubig ang lumulubog na plate na tumutulong sa pagtunaw ng mantle sa ibabaw nito bilang magma! Ang distansya ng trench at volcanic arc ay tinatawag na 'arc-trench gap'.

statements.text: Oceanic crust is generally thinner and denser than continental crust. Density compares mass in the same volume; it does not mean a whole oceanic plate must weigh more than a whole continental plate. At many convergent boundaries, dense oceanic lithosphere sinks beneath another plate in subduction.
statements.tl: Karaniwang mas manipis at mas dense ang oceanic crust kaysa continental crust. Inihahambing ng density ang mass sa parehong volume; hindi nito ibig sabihing laging mas mabigat ang buong oceanic plate kaysa buong continental plate. Sa maraming convergent boundary, lumulubog ang dense na oceanic lithosphere sa ilalim ng ibang plate sa subduction.

statements.text:
How is a giant underwater ridge called an accretionary wedge formed?

As an oceanic plate sinks, it scrapes off soft sediments! These pile up against the plate above, building the wedge.
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang isang malaking underwater ridge na tinatawag na accretionary wedge?

Habang lumulubog ang oceanic plate, kinakayod nito ang malalambot na sediments! Naiipon ang mga ito sa harap ng plate sa itaas, bumubuo ng wedge.

statements.text:
How do sinking tectonic plates cause earthquakes on land?

The sinking plate drags the top plate down, bending it like a spring! When it snaps back, it releases earthquakes.
statements.tl:
Paano nagdudulot ng lindol sa lupa ang paglubog ng mga tectonic plates?

Hinihila ng lumulubog na plate pababa ang plate sa itaas, binabaluktot ito na parang spring! Kapag bumalik ito sa dating hugis, naglalabas ito ng mga lindol.

statements.text:
Ever wonder how a back-arc basin forms?

Behind the volcanic arc, the sinking plate stretches the plate above apart. It cracks, making the sea floor sink to form a back-arc basin!
statements.tl:
Naisip mo ba kung paano nabubuo ang back-arc basin?

Sa likod ng volcanic arc, iniunat ng lumulubog na plate ang plate sa itaas. Mabitak ito, kaya lumulubog ang sea floor para bumuo ng back-arc basin!

statements.text: The subducting plate squeezes the plate above! Over millions of years, this compresses the crust, making it fold and thicken into huge mountain ranges.
statements.tl: Pinipiga ng subducting plate ang plate sa itaas! Sa loob ng milyon-milyong taon, kumakapal at tumutupi ang crust para maging mga bundok.

statements.text:
Why doesn't the trench just fill up with mud and sand?

The plate keeps sinking! Even if sediment falls in, it stays deep because the ground is always moving down.
statements.tl:
Bakit hindi napupuno ng putik at buhangin ang trench?

Patuloy kasing lumulubog ang plate! Kaya kahit may pumapasok na sediment, nananatili itong malalim dahil laging gumagalaw pababa ang lupa.

statements.text: When two plates push together, Earth's crust crumples and rises up — forming giant mountains like the Himalayas!
statements.tl: Kapag nagtutulakan ang dalawang plaka, nalulukot at tumataas ang crust — na bumubuo ng matataas na bundok tulad ng Himalayas!

statements.text: The Himalayas formed from two continents colliding! The Andes formed from an ocean plate sinking under a continent, so they grow differently.
statements.tl: Ang Himalayas ay nagmula sa pagbangga ng dalawang kontinente! Ang Andes naman ay galing sa paglubog ng ocean plate, kaya magkaiba sila.

statements.text: The Rocky Mountains in North America formed starting 75 million years ago when tectonic plates collided and pushed up the land.
statements.tl: Ang Rocky Mountains sa North America ay nagsimulang mabuo 75 million years na ang nakalipas nang magbanggaan ang mga tectonic plate at naitulak pataas ang lupa.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 10Pb80v8BbgFnZCIDMDfQtXCNqWaYMFrp), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Mountain ranges form at continental-continental convergent boundaries when two continents collide and their edges crumple, fold, and push upward over millions of years.
statements.tl: Ang mga bulubundukin ay nabubuo sa continental-continental convergent boundaries kapag nagbanggaan ang dalawang kontinente at ang kanilang mga gilid ay nagkukulubot, tumitiklop, at nagtutulakan paitaas sa loob ng milyun-milyong taon.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 121-uDtX-5IqzkiXeWEKqkzlKaCideMpg), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How did the tallest mountains on Earth form?

The Himalayas formed when India and Eurasia, two large landmasses, collided about 40 to 50 million years ago and their crust crumpled upward.
statements.tl:
Paano nabuo ang pinakamatataas na bundok sa mundo?

Nabuo ang Himalayas nang magbanggaan ang India at Eurasia, dalawang malalaking landmass, mga 40 hanggang 50 milyong taon na ang nakalipas at tumupi paitaas ang kanilang crust.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 130utqrpVVXt9JXlDvfrBcmBrGhxVmIts), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When two giant pieces of Earth's crust called tectonic plates collide, the land gets pushed up to form mountains!
statements.tl: Kapag nagbanggaan ang dalawang malalaking tipak ng balat ng Lupa na tinatawag na tectonic plates, natutulak ang lupa pataas para mabuo ang mga bundok!

statements.text:
How did the world's tallest mountains form?

The tallest peaks, like Mount Everest, were created when two giant continents crashed into each other!
statements.tl:
Paano nabuo ang pinakamatataas na bundok sa mundo?

Ang mga pinakamataas na tugatog, gaya ng Mount Everest, ay nabuo nang magbanggaan ang dalawang kontinente!

statements.text: When two tectonic plates crash into each other, they push the ground up to build huge mountains!
statements.tl: Kapag nagbanggaan ang dalawang plates, itutulak nila pataas ang lupa para gumawa ng mga bundok!

statements.text:
How does convection help build mountains?

Mantle convection pushes the plates! Some plates collide and crumple the crust upward — that's how great mountain ranges like the Himalayas form.
statements.tl:
Paano nakakabuo ng bundok ang convection?

Itinutulak ng mantle convection ang mga plate! May mga plate na nagbabanggaan at nagdudulot ng pagkukulubot at pagtaas ng crust — ganito nabuo ang malalaking bulubundukin tulad ng Himalayas.

statements.text: Mountain ranges form when tectonic plates slowly push together! Over a long time, land folds upward. It is very slow, just like your fingernails grow!
statements.tl: Nabubuo ang mountain range kapag dahan-dahang nagtutulakan ang tectonic plates! Sa mahabang panahon, nakukulubot pataas ang lupa. Napakabagal, parang pagtubo ng kuko mo!

statements.text: The Himalayas in Asia have the world's tallest peaks, including Mount Everest! They formed when India's plate crashed into Asia's plate — and they're still slowly rising today!
statements.tl: Ang Himalayas sa Asya ang may pinakamataas na tuktok sa mundo, kasama ang Mount Everest! Nabuo ito nang magbangga ang plato ng India sa plato ng Asya — at dahan-dahan pa ring tumataas!

statements.text: Mountains form when huge pieces of the Earth's crust slowly push against each other over millions of years, pushing the ground up. Some also come from volcanoes!
statements.tl: Nabubuo ang mga bundok kapag dahan-dahang nagtutulakan ang malalaking piraso ng balat ng Daigdig sa loob ng milyong taon, kaya tumataas ang lupa. May iba ring galing sa mga bulkan!

statements.text: Many mountains form when huge pieces of Earth's crust slowly push against each other, lifting the land upward!
statements.tl: Maraming bundok ang nabubuo kapag dahan-dahang nagtutulak ang malalaking piraso ng balat ng Mundo, nag-aangat ng lupa pataas!

statements.text: Most Philippine mountain ranges, like Sierra Madre and Cordillera, formed by tectonic uplift: when plates converge, land is pushed upward. These mountains still rise a few millimetres each year as plates collide!
statements.tl: Karamihan ng kabundukan ng Pilipinas, tulad ng Sierra Madre at Cordillera, ay nabuo ng tectonic uplift: kapag nagtatagpo ang mga plato, itinataas ang lupa. Patuloy pa ring tumatangkad ng ilang millimeter bawat taon ang mga bundok habang nagbabanggaan ang mga plato!

statements.text: When two continental plates crash together, neither sinks! Both are too light, so the crust crumples upward — building giant mountains like the Himalayas!
statements.tl: Kapag nagbanggaan ang dalawang continental plate, walang lumulubog! Pareho silang magaan, kaya ang crust ay natitiklop pataas — bumubuo ng matataas na bundok tulad ng Himalayas!

statements.text: Mount Everest grows about four millimeters taller every year because tectonic plates are still pushing it upward!
statements.tl: Tumataas ang Bundok Everest ng halos apat na milimetro kada taon dahil patuloy na nagtutulak ang mga tectonic plate pataas!

statements.text: The Appalachians are an old, eroded mountain range. The Himalayas are young and still sharp, showing how mountains change over time!
statements.tl: Ang Appalachians ay isang luma at eroded na bulubundukin. Ang Himalayas ay bata pa at matutulis, na nagpapakita kung paano nagbabago ang bundok!

statements.text:
Are large mountain ranges like the Himalayas built by volcanic eruptions?

Nope! They are folded and faulted from squeezing! Huge forces push the rocks together to build these giant mountains.
statements.tl:
Ang mga malalaking bulubundukin tulad ng Himalayas ba ay gawa ng pagsabog ng bulkan?

Hindi! Nakatiklop at nagkalamat sila dahil sa pagpisil! Malakas na pwersa ang nagtutulak sa mga bato para buuin ang mga bundok.

statements.text: As a projectile flies, gravity pulls it down! This makes its vertical motion slow down while rising, and speed up while falling.
statements.tl: Habang lumilipad ang projectile, hinihila ito pababa ng gravity! Kaya ang patayong galaw ay bumabagal kapag pataas, at bumibilis kapag pababa.
statements.source: AAAS 4F/H1; NRC PS2.A; DepEd G9 Q4

statements.text: With no air resistance and level ground, a thrown object travels the farthest (greatest range) when launched at an angle of 45 degrees!
statements.tl: Kung walang resistensya ng hangin at pantay ang lupa, pinakamalayo ang abot (range) ng isang itinapong bagay kapag inihagis sa anggulong 45 degrees!
statements.source: AAAS 4F/H1; consensus physics; DepEd G10 Q4

statements.text: In real life, air resistance pushes back on a projectile! This makes its range shorter and its path not a perfect parabola.
statements.tl: Sa totoong buhay, ang resistensya ng hangin ay tumutulak pabalik sa projectile! Kaya mas maikli ang range nito at hindi perpektong parabola ang landas.
statements.source: AAAS 4F/H7; consensus physics; DepEd G10 Q4

statements.text: Projectile motion happens when an object is thrown with an initial velocity at an angle of launch, and air resistance is ignored for simple calculations.
statements.tl: Nangyayari ang projectile motion kapag ang isang bagay ay inihagis na may initial velocity sa isang anggulo, at hindi pinapansin ang air resistance para sa simpleng pagkalkula.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GFVhCpjqjbKxoxs3HTizYAYgJLZJzXOm), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What happens to a projectile's height before and after its peak?

Before the maximum height, the object is ascending and its height increases; after the peak, it is descending and its height decreases.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa taas ng projectile bago at pagkatapos ng tuktok?

Bago ang maximum height, umaakyat ang bagay at tumataas ang height nito; pagkatapos ng tuktok, bumababa ito at bumababa ang height.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GFVhCpjqjbKxoxs3HTizYAYgJLZJzXOm), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The sideways part of the launch velocity is vx = v0 cos θ, and the upward part is vy = v0 sin θ, where θ is the launch angle.
statements.tl: Ang pahalang na bahagi ng launch velocity ay vx = v0 cos θ, at ang paitaas na bahagi ay vy = v0 sin θ, kung saan ang θ ay ang anggulo ng paghagis.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GFVhCpjqjbKxoxs3HTizYAYgJLZJzXOm), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A monkey jumping from a branch at 38° with an initial velocity of 10 m/s follows the same projectile rules as any thrown object.
statements.tl: Ang unggoy na tumatalon mula sa sanga sa 38° na may initial velocity na 10 m/s ay sumusunod sa parehong projectile rules tulad ng anumang inihagis na bagay.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GFVhCpjqjbKxoxs3HTizYAYgJLZJzXOm), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A soccer ball kicked at 35 m/s at a 20° angle is a projectile, and its height and range can be calculated with the same formulas.
statements.tl: Ang soccer ball na sinipa sa 35 m/s sa 20° na anggulo ay isang projectile, at ang taas at layo nito ay maaaring kalkulahin gamit ang parehong mga formula.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GFVhCpjqjbKxoxs3HTizYAYgJLZJzXOm), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The initial velocity of a projectile can be split into a horizontal component and a vertical component, which are analyzed separately.
statements.tl: Ang initial velocity ng isang projectile ay maaaring hatiin sa horizontal component at vertical component, na sinusuri nang magkahiwalay.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1HvuEsjJFyqwRvV5MLqPbtducCzJSJYzC), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The horizontal range of a projectile is calculated by multiplying its horizontal velocity component by the total time of flight.
statements.tl: Ang horizontal range ng projectile ay kinakalkula sa pamamagitan ng pag-multiply ng horizontal velocity component nito sa kabuuang time of flight.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1HvuEsjJFyqwRvV5MLqPbtducCzJSJYzC), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: At the same launch speed and angle, launching a projectile from a higher place, like a table, gives it more time to fall, so it travels a longer range before landing.
statements.tl: Sa parehong bilis at anggulo ng paglunsad, kapag inilunsad ang projectile mula sa mas mataas na lugar, tulad ng mesa, mas mahaba ang oras nito para bumagsak, kaya mas malayo ang mararating nito bago lumapag.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1rZr0CDC-by1ZJquFa-8MxEAURYL3U2T-), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Using a computer simulation, you can change the launch speed, height, and air resistance of a cannonball to see how each one changes its curved path.
statements.tl: Gamit ang computer simulation, maaari mong baguhin ang launch speed, height, at air resistance ng isang cannonball para makita kung paano binabago ng bawat isa ang kanyang kurbadong path.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1rZr0CDC-by1ZJquFa-8MxEAURYL3U2T-), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A simple catapult made of popsicle sticks and a bottle cap can launch clay balls, letting you measure how launch height changes the ball's range and flight time.
statements.tl: Ang simpleng catapult na gawa sa popsicle sticks at bottle cap ay kayang maglunsad ng clay balls, para masukat mo kung paano binabago ng launch height ang range at flight time ng bola.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1rZr0CDC-by1ZJquFa-8MxEAURYL3U2T-), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: As the launch angle increases from 20 degrees toward 45 degrees, the range of the projectile increases because the object stays in the air longer while still moving forward.
statements.tl: Habang tumataas ang launch angle mula 20 degrees papuntang 45 degrees, tumataas din ang range ng projectile dahil mas matagal itong nananatili sa ere habang umaabante pa rin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1xiWp7F_4G1RkCD0lxBmKieW8x_-gruAk), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A ball thrown upward at 29.4 m/s reaches a maximum height of 44.1 meters before it starts falling back down.
statements.tl: Ang bolang inihagis pataas sa 29.4 m/s ay umaabot sa maximum height na 44.1 metro bago ito magsimulang bumagsak pabalik.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-17949), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What happens if you launch a projectile at two different angles that add up to 90 degrees, like 30 and 60?

At the same launch speed and launch/landing height, with no air resistance, they give the same range! But the steeper angle makes it go higher and stay in the air longer.
statements.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kung ihahagis mo ang projectile sa dalawang anggulo na nagsusuma ng 90 degrees, gaya ng 30 at 60?

Sa parehong bilis ng hagis at taas ng pag-alis at paglapag, na walang air resistance, magbibigay ito ng parehong range! Pero ang mas matarik na anggulo ay magpapataas at magpapalipad ng mas matagal sa hangin.

statements.text:
What determines how long a projectile stays in the air?

It depends only on its vertical motion (how high it goes up), not on how fast it moves forward!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nagtutukoy kung gaano katagal ang isang projectile sa hangin?

Nakadepende lamang ito sa patayong galaw (gaano ito kataas umakyat), hindi sa kung gaano kabilis ito pasulong!
statements.source: consensus physics; AAAS 4F/H1; DepEd G10 Q4

statements.text: A projectile reaches its highest point when its vertical speed becomes zero—its vertical motion pauses for an instant before falling back down!
statements.tl: Naaabot ng projectile ang pinakamataas na punto kapag naging sero na ang vertical speed nito—sandaling humihinto ang patayong galaw nito bago bumagsak pababa!

statements.text: A car crashing into a wall is an inelastic collision because the car deforms and much kinetic energy becomes sound and heat.
statements.tl: Ang pagbangga ng kotse sa pader ay inelastic collision dahil ang kotse ay nade-deform at maraming kinetic energy ang nagiging tunog at init.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 10dyzdKM8PCmTOSpNjf5tRLD-Co8l9Ey8), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: In an elastic collision, objects bounce apart without losing motion energy, so the total kinetic energy stays exactly the same before and after!
statements.tl: Sa elastic collision, tumataltag ang mga bagay nang hindi nawawalan ng motion energy, kaya ang kabuuang kinetic energy ay nananatiling pareho bago at pagkatapos!
statements.source: NRC PS2.A, PS3.A; DepEd G9-10 collisions; encyclopedia-stable consensus

statements.text: In an inelastic collision, total kinetic energy is not conserved: some becomes deformation, thermal energy or sound. The objects may rebound; sticking together is the special case called perfectly inelastic. Total momentum is conserved if the system has negligible net external impulse. Energy does not disappear.
statements.tl: Sa inelastic collision, hindi nananatili ang kabuuang kinetic energy: ang ilan ay napupunta sa deformation, thermal energy o tunog. Maaaring tumalbog ang mga bagay; espesyal na kasong perfectly inelastic ang pagdikit nila. Nananatili ang kabuuang momentum kung napakaliit ng net external impulse sa system. Hindi nawawala ang energy.
statements.source: NRC PS2.A, PS3.A; DepEd G9-10 collisions; encyclopedia-stable consensus

statements.text: A dart sticking into a dartboard is an inelastic collision because the dart and board stay together after impact.
statements.tl: Ang dart na bumabaon sa dartboard ay inelastic collision dahil ang dart at board ay nananatiling magkasama pagkatapos ng impact.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 10dyzdKM8PCmTOSpNjf5tRLD-Co8l9Ey8), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Two soccer players colliding on the field is an inelastic collision because their bodies deform slightly and they may fall together.
statements.tl: Ang banggaan ng dalawang soccer player sa field ay inelastic collision dahil bahagyang nade-deform ang kanilang katawan at maaari silang sabay na matumba.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 10dyzdKM8PCmTOSpNjf5tRLD-Co8l9Ey8), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When a rubber ball hits the floor, it squishes and stores energy. It quickly springs back to shape, giving that energy back as an upward bounce! That is why rubber bounces, but clay does not.
statements.tl: Kapag tumama sa sahig ang gomang bola, namumukol ito at nag-iipon ng enerhiya. Mabilis itong bumabalik sa hugis, ibinabalik ang enerhiya bilang paglundag! Kaya tumatalbog ang goma, pero hindi ang luwad.

statements.text: In a Newton's cradle, releasing one steel ball at the end makes just one ball fly out the far end because momentum and motion energy pass through elastic collisions!
statements.tl: Sa Newton's cradle, kapag binitawan mo ang isang bolang bakal sa dulo, isang bola lang sa kabilang dulo ang lumilipad dahil naipapasa ang momentum at enerhiya ng galaw sa elastikong banggaan!
statements.source: NRC PS2.A; encyclopedia-stable consensus; DepEd G9-10 momentum

statements.text:
What happens when objects crash into each other?

In some crashes, objects bounce apart! In others, they stick together and move as one big lump!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagbanggaan ang mga bagay?

Sa ilang banggaan, ang mga bagay ay tumatalbog palayo! Sa iba, nagkakadikit sila at magkasamang gumagalaw bilang isa!

statements.text: Throw two clay lumps together, and they stick into one big lump! Moving together like this makes a perfectly inelastic collision.
statements.tl: Pag ibinato mo ang dalawang clay, didikit sila sa isang piraso! Sabay silang gagalaw, na gumagawa ng perfectly inelastic collision.

statements.text: Most everyday collisions are somewhere in between! They aren't perfectly elastic or inelastic; some kinetic energy is converted to other forms, but the objects still separate.
statements.tl: Karamihan sa pang-araw-araw na collision ay nasa pagitan! Hindi sila perfectly elastic o inelastic; may kinetic energy na nagiging ibang anyo ng energy, pero naghihiwalay pa rin ang mga bagay.

statements.text: When a car crumples in a crash, its motion energy folds the metal! The car slows down as the metal bends and crumples.
statements.tl: Pag nayupi ang kotse sa banggaan, ang energy mula sa paggalaw niya ang nagtitiklop sa metal! Bumabagal ang kotse habang nababaluktot ito.

statements.text:
What materials make elastic collisions happen?

Hard, springy materials like steel or glass! They bounce right back to their original shape immediately after the hit.
statements.tl:
Anong mga materyales ang gumagawa ng elastic collisions?

Matitigas at springy na materyales tulad ng steel o glass! Bumabalik sila agad sa orihinal na hugis pagkatapos ng tama.

statements.text:
What happens in inelastic collisions?

Soft or sticky materials stay deformed after the hit! Think of a crumpled soda can that doesn't bounce back.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa inelastic collisions?

Malalambot o madidikit na materyales ang nananatiling deformed pagkatapos ng tama! Isipin mo ang napiis na lata ng soda.

statements.text: Scientists measure collision elasticity with a number from zero to one! One means perfectly elastic, and zero means perfectly inelastic.
statements.tl: Sinusukat ng mga scientist ang elasticity gamit ang numero mula sero hanggang isa! Ang isa ay perfectly elastic, at ang sero ay perfectly inelastic.

statements.text: When two identical billiard balls meet head-on in an elastic collision, they simply swap their speeds and directions like magic!
statements.tl: Kapag nagtagpong harapan ang dalawang magkaparehong billiard balls sa elastic collision, pinagpapalit lang nila ang kanilang bilis at direksyon!

statements.text: A superball is made of rubber that stores energy when squashed! It returns almost all of it, bouncing very high in a nearly elastic collision.
statements.tl: Ang superball ay gawa sa goma na nag-iimbak ng energy kapag napipisil! Ibinabalik niya ang halos lahat nito, kaya tumatalbog ito nang napakataas!

statements.text:
Why do cars have crumple zones?

They are designed to be inelastic on purpose! They crush slowly to absorb crash energy and protect the people inside.
statements.tl:
Bakit may crumple zones ang kotse?

Sadyang ginawa silang inelastic! Dahan-dahang nadudurog para sumipsip ng crash energy at protektahan ang mga tao sa loob.

statements.text: Two repelling magnets can have an elastic collision without even touching! Their magnetic field simply pushes them apart.
statements.tl: Ang dalawang nagtutulakang magnet ay pwedeng magkaroon ng elastic collision nang hindi nagkakadikit! Tinutulak lang sila palayo ng magnetic field.

statements.text: When rain hits a gabi leaf, it forms tiny round beads of water that roll right off instead of soaking in.
statements.tl: Kapag tumama ang tubig-ulan sa dahon ng gabi, nagiging maliliit na bilog na patak ito na gumugulong palabas sa halip na bumasa sa dahon.

statements.text: Tinapa is fish cooked and dried over a smoky fire! The smoke gives it a special flavor and helps it last longer.
statements.tl: Ang tinapa ay isdang niluto at pinatuyo sa ibabaw ng mausok na apoy! Nagbibigay ito ng natatanging lasa at tumutulong na tumagal.

statements.text:
How does salt appear faster in salt beds?

The sun's heat and blowing wind help dry the water in salt beds faster!
statements.tl:
Paano mas mabilis lumitaw ang asin sa mga asinan?

Ang init ng araw at ihip ng hangin ang tumutulong patuyuin ang tubig sa asinan!
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable; solar evaporation needs sun and wind

statements.text: Science helps explain how the natural world works, from why rain falls to why day changes into night.
statements.tl: Tinutulungan tayo ng science na maipaliwanag kung paano gumagana ang kalikasan, mula sa kung bakit umuulan hanggang sa kung bakit nagiging gabi ang araw.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1OSLTjgRBCTcb_rZKcadCvGpM1uW7lrsz), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Carbon sequestration is the process of capturing and storing carbon dioxide from the air, and forests and oceans do this naturally.
statements.tl: Ang carbon sequestration ay ang proseso ng pagkuha at pag-imbak ng carbon dioxide mula sa hangin, at natural itong ginagawa ng mga kagubatan at karagatan.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-23845), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Aphids are tiny insects that suck plant sap — they multiply fast and can badly damage crops and garden plants.
statements.tl: Ang mga aphid ay maliliit na insektong sumisipsip ng katas ng halaman — mabilis silang dumarami at nakakasira ng pananim at halaman sa hardin.

statements.text:
Does cooking remove pufferfish poison?

No! Cooking or heating a pufferfish does not remove its poison at all.
statements.tl:
Nawawala ba sa pagluluto ang lason ng butete?

Hindi! Kahit lutuin o painitin ang butete, hindi mawawala ang lason nito.

statements.text: Laing is made from dried taro leaves, which have calcium-oxalate crystals that itch the throat, so the leaves must be fully cooked in coconut milk before eating.
statements.tl: Ang laing ay gawa sa tuyong dahon ng gabi na may crystal ng calcium oxalate na nakakangati, kaya kailangan itong lutuing mabuti sa gata bago kainin.

statements.text: Pateros in Metro Manila is famous nationwide as the center for raising ducks and making balut!
statements.tl: Bantog sa buong bansa ang Pateros sa Metro Manila bilang sentro ng pag-aalaga ng itik at paggawa ng balut!

statements.text: A chili plant can produce peppers many times over several months — you don't need to replant right away because it just keeps giving chilies.
statements.tl: Ang halaman ng siling haba ay nagbubunga nang maraming beses sa loob ng ilang buwan — hindi mo kailangang magtanim ulit agad dahil patuloy itong nagbibigay ng sili.

statements.text: Some termites build tall mounds of hardened mud and saliva with complex tunnels inside that move air around — keeping it cool and fresh like natural air-conditioning!
statements.tl: Ang ilang anay ay nagtatayo ng matataas na punso na yari sa tumigas na putik at laway, may masalimuot na lagusan sa loob na nagpapadaloy ng hangin — kaya nananatiling sariwa at banayad ang temperatura, parang likas na air-conditioning!

statements.text:
Why is ube purple?

Thanks to anthocyanins! These plant pigments dissolve in water and also act as antioxidants.
statements.tl:
Bakit purple ang ube?

Dahil sa anthocyanins! Mga pigment na natutunaw sa tubig ng halaman na gumaganap din bilang antioxidants.

statements.text:
Are ube and purple sweet potato the same?

Nope! Ube and purple sweet potato are actually different plants, even though both are purple.
statements.tl:
Magkapareho ba ang ube at kamote?

Hindi pala! Magkaiba ang ube at ang purple na kamote bilang halaman, kahit pareho silang kulay-lila.
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable; Dioscorea alata vs Ipomoea batatas

statements.text: The tabon bird has loud calls that people often hear at night or early in the morning.
statements.tl: Ang tabon ay may malakas na huni na madalas marinig sa gabi o madaling-araw.

statements.text: In the Philippines, mosquito pupae live in stagnant water — like old tires, cans, flower pots, and puddled rainwater — that's why we cover these up.
statements.tl: Sa Pilipinas, makikita ang mga pupa ng lamok sa nakatigil na tubig — gaya ng lumang gulong, lata, paso, at naipong tubig-ulan — kaya tinatakpan natin ang mga ito.

statements.text:
Why do raw taro leaves itch your mouth?

The leaves and stems of the taro plant have tiny calcium oxalate crystals that badly irritate your mouth if you eat them raw.
statements.tl:
Bakit nangangati ang hilaw na gabi?

May maliliit na calcium oxalate crystals ang dahon at tangkay ng gabi na nagdudulot ng matinding pangangati sa bibig kapag kinain nang hilaw.

statements.text: Frost is a thin layer of ice on grass and objects on very cold nights, formed when water vapor turns directly into tiny ice crystals.
statements.tl: Ang frost ay manipis na yelo sa damo at mga bagay sa napakalamig na gabi, nabubuo kapag ang singaw ng tubig ay direktang nagiging maliliit na crystal ng yelo.
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable consensus; NRC PS1.A (changes of state)

statements.text: Leche flan is cooked with gentle steam, not a hard boil! Too much heat makes bubbles and holes, turning the smooth custard grainy instead.
statements.tl: Ang leche flan ay niluluto sa mahinang steam, hindi sa malakas na kumukulong tubig! Sobrang init ay gumagawa ng bula at butas, kaya magaspang ang custard imbes na makinis.

statements.text: Measuring is a science process skill that uses units like millimeters, centimeters, and meters to describe the size of objects.
statements.tl: Ang measuring ay isang science process skill na gumagamit ng mga unit tulad ng millimeters, centimeters, at meters para ilarawan ang sukat ng mga bagay.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17L1W4QsuxQmlAkIVoiYHyG5fKX7HpIqY), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Predicting is a science process skill where you use careful observations and patterns to make a smart guess about what will happen next.
statements.tl: Ang predicting ay isang science process skill kung saan ginagamit mo ang maingat na pag-oobserve at mga pattern para makagawa ng matalinong hula sa susunod na mangyayari.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1I-0H1t3GyEVh8CJwTK4mXAYaMtx_MTvz), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Observing is a science process skill that uses your senses to describe things around you.
statements.tl: Ang observing ay isang science process skill na ginagamitan ng iyong senses upang ilarawan ang mga bagay sa paligid mo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1RXQj0EGi5rGj4BqLyzJRJ3Gv2U9hySIz), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Observing is the most basic science process skill, and it means using your five senses to gather information from the world around you.
statements.tl: Ang observing ang pinaka-basic na science process skill, at ibig sabihin nito ay ginagamit mo ang iyong limang pandama para mangalap ng impormasyon mula sa iyong paligid.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17L1W4QsuxQmlAkIVoiYHyG5fKX7HpIqY), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: You can observe and record living things in a nearby environment by writing or drawing what you see in front, behind, and beside you.
statements.tl: Maaari mong obserbahan at itala ang mga living things sa malapit na kapaligiran sa pamamagitan ng pagsusulat o pagguhit ng nakikita mo sa harap, likod, at tabi mo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1HW6wsHIoEYSZKSfUf_V7flxDswWTWDHM), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Observing is the most basic science process skill, where you use your senses to gather information about objects and events around you.
statements.tl: Ang observing ang pinaka-basic na science process skill, kung saan ginagamit mo ang iyong senses para mangalap ng impormasyon tungkol sa mga bagay at pangyayari sa paligid mo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1I-0H1t3GyEVh8CJwTK4mXAYaMtx_MTvz), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Observing means using your senses to identify and describe the properties of objects and events, and it is the most basic science process skill.
statements.tl: Ang observing ay ang paggamit ng iyong mga pandama upang matukoy at mailarawan ang mga katangian ng mga bagay at pangyayari, at ito ang pinaka-basic na science process skill.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1OSgczAaDPaJCjr64sbnEKss8H38P7Yjw), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why is experimenting at the top of the science skills pyramid?

Conducting a meaningful experiment combines all the basic process skills under it, like observing, measuring, and predicting, to answer a question.
statements.tl:
Bakit nasa tuktok ng science skills pyramid ang experimenting?

Ang pagsasagawa ng isang makabuluhang experiment ay pinagsasama ang lahat ng basic process skills sa ilalim nito, tulad ng observing, measuring, at predicting, upang masagot ang isang tanong.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1OSgczAaDPaJCjr64sbnEKss8H38P7Yjw), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why do we need a standard when measuring?

A measurement is just comparing an object to a standard. Without a standard, everyone would get a different answer for the same thing!
statements.tl:
Bakit kailangan natin ng standard kapag sumusukat?

Ang pagsukat ay paghahambing lamang ng isang bagay sa isang standard. Kapag walang standard, iba-iba ang makukuhang sagot ng bawat isa sa iisang bagay!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Ze3xgTqtC755O4IDvL9lZlblXqES9WUs), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How can I find the shortest and longest leaves?

Compare their lengths by measuring from tip to base along the longest part.
statements.tl:
