statements.text: Solar energy comes directly from the bright light and cozy heat of our sun!
statements.tl: Ang solar energy ay nagmumula sa liwanag at init ng ating araw!

statements.text:
How does the Sun's size compare to Earth?

The Sun is about 109 times wider than the Earth. It's truly massive!
statements.tl:
Gaano kalaki ang Araw kumpara sa Mundo?

Ang Araw ay mga 109 na beses na mas malaki ang lapad kaysa sa Mundo. Sobrang laki!

statements.text:
What is the Sun mostly made of?

The Sun is mostly made of hydrogen, along with some helium!
statements.tl:
Ano ang pangunahing sangkap ng Araw?

Ang Araw ay halos puro hydrogen, kasama ang kaunting helium!

statements.text: The photosphere is the visible surface of the Sun, and it is where the light we see comes from.
statements.tl: Ang photosphere ang nakikitang surface ng Araw, at dito nanggagaling ang liwanag na nakikita natin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1_JOcvbJ2tw9bl3dHB_ITf6sDjoZl_VTM), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What's the lightest element in the universe?

Hydrogen! It's the most abundant element and the main fuel for stars like our sun. Nuclear fusion of hydrogen creates the heat and light we feel!
statements.tl:
Ano ang pinakamagaan na elemento sa sansinukob?

Hydrogen! Ito ang pinakamarami at pangunahing fuel ng mga bituin tulad ng araw. Ang nuclear fusion ng hydrogen ang gumagawa ng init at liwanag!

statements.text: The sun and stars are mainly made of hydrogen! Through nuclear fusion, hydrogen atoms combine to form helium, releasing enormous energy as light and heat.
statements.tl: Ang araw at mga bituin ay pangunahing gawa sa hydrogen! Sa pamamagitan ng nuclear fusion, pinagsasama ang hydrogen atoms para gumawa ng helium, na naglalabas ng napakalaking enerhiya bilang liwanag at init.

statements.text: The Sun gets its energy from nuclear fusion! Inside, hydrogen nuclei fuse together to create helium and power our star.
statements.tl: Ang Araw ay nakakakuha ng enerhiya mula sa nuclear fusion! Dito, pinagsasama ang hydrogen para maging helium at magbigay-buhay sa Araw.

statements.text: Deep inside the Sun, a cool process called fusion happens! Hydrogen nuclei squish together to make helium.
statements.tl: Sa loob ng Araw, may nangyayaring fusion! Ang mga hydrogen ay pinagsasama-sama para makabuo ng helium.

statements.text: The Sun's surface is made of plasma at 5,500 degrees Celsius—far hotter than boiling water at 100 degrees Celsius!
statements.tl: Ang ibabaw ng Araw ay gawa sa plasma na 5,500 degrees Celsius—mas mainit nang husto kaysa kumukulong tubig na 100 degrees Celsius!

statements.text: The Sun and stars are made of plasma! It is a superheated state of matter where electrons separate from their atoms.
statements.tl: Ang Araw at mga bituin ay gawa sa plasma! Ito ay isang superheated na estado ng matter kung saan ang mga electron ay hiwalay sa kanilang mga atom.

statements.text: Most visible matter in the universe is plasma, the fourth state of matter, which makes up glowing stars like our Sun!
statements.tl: Karamihan sa nakikitang matter sa uniberso ay plasma, ang ika-apat na estado ng matter, na bumubuo sa mga nagliliwanag na bituin tulad ng Araw!

statements.text:
What is the Sun made of?

The Sun is made of plasma, a state of matter with charged particles, at about 5,500 degrees Celsius at its visible surface!
statements.tl:
Sa ano gawa ang Araw?

Ang Araw ay gawa sa plasma, isang estado ng matter na may mga partikulong may karga, na nasa humigit-kumulang 5,500 degrees Celsius sa nakikitang ibabaw nito!

statements.text:
How hot is the Sun's core?

The Sun's core reaches 15 million degrees Celsius, turning hydrogen into dense plasma where nuclear fusion happens!
statements.tl:
Gaano kainit ang core ng Araw?

Ang core ng Araw ay umaabot ng 15 milyong degrees Celsius, nagko-convert ng hydrogen sa dense plasma kung saan nangyayari ang nuclear fusion!

statements.text: Our bright sun sends out more than just visible light; it also beams down invisible ultraviolet and infrared!
statements.tl: Ang ating araw ay hindi lang nagpapadala ng nakikitang liwanag; nagpapadala rin ito ng ultraviolet at infrared!

statements.text: The Sun is the main natural source of heat and light energy for the Philippines and our whole Earth!
statements.tl: Ang Araw ang pangunahing natural na pinagmumulan ng init at liwanag para sa Pilipinas at sa buong Mundo!

statements.text:
How long does it take for sunlight to reach us?

Even with the amazing speed of light, sunlight still takes about 8 minutes to travel all the way from the Sun to Earth!
statements.tl:
Gaano katagal bago makarating sa atin ang sinag ng Araw?

Kahit sa bilis ng liwanag, umaabot ng halos 8 minuto ang sinag ng Araw bago makarating sa Earth!

statements.text: The Sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion! Hydrogen atoms join to form helium, releasing huge amounts of heat and light.
statements.tl: Ang enerhiya ng Araw ay galing sa nuclear fusion! Pinagsasama ang hydrogen atoms para maging helium, naglalabas ng napakaraming init at liwanag.

statements.text: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to travel all the way from the Sun to reach our Earth!
statements.tl: Umaabot ng mga 8 minuto bago makarating ang liwanag ng Araw dito sa ating Mundo!

statements.text: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space, just like a rock, water, and even air!
statements.tl: Ang bagay ay anumang may masa at sumasakop ng puwang, gaya ng isang bato, tubig, at hangin!

statements.text:
Is the air around us just empty space?

Air is not empty! It is a mixture of gases like nitrogen and oxygen that has mass and takes up physical space.
statements.tl:
Ang hangin ba ay walang laman na espasyo?

Ang hangin ay hindi walang laman! Ito ay halo ng mga gas tulad ng nitrogen at oxygen na may masa at sumasakop ng espasyo.

statements.text: Light and sound are not matter because they do not occupy space and do not have mass.
statements.tl: Ang liwanag at tunog ay hindi matter dahil hindi sila sumasakop ng space at walang mass.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1IcyUPBzLyDB68zJTQuSoPnwbR3mMlz54), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Water is a liquid, and liquids are matter, so water has mass that can be measured with a balance.
statements.tl: Ang tubig ay liquid, at ang liquid ay matter, kaya may mass ang tubig na maaaring sukatin gamit ang balance.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1aM3wMlrxKITYVpGo1SlU8jHV3DHz-gGA), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What exactly is matter?

Matter is anything with mass that takes up space! Almost everything you see or touch—like rocks, water, and air—is matter.
statements.tl:
Ano ba ang matter?

Ang matter ay anumang bagay na may mass at sumasakop ng espasyo! Halos lahat ng nakikita o nahahawakan mo—tulad ng bato, tubig, at hangin—ay matter.

statements.text:
What is the difference between mass, volume, and weight?

Mass is the amount of matter, volume is the space it takes, and weight is gravity's pull! Your mass is the same everywhere, but you weigh less on the Moon!
statements.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng mass, volume, at weight?

Ang mass ay dami ng matter, volume ay espasyong sinasakop, at weight ay hila ng gravity! Pareho ang mass mo kahit saan, pero mas magaan ang weight mo sa buwan!

statements.text:
Ever wonder what density really means?

Density is how much mass is packed into a space! It’s higher when more mass fits in the same volume.
statements.tl:
Napag-isipan mo na ba kung ano ang densidad?

Ang densidad ay kung gaano kasiksik ang masa sa isang espasyo! Mas mataas ito kapag mas maraming masa sa parehong sukat.

statements.text:
Did you know air can push you?

Air actually has weight and pushes on everything from all sides! We call this amazing push air pressure.
statements.tl:
Alam mo ba na may puwersa ang hangin?

May bigat ang hangin at tumutulak sa lahat ng bagay mula sa lahat ng panig. Tawag nito ay air pressure!

statements.text: Air is real stuff that takes up space, which is why a balloon grows bigger when you fill it with air!
statements.tl: Ang hangin ay totoong bagay na sumasakop ng espasyo, kaya lumalaki ang lobo kapag pinupuno mo ito ng hangin!

statements.text: All forms of matter—solid, liquid, and gas—have mass and take up space!
statements.tl: Lahat ng anyo ng matter—solido, likido, at gas—ay may mass at sumasakop ng espasyo!

statements.text:
Does invisible air have weight?

Yes! Even though we cannot see it, a gas like air still has weight.
statements.tl:
May bigat ba ang hindi nakikitang hangin?

Oo! Kahit hindi natin ito nakikita, ang gas tulad ng hangin ay may bigat din.

statements.text:
Does invisible air actually have mass?

Even though we cannot see it, air has mass because it is also a kind of matter!
statements.tl:
May masa ba ang hindi nakikitang hangin?

Kahit hindi natin ito nakikita, ang hangin ay may masa dahil ito rin ay isang uri ng bagay!

statements.text:
Can two objects of the same size have different masses?

Yes! Like a heavy metal ball and a light wooden ball.
statements.tl:
Maaari bang magkaiba ng masa ang dalawang bagay na magkasinlaki?

Oo! Gaya ng mabigat na bola ng metal at magaan na bola ng kahoy.

statements.text:
Can invisible air actually have weight?

Yes! Even though you can't see it, the gases in air have mass and weight — air is real matter that presses on you!
statements.tl:
May bigat ba ang hindi nakikitang hangin?

Oo! Kahit hindi mo nakikita, ang mga gas sa hangin ay may mass at bigat — ang hangin ay totoong matter na nakadidiin sa iyo!

statements.text:
What exactly is density?

Density is how tightly packed a material is—its mass for each amount of space (volume) it takes up!
statements.tl:
Ano ba ang density?

Ang density ay kung gaano kasiksik ang isang bagay—ang mass nito sa bawat volume ng espasyong inookupahan nito!

statements.text: Air has weight even though we can't see it! A balloon filled with air is a little heavier than an empty one — proof that gas is real matter with mass.
statements.tl: May timbang ang hangin kahit hindi natin nakikita! Ang lobong puno ng hangin ay bahagyang mas mabigat kaysa walang laman — patunay na ang gas ay tunay na bagay na may mass.

statements.text:
Why does a balloon grow when you blow into it?

Air from your lungs fills it and takes up space inside! This makes the balloon grow bigger and stretch out.
statements.tl:
Bakit lumalaki ang lobo kapag hinihipan mo ito?

Pumupuno ang hangin mula sa baga mo at kumukuha ng espasyo sa loob! Kaya lumalaki at namamaga ang lobo.

statements.text:
If you crush a cookie into crumbs, does it weigh less?

No way! The total weight of all the pieces stays exactly the same — no mass is lost when you crush or tear something!
statements.tl:
Kung durugin mo ang isang cookie, bababa ba ang timbang nito?

Hindi! Pareho pa rin ang kabuuang timbang ng lahat ng piraso — walang masang nawawala kapag dinurog o pinunit mo ang isang bagay!

statements.text: Calamansi and dalandan grow on small trees—the trees bloom with flowers first, then those flowers turn into fruit.
statements.tl: Ang calamansi at dalandan ay tumutubo sa maliliit na puno—namumulaklak muna ito bago maging prutas.

statements.text:
What don't fungi have?

Unlike plants, fungi have no true roots, leaves, or seeds!
statements.tl:
Ano ang wala sa fungi?

Hindi tulad ng halaman, walang tunay na ugat, dahon, o buto ang mga fungi!

statements.text: A fern (pako) is a leafy green plant with broad or finely divided leaves, but it never grows flowers.
statements.tl: Ang pako ay isang halamang madahon at luntian na may malalapad o pino-pinong dahon, ngunit hindi ito namumulaklak.

statements.text: Mosses are tiny flowerless plants that grow packed together, forming a soft green carpet!
statements.tl: Ang lumot ay napakaliit na halamang walang bulaklak, tumutubo itong siksikan na parang malambot na alpombra!

statements.text: A goat is a mammal that makes milk to feed its babies.
statements.tl: Ang kambing ay isang mammal na gumagawa ng gatas para pakainin ang mga anak nito.

statements.text: A classification table has rows and columns! You can line up living things and see which characteristics they share.
statements.tl: May mga row at column ang classification table! Maaari mong ihanay ang mga bagay na may buhay at makita kung aling mga katangian ang pareho nila.

statements.text: Angiosperms are the only plants that produce flowers and fruits, which help them attract pollinators and protect their seeds.
statements.tl: Ang mga angiosperm lang ang gumagawa ng mga bulaklak at prutas, na tumutulong sa kanila na makaakit ng mga pollinator at maprotektahan ang kanilang mga buto.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 13mCWGlfvHkuL0NmZUgnCmoyVRMAMX_f3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How can a table help you classify plants?

You can list features like seeds, leaves, flowers, and fruits, then check which ones match angiosperms or gymnosperms!
statements.tl:
Paano makakatulong ang isang table sa pag-uuri ng mga halaman?

Maaari mong ilista ang mga katangian tulad ng buto, dahon, bulaklak, at prutas, pagkatapos ay tingnan kung alin ang tumutugma sa angiosperms o gymnosperms!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 13mCWGlfvHkuL0NmZUgnCmoyVRMAMX_f3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why do baby mammals drink milk from their mothers?

Because mammals have special body parts called mammary glands that produce milk, and this milk is the first food for their young.
statements.tl:
Bakit umiinom ng gatas ang mga sanggol na mammal mula sa kanilang ina?

Dahil ang mga mammal ay may espesyal na bahagi ng katawan na tinatawag na mammary glands na gumagawa ng gatas, at ito ang unang pagkain ng kanilang anak.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YVAugOh6tS2hAJ2G5TMGknE6vwkCSkq0), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Amphibians like frogs have two life stages: an aquatic gill-breathing larval stage and a terrestrial lung-breathing adult stage.
statements.tl: Ang mga amphibian tulad ng palaka ay may dalawang yugto ng buhay: isang aquatic na larval stage na humihinga gamit ang hasang, at isang terrestrial na adult stage na humihinga gamit ang baga.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YVAugOh6tS2hAJ2G5TMGknE6vwkCSkq0), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Some bacteria are pathogens, which means they can cause diseases like food poisoning, pneumonia, and tetanus.
statements.tl: Ang ilang bacteria ay pathogens, ibig sabihin maaari silang magdulot ng mga sakit tulad ng food poisoning, pneumonia, at tetanus.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YVAugOh6tS2hAJ2G5TMGknE6vwkCSkq0), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why do we group animals like mammals, reptiles, and insects?

Because grouping them by their characteristics helps us understand how they live, what they need, and how to protect them.
statements.tl:
Bakit natin pinapangkat ang mga hayop tulad ng mammals, reptiles, at insects?

Dahil ang pagpapangkat sa kanila ayon sa kanilang katangian ay tumutulong sa atin na maunawaan kung paano sila nabubuhay, ano ang kailangan nila, at paano sila mapoprotektahan.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YVAugOh6tS2hAJ2G5TMGknE6vwkCSkq0), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Amphibians are ectothermic, which means they are cold-blooded animals that need a warm environment to stay active.
statements.tl: Ang mga amphibian ay ectothermic, ibig sabihin sila ay cold-blooded na mga hayop na nangangailangan ng mainit na kapaligiran para manatiling aktibo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YVAugOh6tS2hAJ2G5TMGknE6vwkCSkq0), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Animals use special body parts for protection, like a cow using its horns or a fish using its scales as a shield.
statements.tl: Gumagamit ang mga hayop ng espesyal na bahagi ng katawan para sa proteksyon, tulad ng baka na gumagamit ng sungay o isda na gumagamit ng kaliskis bilang panangga.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1kS8zS-WZr5bwEPb4GO0eWlIDhvUJGax5), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Insects have jointed legs that bend at the joints, which helps them walk, jump, and climb, while animals like snakes have no legs at all.
statements.tl: Ang mga insect ay may jointed legs na nababaluktot sa mga kasukasuan, na tumutulong sa kanila na lumakad, tumalon, at umakyat, habang ang mga ahas ay walang mga paa.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1yWeogp7s-ySyoG9nbgTo0WN6t-3yFpRt), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Birds are warm-blooded, have feathers covering their bodies, lay hard-shelled eggs, and use their beaks for eating.
statements.tl: Ang mga bird ay warm-blooded, may feathers sa katawan, nangingitlog ng hard-shelled eggs, at ginagamit ang beak sa pagkain.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-22621), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Which mammal can really fly?

The bat! It is the only mammal in the whole world that can truly fly using its own wings.
statements.tl:
Anong mammal ang talagang nakakalipad?

Ang paniki! Ito lang ang mammal sa buong mundo na talagang nakakalipad gamit ang sarili niyang mga pakpak.

statements.text:
What does 'amphibian' really mean?

Amphibian means 'two lives' — most begin life in water breathing with gills, then move onto land once they grow lungs.
statements.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng amphibian?

Ang amphibian ay nangangahulugang 'dalawang buhay' — karamihan sa kanila ay nagsisimula sa tubig na may hasang, pagkatapos ay lumilipat sa lupa kapag may baga na.

statements.text: A potato is actually an underground stem called a tuber, and its 'eyes' are buds that can sprout into new plants.
statements.tl: Ang patatas ay isang uri ng tangkay sa ilalim ng lupa na tinatawag na tuber, at ang mga 'mata' nito ay usbong na maaaring tumubo.

statements.text: Seagrass spreads underwater through creeping stems called rhizomes that grow beneath the sand.
statements.tl: Kumakalat ang damong-dagat sa ilalim ng tubig sa pamamagitan ng mga tangkay na tinatawag na rhizome na gumagapang sa ilalim ng buhangin.

statements.text: A bulb, like garlic or onion, is an underground part of a plant that stores food to keep it growing.
statements.tl: Ang bulb ng halaman, tulad ng bawang o sibuyas, ay bahagi ng halaman sa ilalim ng lupa na nag-iimbak ng pagkain para patuloy itong tumubo.

statements.text:
Why do some orchids have roots in the air?

Many orchids growing on trees have aerial roots out in the open air, which they use to cling to branches and soak up water from rain and dew.
statements.tl:
Bakit may ugat sa hangin ang mga orkidya?

Maraming orkidyang tumutubo sa puno ang may aerial roots na nasa hangin, na ginagamit nila para kumapit sa sanga at sumipsip ng tubig mula sa ulan at hamog.

statements.text: Many plants grow sharp thorns or spines just so hungry animals will leave them alone.
statements.tl: Maraming halaman ang may matutulis na tinik para hindi sila kainin ng mga hayop.

statements.text: A rhizome is a stem that grows underground or along the soil surface, and its nodes can send out roots and shoots to make a new plant.
statements.tl: Ang rhizome ay isang stem na tumutubo sa ilalim ng lupa o sa surface ng lupa, at ang mga nodes nito ay maaaring maglabas ng mga ugat at shoot para gumawa ng bagong halaman.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GA1do9DktUoJfHmsQMsNkps6uWZeoEai), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Ginger is a rhizome, a stem that grows underground and has nodes from which new roots and shoots can grow.
statements.tl: Ang luya ay isang rhizome, isang stem na tumutubo sa ilalim ng lupa at may mga nodes kung saan maaaring tumubo ang mga bagong ugat at shoot.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GA1do9DktUoJfHmsQMsNkps6uWZeoEai), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The thick leaves of a bulb are full of stored food, which gives the new shoot energy to start growing.
statements.tl: Ang makakapal na dahon ng bulb ay puno ng nakaimbak na pagkain, na nagbibigay ng enerhiya sa bagong shoot para magsimulang tumubo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1GA1do9DktUoJfHmsQMsNkps6uWZeoEai), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why do calamansi and bougainvillea have thorns?

Thorns and spines are specialized structures that protect plants from animals that try to attack or eat them.
statements.tl:
Bakit may tinik ang calamansi at bougainvillea?

Ang mga tinik at spines ay specialized structures na nagpoprotekta sa halaman mula sa mga hayop na sumusubok umatake o kumain sa kanila.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1IqtRthEHa0dLtv1KAIMH1I-CfoymJSmS), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Plants have specialized structures like thorns, spines, sharp leaves, and bad smells to protect themselves from predators.
statements.tl: Ang mga halaman ay may specialized structures tulad ng tinik, spines, matutulis na dahon, at mabahong amoy para protektahan ang sarili sa mga predator.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1IqtRthEHa0dLtv1KAIMH1I-CfoymJSmS), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Plants reproduce asexually through natural vegetative propagation using parts like bulbs, tubers, runners, and rhizomes without seeds.
statements.tl: Ang mga halaman ay nagpaparami nang asexual sa pamamagitan ng natural vegetative propagation gamit ang mga bahagi tulad ng bulbs, tubers, runners, at rhizomes nang walang buto.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1KPfjghE2Qp_5wmTuwOTczrPnFVq9vfdE), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A bulb is a short stem surrounded by fleshy leaves that store food, helping the plant survive dormancy, a resting period, and grow again later.
statements.tl: Ang bulb ay isang maikling stem na napapalibutan ng malalamang mga dahon na nag-iimbak ng pagkain, na tumutulong sa halaman na mabuhay sa dormancy, o panahon ng pahinga, at tumubo muli sa susunod.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1LA82G6udpL4XCNc3vQT1_r_6CbQqcGYZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Thorns are especially useful in places with many grazing animals, because the sharp points make the plant painful or difficult to eat.
statements.tl: Ang mga tinik ay lalong kapaki-pakinabang sa mga lugar na maraming grazing animals, dahil ang matutulis na dulo ay nagpapahirap o nagpapasakit sa pagkain ng halaman.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1LA82G6udpL4XCNc3vQT1_r_6CbQqcGYZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Specialized structures like rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots help plants survive by storing food, protecting themselves, or absorbing what they need.
statements.tl: Ang mga specialized structures tulad ng rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, at aerial roots ay tumutulong sa mga halaman na mabuhay sa pamamagitan ng pag-iimbak ng pagkain, pagprotekta sa sarili, o pagsipsip ng kanilang kailangan.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1LA82G6udpL4XCNc3vQT1_r_6CbQqcGYZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Citrus plants like kalamansi have thorny stems and branches, and their leaves and fruits have strong-smelling oils with an unpleasant taste.
statements.tl: Ang mga citrus plant tulad ng kalamansi ay may matinik na tangkay at sanga, at ang kanilang mga dahon at prutas ay may mga langis na may malakas na amoy at hindi kaaya-ayang lasa.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1MzX57zZ5PswjHsAam-unYb8H0YzRgGk7), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Thorns and hairs are specialized structures present on some terrestrial plants to help them adapt to their environment.
statements.tl: Ang mga tinik at buhok ay mga specialized structures na makikita sa ilang terrestrial plants para tulungan silang umangkop sa kanilang kapaligiran.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YehRIDC7MAmNg1btRC7G_LFkkw6nvvOE), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The thick and fleshy stem of a cactus is a specialized structure that stores large amounts of water.
statements.tl: Ang makapal at malaman na tangkay ng cactus ay isang specialized structure na nag-iimbak ng maraming tubig.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1YehRIDC7MAmNg1btRC7G_LFkkw6nvvOE), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The taro corm is like the plant's food storehouse—even if you cut off the top, it can grow new shoots using the starch stored inside.
statements.tl: Ang corm ng gabi ay parang imbakan ng pagkain ng halaman—kahit putulin ang itaas, kaya pa itong magpatubo ng bagong usbong gamit ang almirol na nakaimbak sa loob.

statements.text: Storing water inside its body is a plant's clever trick for surviving in hot, dry places.
statements.tl: Ang pag-iimbak ng tubig ay isang matalinong paraan ng halaman para mabuhay sa mainit at tuyong lugar.

statements.text: A cactus keeps water stored inside its thick stem, which is how it survives in dry places.
statements.tl: Nag-iimbak ng tubig ang kaktus sa loob ng makapal nitong tangkay para mabuhay ito sa tuyong lugar.

statements.text:
Why do some mangroves have upright roots?

Wet mud has very little air, so some mangroves grow special roots that stick up above the ground to breathe in oxygen.
statements.tl:
Bakit may nakatirik na ugat ang ilang mangrove?

Kaunti lang ang hangin sa basang putik, kaya may mga mangrove na may ugat na tumataas sa ibabaw para makahinga ng oxygen.

statements.text: The Philippines' tropical dry forests, like those on Cebu and parts of the Visayas, drop their leaves in the dry season and are home to unique native species.
statements.tl: Ang mga tropical dry forest ng Pilipinas, gaya ng sa Cebu at ilang bahagi ng Visayas, nagtatanggal ng dahon sa tag-init at may natatanging katutubong species.

statements.text:
Why don't trees take over the savanna?

Grass fires! Dry grass burns but grows back quickly from roots underground, and the fires keep trees from spreading.
statements.tl:
Bakit hindi natatakpan ng puno ang savanna?

Dahil sa sunog ng damo! Nasusunog ang tuyong damo pero mabilis itong tumutubong muli mula sa ugat, at ang sunog ang pumipigil sa mga puno.

statements.text:
How do desert plants survive dry days?

A cactus stores water in its thick body, and its spines — instead of leaves — help it lose less water in the dry desert.
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuhay ang halaman sa disyerto?

Nag-iimbak ng tubig ang cactus sa makapal nitong katawan, at ang mga tinik nito — sa halip na dahon — ay tumutulong para hindi ito madaling matuyuan.

statements.text:
How do mangroves survive salty water?

Different mangroves cope in different ways — some block salt at the roots, others push extra salt out through special glands on their leaves.
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuhay ang bakawan sa maalat na tubig?

Iba't ibang paraan ang ginagamit ng bakawan — ang iba ay humaharang ng asin sa ugat, ang iba naman ay naglalabas ng asin sa gland ng dahon.

statements.text:
How does rice survive underwater roots?

Rice plants have special air channels inside that carry oxygen from the leaves all the way down to roots sitting underwater.
statements.tl:
Paano huminga ang ugat ng palay sa tubig?

May espesyal na daanan ng hangin ang palay sa loob nito na nagdadala ng oxygen mula sa dahon papunta sa ugat na nasa tubig.

statements.text: Thick bark protects some trees from fire and from extreme heat or cold.
statements.tl: Ang makapal na balat ng ilang puno ay nagbibigay proteksyon laban sa sunog at matinding init o lamig.

statements.text: Some plants eat insects because they grow in poor soil that lacks nutrients like nitrogen!
statements.tl: Kumakain ng insekto ang ilang halaman dahil tumutubo sila sa mahirap na lupa na kulang sa sustansya gaya ng nitroheno!
statements.source: NRC LS1.A; Britannica carnivorous plant; encyclopedia-stable

statements.text:
What's the difference between a habitat and an adaptation?

A habitat is an organism's natural home, while an adaptation is a special trait that helps it survive there, like thick fur in the cold or deep roots in the desert.
statements.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng habitat at adaptation?

Ang habitat ay ang natural na tirahan ng halaman o hayop, habang ang adaptation ay katangiang tumutulong dito mabuhay, tulad ng makapal na balahibo sa lamig o malalim na ugat sa disyerto.

statements.text: Some plants have special adaptations to their environment: a cactus has a thick stem to store water in the desert, and a mangrove has roots that can stand in the salty water of the shore.
statements.tl: May mga halamang may espesyal na angkop na tampok sa kanilang kapaligiran: ang cactus ay may makapal na tangkay na nag-iimbak ng tubig sa disyerto, at ang bakawan ay may ugat na kayang tumayo sa maalat na tubig ng baybayin.

statements.text:
Why are stomata mostly on the underside of leaves?

To reduce the amount of water the leaf loses — being underneath keeps them shaded and cooler.
statements.tl:
Bakit karamihan ng stomata ay nasa ilalim ng dahon?

Para mabawasan ang tubig na nawawala sa dahon — sa ilalim, mas malamig at protektado ang mga stomata.

statements.text:
Why does talisay grow by the beach?

The talisay tree can handle the salt in seawater and the salty sea breeze, which many other trees can't — that's why it grows right along the beach.
statements.tl:
Bakit tumutubo sa tabing-dagat ang talisay?

Kaya ng talisay na tiisin ang asin sa tubig-dagat at ang maalat na hangin, hindi tulad ng ibang puno, kaya madalas itong nakatanim sa tabing-dagat.

statements.text:
Why do trees in cold countries drop their leaves?

In cold countries, trees drop their leaves in winter to save water and avoid damage from the deep cold.
statements.tl:
Bakit naglalaglag ng dahon ang mga punong nasa malamig na bansa?

Sa malalamig na bansa, naglalaglag ng dahon ang mga puno tuwing taglamig para makatipid ng tubig at maiwasan ang pinsala mula sa matinding lamig.

statements.text:
Are cactus spines really leaves?

A cactus's spines are actually leaves that changed shape — this helps the plant lose only a little water!
statements.tl:
Dahon ba talaga ang tinik ng kaktus?

Ang mga tinik ng kaktus ay dahon na nagbago ng anyo — tumutulong ito para kaunti lang ang mawalang tubig ng halaman!

statements.text: Some desert plants wait patiently, then quickly bloom and make seeds the moment rare rain finally falls.
statements.tl: Ilang halaman sa disyerto ay matiyagang naghihintay, at mabilis na namumulaklak at gumagawa ng buto sa sandaling dumating ang bihirang ulan.

statements.text:
Are pine needles really leaves?

Yes! Pine trees in Baguio have thin, needle-shaped leaves — their slim shape helps them save water in cold places.
statements.tl:
Dahon ba ang matulis na 'karayom' ng pino?

Oo! Ang mga pino sa Baguio ay may manipis at matulis na dahon na parang karayom — tumutulong ang manipis na hugis nila para makatipid ng tubig sa malamig na lugar.

statements.text: All forms of matter—solid, liquid, and gas—have mass and take up space!
statements.tl: Lahat ng anyo ng matter—solido, likido, at gas—ay may mass at sumasakop ng espasyo!

statements.text: Matter in solid, liquid, and gas states is made of particles, but the particles are arranged differently in each state.
statements.tl: Ang matter sa solid, liquid, at gas states ay gawa sa particles, pero magkakaiba ang pagkakaayos ng particles sa bawat state.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 15pMwYkMQl0wMZjzuH60KvYT497oEzrmJ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Matter has three common states! A solid keeps its shape, like a rock. Liquid flows to fit its container, like water. Gas spreads out, like air. All have mass!
statements.tl: May tatlong karaniwang estado ang matter! Solid ay may sariling hugis, tulad ng bato. Liquid ay umaayos sa lalagyan, tulad ng tubig. Gas ay kumakalat, tulad ng hangin. Lahat ay may mass!

statements.text: Evaporation, condensation, and sublimation are amazing changes of state of matter between solid, liquid, and gas!
statements.tl: Ang pagsingaw, paghalay, at sublimation ay mga pagbabago ng anyo ng bagay sa pagitan ng solido, likido, at gas!

statements.text:
What are the three common forms of matter?

Three: solid, liquid, and gas!
statements.tl:
Ilan ang pangunahing anyo ng matter?

Tatlo: solido, likido, at gas!

statements.text: Water is amazing! It can be a solid (ice), a liquid (water), or a gas (water vapor).
statements.tl: Nakakamangha ang tubig! Maaari itong maging solido (yelo), likido (tubig), o gas (singaw ng tubig).

statements.text: Matter can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas, just like ice, water, and steam!
statements.tl: Ang bagay ay maaaring solido, likido, o gas, gaya ng yelo, tubig, at singaw!

statements.text:
Why is water so special on Earth?

Water is the only common thing on Earth naturally found as a solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (vapor) at everyday temperatures!
statements.tl:
Bakit espesyal ang tubig sa Earth?

Ang tubig lang ang karaniwang bagay sa Earth na natural na naging solido (yelo), likido (tubig), at gas (singaw) sa pang-araw-araw na temperatura!

statements.text:
Is steam really just water?

Yes! Steam is still water, just in gas form. It turns back into liquid water when it cools down through condensation.
statements.tl:
Tubig pa rin ba ang singaw?

Oo! Ang singaw ay tubig pa rin, nasa anyong gas lang. Babalik ito sa likido kapag lumamig sa proseso ng condensation.

statements.text: Water is awesome! We encounter it in three common states: solid ice, liquid water, and water vapor.
statements.tl: Ang tubig ay espesyal! Nakatatagpo natin ito sa tatlong karaniwang anyo: solid na yelo, likidong tubig, at gas na singaw.
statements.source: NRC PS1.A grade-2 endpoint (solid or liquid by temperature)

statements.text: Smoke is made of tiny solid pieces and liquid droplets floating in gases released when something burns!
statements.tl: Ang usok ay gawa sa napakaliit na piraso ng solido at patak ng likido na lumulutang sa mga gas ng nasusunog!

statements.text: Ice, liquid water, and steam are actually all the exact same thing—just water in three different forms!
statements.tl: Ang yelo, tubig, at singaw ay iisang bagay lamang—tubig na may tatlong iba't ibang anyo!

statements.text: True water vapor is an invisible gas! The white steam or cloud you see is actually made of tiny liquid water droplets.
statements.tl: Ang tunay na singaw ng tubig ay isang gas na hindi nakikita! Ang puting usok o ulap na nakikita mo ay maliliit na patak ng tubig.

statements.text: You can't pour a solid rock, but a liquid pours easily! A gas is even sneakier—it spreads all by itself without you pouring it at all.
statements.tl: Hindi mo maibubuhos ang isang solidong bato, pero madaling maibubuhos ang likido! Ang gas ay mas nakakagulat—kumakalat ito nang kusa kahit hindi mo ibuhos.

statements.text:
Are all metals solid at room temperature?

Almost all metals are solid, except mercury, which is a liquid!
statements.tl:
Lahat ba ng metal ay solido sa temperatura ng kuwarto?

Halos lahat ng metal ay solido, maliban sa asoge na likido!

statements.text:
How can we sort matter into three common states?

Matter is sorted into solids that hold their shape, liquids that flow, and gases that spread out to fill their container!
statements.tl:
Paano natin iuuri ang materya sa tatlong karaniwang estado?

Ang materya ay inuuri sa solidong may sariling hugis, likidong umaagos, at gas na kumakalat upang punuin ang lalagyan!
statements.source: NRC PS1.A; DepEd MATATAG Science (states of matter)

statements.text:
Did you know fuel comes in different shapes?

Fuel that burns can be a solid like wood, a liquid like gasoline, or a gas like LPG!
statements.tl:
Alam mo ba na iba-iba ang hugis ng panggatong?

Maaaring solido tulad ng kahoy, likido tulad ng gasolina, o gas tulad ng LPG ang panggatong na nasusunog!

statements.text: Real steam is actually invisible! The white cloud above boiling water is just tiny water droplets. The true, clear steam hides in the small gap right at the spout!
statements.tl: Ang totoong singaw ay hindi nakikita! Ang puting ulap sa ibabaw ng kumukulong tubig ay maliliit na patak ng tubig. Ang tunay na singaw ay nasa maliit na puwang sa labasan!

statements.text:
What shape does a gas have?

A gas has no fixed shape — it spreads to fill its whole container, like air in a balloon!
statements.tl:
Anong hugis ang gas?

Walang sariling hugis ang gas — pinupuno nito ang buong lalagyan, tulad ng hangin sa lobo!

statements.text: A solid keeps its own shape and volume, even when you move it to a completely different container!
statements.tl: Ang solido ay may sariling hugis at bolyum na hindi nagbabago kahit ilipat sa ibang sisidlan!

statements.text:
How does a liquid behave in a new cup?

A liquid has a fixed volume, but it takes the shape of whatever container holds it!
statements.tl:
Paano kumikilos ang likido sa bagong baso?

Ang likido ay may tiyak na bolyum, pero kumukuha ito ng hugis ng anumang sisidlang kinalalagyan nito!

statements.text: A solid has a definite volume, meaning the amount of space it takes up does not change when you move it to a different container.
statements.tl: Ang solid ay may definite volume, ibig sabihin ang dami ng espasyong sinasakop nito ay hindi nagbabago kapag inilipat mo ito sa ibang lalagyan.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 12UG4A8tr3q5AR60H01GUIZdgeTr43w4I), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A solid has a fixed shape and a fixed volume, so a rock stays the same shape whether you put it on a table or in a jar.
statements.tl: Ang solid ay may hindi nagbabagong hugis at volume, kaya ang bato ay nananatiling pareho ang hugis kahit ilagay mo sa mesa o sa garapon.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1mZt24F4MX_KphuITxqd833M0CkHXWMfV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A gas expands to fill all the available space in a room or container, so the air from a balloon spreads out everywhere when the balloon pops.
statements.tl: Ang gas ay lumalaki at pumupuno sa buong espasyo ng silid o lalagyan, kaya kumakalat ang hangin mula sa lobo kapag ito ay pumutok.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1mZt24F4MX_KphuITxqd833M0CkHXWMfV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What happens to a solid's shape when you move it?

A solid keeps its own shape even when you move it — just like a rock!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa hugis ng solido kapag inilipat mo?

Pinapanatili ng solido ang hugis nito kahit ilipat mo — tulad ng bato!

statements.text: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container — just like water filling a glass!
statements.tl: Umaagos ang likido at kumukuha ng hugis ng lalagyan nito — tulad ng tubig sa baso!

statements.text: A solid normally keeps its own shape and size (volume) rather than taking its container's shape!
statements.tl: Karaniwang pinapanatili ng solido ang sarili nitong hugis at laki (volume) sa halip na sundin ang hugis ng lalagyan!

statements.text:
Does a liquid keep the same volume when it changes shape?

Yes! A liquid changes shape but keeps the same amount of space (volume).
statements.tl:
Nanatili ba ang parehong volume ng likido kapag nagbabago ang hugis?

Oo! Nagbabago ng hugis ang likido pero nananatiling pareho ang laki (volume).

statements.text: A gas has no fixed shape or size — it spreads out to fill any space available!
statements.tl: Walang tiyak na hugis o laki ang gas — lumalawak ito upang punuin ang anumang espasyo!

statements.text:
Can you squeeze a gas into a smaller space?

Yes! A gas can be squeezed into a smaller space, which is why we can pump air into a tire!
statements.tl:
Pwede bang siksikin ang gas sa mas maliit na espasyo?

Oo! Pwedeng siksikin ang gas sa mas maliit na espasyo, kaya napupuno natin ng hangin ang gulong!

statements.text:
Does gas have its own shape?

No! Gas takes the shape of its container. The same air becomes round in a round balloon and long in a long balloon!
statements.tl:
May sarili bang hugis ang gas?

Wala! Sumusunod ang gas sa hugis ng lalagyan nito. Nagiging bilog ang hangin sa bilog na lobo at mahaba sa mahabang lobo!

statements.text: When you look at them up close, salt crystals are shaped like tiny cubes or little boxes!
statements.tl: Kapag tiningnan nang malapitan, ang mga crystal ng asin ay parang maliliit na kubo o kahon!

statements.text: Sand and salt seem to pour like a liquid, but each tiny grain is actually a solid that keeps its own shape!
statements.tl: Parang umaagos ang buhangin at asin kapag ibinubuhos, pero bawat maliit na butil ay solido na may sariling hugis!

statements.text: When you break a solid like a chocolate bar, every single piece is still a solid and keeps its own shape!
statements.tl: Kapag binasag mo ang solido tulad ng tsokolate, bawat piraso ay solido pa rin at may sariling hugis!

statements.text: You can easily hold a solid in your hand! But liquids drip and gases spread out, so you need a container for them.
statements.tl: Madali mong mahawakan ang solido sa kamay! Pero tumutulo ang likido at kumakalat ang gas, kaya kailangan ng lalagyan para sa kanila.

statements.text: When you pour water into a different container, its shape changes, but its volume stays exactly the same!
statements.tl: Kapag ibinuhos mo ang tubig sa ibang lalagyan, nagbabago ang hugis nito, ngunit pareho pa rin ang bolyum!

statements.text:
Is air just one single gas?

Nope! Air is actually a mixture of several different gases mixed all together.
statements.tl:
Iisang gas lang ba ang hangin?

Hindi! Ang hangin ay isang halo o mixture ng iba't ibang gas.

statements.text: Ice is simply water in its solid form — water that has frozen and turned hard because of the cold! ❄️
statements.tl: Ang yelo ay tubig sa solidong anyo nito — tubig na naging matigas dahil sa lamig! ❄️
statements.source: NRC PS1.A states of matter; encyclopedia-stable

statements.text: Air is a common example of gas, and it is all around us, filling the sky, our homes, and even the empty spaces inside a sponge.
statements.tl: Ang hangin ay karaniwang halimbawa ng gas, at ito ay nasa paligid natin, pinupuno ang kalangitan, ang ating mga tahanan, at maging ang mga bakanteng espasyo sa loob ng espongha.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-FfkBsuzLybxVgQMJw4KW36ZO9rpRqEx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The air that comes out of your mouth when you breathe out is also a gas, and you can feel it when you blow on your hand.
statements.tl: Ang hangin na lumalabas sa iyong bibig kapag humihinga ka palabas ay gas din, at nararamdaman mo ito kapag humihip ka sa iyong kamay.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-FfkBsuzLybxVgQMJw4KW36ZO9rpRqEx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What liquid has a pleasant smell?

Cologne is a liquid with a pleasant odor, so we use it to smell nice!
statements.tl:
Anong liquid ang may kaaya-ayang amoy?

Ang cologne ay liquid na may magandang amoy, kaya ginagamit natin ito para bumango!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 11eKcrRRHW0sotb6u1yPuyqNeqX9aeCdG), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The air we breathe and the helium in birthday balloons are gases, and their particles are not close together at all.
statements.tl: Ang hangin na ating nilalanghap at ang helium sa mga lobo ay mga gas, at ang kanilang particles ay hindi magkakadikit.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 13B5-eOIrBv9RttyTRQ3Wu32Xxaqpz8G9), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Water, alcohol, and soft drinks are liquids that flow fast when you pour them.
statements.tl: Ang tubig, alcohol, at soft drinks ay mga liquid na mabilis dumaloy kapag ibinuhos.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 155KTsnyP1ybTX4NcppZsToCZPd8KEyE3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Beans and rice grains form a solid-solid mixture because both are solids that stay separate and can be easily distinguished.
statements.tl: Ang beans at butil ng bigas ay bumubuo ng solid-solid mixture dahil pareho silang solids na nananatiling hiwalay at madaling makilala.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Mp2MU2u71DAEh3xm_bIq7faZrPIzu2Rv), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When ice cubes are exposed to sunlight, they absorb heat and melt into liquid water, but the composition stays the same.
statements.tl: Kapag ang ice cubes ay nalantad sa sikat ng araw, sumisipsip sila ng init at natutunaw para maging liquid na tubig, pero ang komposisyon ay nananatiling pareho.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1WlUc-vwin-7tox1tG4razIHf_JZNq15n), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Air, oxygen, carbon dioxide, helium, steam, methane, and chlorine gas are examples of gases that surround us.
statements.tl: Ang hangin, oxygen, carbon dioxide, helium, steam, methane, at chlorine gas ay mga halimbawa ng gas na nakapaligid sa atin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1mZt24F4MX_KphuITxqd833M0CkHXWMfV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: In school, solids include erasers, chalk, books, pad paper, tables, chairs, and the blackboard.
statements.tl: Sa paaralan, ang mga solid ay eraser, chalk, libro, pad paper, mesa, upuan, at blackboard.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1mZt24F4MX_KphuITxqd833M0CkHXWMfV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Mercury is a liquid metal with stronger surface tension than water. Instead of spreading out, it forms little round beads!
statements.tl: Ang mercury ay isang likidong metal na may mas malakas na surface tension kaysa tubig. Sa halip na kumalat, nagbibilog ito sa maliliit na butil!

statements.text:
What happens when you pour a liquid?

You can pour and stir liquids like water! It splits apart when poured, then joins back together in a container.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagbubuhos ng likido?

Pwede mong ibuhos at haluin ang likido tulad ng tubig! Humihiwalay ito kapag binuhos, at muling nagsasama sa lalagyan.

statements.text: Bubbles in water are actually tiny pockets of gas trapped inside the liquid! They float up to the top and pop right into the air.
statements.tl: Ang mga bula sa tubig ay maliliit na bulsa ng gas na nakakulong sa loob ng likido! Pumapaibabaw sila at sumasabog sa hangin.

statements.text:
Can you spot all three states of matter at home?

Yes! Look for solids like rice and a spoon, liquids like soup and water, and gases like the air inside a balloon.
statements.tl:
Makikita mo ba ang tatlong estado ng materya sa bahay?

Oo! Hanapin ang mga solido tulad ng kanin at kutsara, likido tulad ng sabaw at tubig, at gas tulad ng hangin sa loob ng lobo.

statements.text: In the Philippines, bamboo builds nipa huts, ladders, and tools because it's a solid with a strong, fixed shape. It stays straight and firm to support weight!
statements.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ginagamit ang kawayan sa paggawa ng bahay kubo, hagdan, at gamit dahil solid ito na may matibay at fixed na hugis. Nanatili itong tuwid at matigas para suportahan ang bigat!

statements.text: Solid metal keeps its shape and doesn't flow, so you can hold a coin! Water is a liquid that flows and takes its container's shape because their tiny parts hold differently.
statements.tl: Ang solid metal ay may sariling hugis at hindi umaagos, kaya kaya mong hawakan ang barya! Ang tubig ay likido at umaayos sa lalagyan dahil iba ang lakas ng kapit ng mga maliliit na bahagi nila.

statements.text: Sublimation is when a solid changes directly into a gas, skipping the liquid state! For example, dry ice (solid CO2) turns straight into carbon dioxide gas.
statements.tl: Ang sublimation ay kapag ang isang solid ay direktang nagiging gas, nilaktawan ang liquid state! Halimbawa, ang dry ice (solid CO2) ay direktang nagiging carbon dioxide gas.

statements.text: The volume of a liquid is usually measured in liters (L) and milliliters (mL)!
statements.tl: Ang volume ng isang likido ay karaniwang sinusukat sa litro (L) at mililitro (mL)!

statements.text: A graduated cylinder is a marked container used to measure the volume of a liquid!
statements.tl: Ang graduated cylinder ay isang sisidlang may marka na ginagamit upang sukatin ang volume ng likido!

statements.text: The meniscus is the curve liquid makes in a container. Water has a concave meniscus! Always read the bottom of the curve at eye level for an accurate measurement.
statements.tl: Ang meniscus ay ang kurba ng likido sa lalagyan. Ang tubig ay may concave na meniscus! Basahin palagi ang ibaba ng meniscus sa antas ng mata para sa tumpak na sukat.

statements.text: Did you know that one whole liter is exactly equal to 1,000 milliliters? That is a lot!
statements.tl: Alam mo ba na isang buong litro ay katumbas ng 1,000 mililitro? Nakakamangha, 'di ba!

statements.text: Common tools for measuring volume include beakers, graduated cylinders, measuring cups, measuring spoons, and droppers.
statements.tl: Ang mga karaniwang tools sa pagsukat ng volume ay beaker, graduated cylinder, measuring cup, measuring spoon, at dropper.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1XhZW7TIbTd2lz5wAoo-htWN63Cp0g_Og), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What is a milliliter?

A milliliter is a small unit of volume, abbreviated mL. It is used for small amounts like a spoonful of medicine or a few drops of liquid.
statements.tl:
Ano ang milliliter?

Ang milliliter ay maliit na unit ng volume, dinadaglat bilang mL. Ginagamit ito para sa maliliit na dami tulad ng isang kutsarang gamot o ilang patak ng liquid.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1XhZW7TIbTd2lz5wAoo-htWN63Cp0g_Og), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: To measure water volume accurately, pour the water into a graduated cylinder placed on a flat, level surface and read the lower meniscus.
statements.tl: Para sukatin ang water volume nang tama, ibuhos ang tubig sa graduated cylinder na nakalagay sa patag at pantay na surface at basahin ang lower meniscus.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Ze3xgTqtC755O4IDvL9lZlblXqES9WUs), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Common volume units include cubic meter, cubic centimeter, liter, and milliliter.
statements.tl: Ang mga karaniwang unit ng volume ay cubic meter, cubic centimeter, liter, at milliliter.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1qbUoKa3pkKVw_g4_HpknWSwb-yvENx1q), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Liters are used to measure larger amounts of liquid, such as the volume of water in a bottle or milk in a carton.
statements.tl: Ang liter ay ginagamit sa pagsukat ng mas malalaking dami ng liquid, tulad ng volume ng tubig sa isang bote o gatas sa isang karton.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1yFNBraZyBnMuCUfOoMptJFQDinX_6Ogi), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Did you know? One full liter of liquid is exactly equal to one thousand tiny milliliters!
statements.tl: Alam mo ba? Ang isang buong litro ng likido ay katumbas ng isang libong maliit na mililitro!

statements.text:
Ever looked closely at water inside a thin glass tube?

The surface curves slightly upward at the edges! Scientists call this cool upward curve the meniscus.
statements.tl:
Napatingin ka na ba nang malapitan sa tubig sa loob ng manipis na tubo?

Kumukurba pataas nang bahagya ang ibabaw sa mga gilid! Tinatawag itong meniscus ng mga siyentipiko.

statements.text: Look at water in a narrow glass — it curves up at the edges! This U-shape curve is called a meniscus, caused by water adhering to the glass.
statements.tl: Tingnan ang tubig sa makitid na baso — mas mataas ito sa gilid! Ang kurbang ito ay tinatawag na meniscus, dahil sa adhesion ng tubig sa salamin.

statements.text:
How do we measure the volume of liquids?

We measure liquid volume in liters and milliliters, and one liter is exactly 1,000 milliliters!
statements.tl:
Paano natin sinusukat ang bolyum ng mga likido?

Sinusukat natin ang bolyum ng likido sa litro at mililitro, at isang litro ay 1,000 mililitro!

statements.text:
What is the density of water, and why is it so special?

Water has a density of about one gram per milliliter! Scientists use this as a standard reference for other materials.
statements.tl:
Ano ang densidad ng tubig, at bakit ito espesyal?

Ang densidad ng tubig ay halos isang gramo bawat mililitro! Ginagamit itong panukat o reference para sa ibang mga bagay.

statements.text: Capacity is how much liquid a container can hold! We measure it in liters or milliliters using a marked measuring tool.
statements.tl: Ang kapasidad ay kung gaano karaming likido ang kayang lamanin ng isang lalagyan! Sinusukat ito sa litro o mililitro gamit ang panukat na may marka.

statements.text:
How do we measure a liquid's volume accurately?

Use a graduated cylinder! It is a tall, narrow container with marked lines to measure liquids in milliliters.
statements.tl:
Paano natin nasusukat nang tumpak ang volume ng likido?

Gamitin ang graduated cylinder! Ito ay matangkad at makitid na sisidlan na may markang guhit para sukatin ang likido sa mililitro.

statements.text: To measure the volume of a rock: note the water level in a graduated cylinder, submerge the rock, and note the new level. The difference is the rock's volume!
statements.tl: Para sukatin ang volume ng bato: tandaan ang water level sa graduated cylinder, isawsaw ang bato, at tandaan ang bagong level. Ang pagkakaiba ay ang volume ng bato!

statements.text: Volume units for liquids: 1 litre (L) = 1,000 millilitres (mL), and 1 mL = 1 cubic centimetre (cm3). A 1.5 L bottle holds 1,500 mL or 1,500 cm3!
statements.tl: Volume units para sa liquids: 1 litre (L) = 1,000 millilitres (mL), at 1 mL = 1 cubic centimetre (cm3). Ang 1.5 L na bote ay may 1,500 mL o 1,500 cm3!

statements.text: When a liquid is cooled enough, it freezes and turns into a solid!
statements.tl: Kapag pinalamig nang husto ang isang likido, nagyeyelo ito at nagiging solido!

statements.text: Cold ice cream melts and turns into a liquid when left in a warm place!
statements.tl: Natutunaw at nagiging likido ang malamig na sorbetes kapag iniwan sa mainit na lugar!

statements.text: Those tiny dew drops on grass? They form by condensation, when water vapor turns into liquid!
statements.tl: Yung mga maliliit na patak ng hamog sa damo? Nabubuo yan ng kondensasyon, kapag ang singaw ng tubig ay nagiging likido!

statements.text: Heat from the Sun causes liquid water in Laguna de Bay to evaporate into invisible water vapor!
statements.tl: Ang init ng Sun ay nagpapasingaw ng likidong tubig sa Laguna de Bay, na nagiging hindi nakikitang water vapor!

statements.text: Heat is the main factor needed for evaporation, because it gives liquid particles enough energy to escape as gas.
statements.tl: Ang init ang pangunahing kailangan sa evaporation, dahil binibigyan nito ng sapat na energy ang mga particle ng likido para makatakas bilang gas.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1AliS4lwIrWBWM75nBStWj9PgV7IO6DJG), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Matter can change from one state to another: melting, evaporation, condensation, freezing, sublimation, and deposition are all phase changes caused by adding or removing heat energy.
statements.tl: Ang matter ay kayang magbago mula sa isang state papunta sa iba: ang melting, evaporation, condensation, freezing, sublimation, at deposition ay mga phase changes na dulot ng pagdagdag o pag-alis ng heat energy.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1XPsep6pac9dLGnh1BresRgf5YqLdWA_Y), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Matter can change its physical form when heated or cooled, and these changes include melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, and deposition.
statements.tl: Ang matter ay maaaring magbago ng physical na anyo kapag naiinitan o nalalamigan, at kabilang sa mga pagbabagong ito ang melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, at deposition.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1cjm47UgdZv_i3qHy2WDTb-hzL_AKeORe), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When water boils or evaporates, some of the liquid water escapes as water vapor into the air, so the volume of water left behind becomes smaller.
statements.tl: Kapag kumukulo o sumisingaw ang tubig, ang ilang likidong tubig ay lumalabas bilang water vapor sa hangin, kaya nababawasan ang volume ng natitirang tubig.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1p0LGJkHVdtMWACFcSzl_O4sYFamoLtVZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: An ice sculpture melts in a warm room, losing its carved details and becoming more rounded.
statements.tl: Natutunaw ang ice sculpture sa mainit na silid, nawawala ang mga inukit na detalye at nagiging mas bilugan.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1sqTHP-QIp686KhokVl4p9aGGYdupmCSU), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When butter is placed on a hot pan, it melts into a liquid, showing that heat can change a solid's form.
statements.tl: Kapag ang butter ay inilagay sa mainit na kawali, ito ay natutunaw at nagiging liquid, na nagpapakita na kayang baguhin ng init ang anyo ng solid.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Cp5-gPDOW6gyu7Z5QvkjGIFwk_Vf3Z1m), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why does your breath 'fog' up?

Your breath carries water vapor, not just carbon dioxide! Breathe onto a cold mirror or into chilly air and you'll see tiny droplets form.
statements.tl:
Bakit umuusok ang hininga mo?

Bukod sa carbon dioxide, may dalang singaw ng tubig ang hininga mo! Huminga sa malamig na salamin o hangin at makikita mong nabubuo ang maliliit na patak.

statements.text:
Why does a whale blow out mist?

The white spout you see a whale blow isn't smoke; it's just the whale's warm breath turning into mist in the cool air.
statements.tl:
Bakit may singaw na lumalabas sa balyena?

Ang puting singaw na sinasabog ng balyena ay hindi usok; ito ay ang mainit nitong hininga na naging ambon dahil sa malamig na hangin.

statements.text:
How does matter change its state?

When heated or cooled, solid melts to liquid, liquid freezes to solid or evaporates to gas, and gas condenses to liquid. It's still the same substance!
statements.tl:
Paano nagbabago ang state ng matter?

Kapag iniinit o pinapalamig, natutunaw ang solid sa liquid, nagyeyelo ang liquid sa solid o sumisingaw sa gas, at nagco-condense ang gas. Pareho pa rin ang sangkap!

statements.text: A bathroom mirror fogs up after a hot shower! Warm water vapor touches the cool mirror and condenses into tiny droplets, just like a sweating cold glass.
statements.tl: Nalalabo ang salamin sa banyo pagkatapos ng mainit na shower! Ang maraming singaw ng tubig ay dumidikit sa malamig na salamin at nag-co-condense sa maliliit na patak.

statements.text: Different materials melt at different temperatures! It takes a low temperature for ice, but a very high temperature for metal.
statements.tl: Iba-iba ang temperaturang kailangan para matunaw ang mga bagay! Mababa lang para sa yelo, pero napakataas para sa bakal.
statements.source: Melting points vary by substance; encyclopedia-stable

statements.text:
What is evaporation?

Evaporation is when liquid water turns into water vapor, a gas, because of heat!
statements.tl:
Ano ang pagsingaw?

Ang pagsingaw ay kapag ang likidong tubig ay nagiging singaw o gas dahil sa init!

statements.text:
What is condensation?

Condensation is when water vapor, a gas, turns back into liquid water when it cools down!
statements.tl:
Ano ang paghalay?

Ang paghalay ay kapag ang singaw o gas ay nagiging likidong tubig kapag lumamig!

statements.text:
How do clouds form in the sky?

Clouds form when water vapor rises into cooler air and condenses into tiny water droplets!
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang mga ulap sa langit?

Nabubuo ang mga ulap kapag ang singaw ng tubig ay umakyat sa malamig na hangin at naging maliliit na patak ng tubig!

statements.text:
What is the first thing you must state in an investigation?

You state the aim or problem, which is the purpose or reason why you are doing the activity. It can be written as a question or a statement.
statements.tl:
Ano ang unang dapat mong sabihin sa isang investigation?

Sasabihin mo ang aim o problem, na siyang layunin o dahilan kung bakit mo ginagawa ang activity. Puwede itong isulat bilang tanong o pahayag.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1My4b2WkUuwo_H0dOdwiuwKUf9-9S00fT), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A simple investigation starts by writing a clear problem, like which material dries faster, so you know exactly what you are trying to find out!
statements.tl: Nagsisimula ang simpleng investigation sa pagsulat ng malinaw na problem, tulad ng kung aling material ang mas mabilis matuyo, para alam mo ang hahanapin!

statements.text: Turn your problem into a question you can actually test, not just a story, so your next steps have a real job to do!
statements.tl: Gawing tanong ang problem na pwedeng i-test, hindi kwento, para ang susunod na steps ay may tunay na gawain!

statements.text: List every material before you begin, including cups, water, and a timer, so you won't be hunting for tools in the middle of a step!
statements.tl: Ilista ang bawat materyal bago magsimula, kabilang ang mga tasa, tubig, at timer, upang hindi ka maghanap ng kagamitan sa gitna ng isang hakbang!

statements.text:
Why should you only list the materials you really need?

Write only the materials the test needs, because extra bottles and powders on the table make it too easy to use the wrong one!
statements.tl:
Bakit kailangan ilista lang ang materials na kailangan talaga?

Isulat lang ang materials na kailangan ng test, kasi kung maraming extra bottles at powders sa mesa, madali kang makagamit ng mali!

statements.text: Write the steps in order before you mix or heat anything, so everyone in the group does the exact same investigation!
statements.tl: Isulat nang sunod-sunod ang mga hakbang bago maghalo o magpainit ng anumang bagay, upang pareho ang pagsisiyasat na gagawin ng lahat sa grupo!

statements.text:
What should you write after finishing your steps?

Write your actual findings in plain words using your measurements! Don't just write what you hoped would happen.
statements.tl:
Ano ang isusulat mo pagkatapos ng mga hakbang?

Isulat ang totoong nakita mo gamit ang sukat! Huwag lang isulat kung ano ang inaasahan mong mangyayari.

statements.text:
What makes a finding really good?

A good finding answers the exact problem you wrote at the start! Even if the answer is 'they were the same.'
statements.tl:
Ano ang nagiging magandang pagtuklas?

Ang magandang pagtuklas ay sumasagot sa problemang isinulat mo sa simula! Kahit na ang sagot ay 'pareho lang sila.'

statements.text: Pick a problem you can test with school materials in just one lesson! Don't choose questions that need a giant laboratory.
statements.tl: Pumili ng problemang kayang subukan gamit ang materyales sa paaralan sa isang aralin! Hindi yung kailangan ng malaking laboratoryo.

statements.text:
Where should safety gear go in your plan?

Put safety gear like goggles right in your materials list! Make safety a main step, not just an afterthought.
statements.tl:
Saan dapat ilagay ang safety gear sa plano?

Isama ang safety gear tulad ng goggles sa listahan ng materyales! Gawing hakbang ang kaligtasan, hindi huli.

statements.text: Gather all your materials on a tray first! This way, a missing spoon won't pause your test halfway through.
statements.tl: Tipunin muna sa tray ang lahat ng materyales! Sa ganitong paraan, hindi maaantala sa gitna ang pagsubok dahil sa nawawalang kutsara.

statements.text:
Is your science problem too big to test?

Shrink it! Test two fabrics instead of ten, so the steps still fit the lesson perfectly.
statements.tl:
Masyado bang malaki ang iyong science problem para subukan?

Paikliin ito! Subukan lang dalawang tela imbes na sampu, para kasya pa sa aralin.

statements.text: Put exact amounts on your materials list! Write "100 milliliters of water" so "some water" isn't different each time.
statements.tl: Ilagay ang eksaktong dami sa listahan! Isulat ang "100 milliliters ng tubig" para hindi mag-iba ang "kaunting tubig" bawat pagsubok.

statements.text:
How do you make sure your steps aren't just a guess?

Good steps say exactly how long to wait, how many times to stir, and what to look for!
statements.tl:
Paano mo masisigurado na ang mga hakbang mo ay hindi hulaan?

Ang magagandang hakbang ay nagsasabi kung gaano katagal maghintay, ilang beses maghalo, at ano ang dapat tingnan!

statements.text: A clear problem names what you will compare! Like wet soil versus dry soil, giving your materials and steps a true purpose.
statements.tl: Ang malinaw na tanong ay nagsasabi kung ano ang ihahambing! Tulad ng basang lupa laban sa tuyong lupa, para may saysay ang mga hakbang.

statements.text:
How do you make sure you have all your tools?

Tick each item on your materials list as you set it out, just like a cook checking a recipe, so no tools are missing!
statements.tl:
Paano masisigurado mong kumpleto ang mga gamit mo?

I-tick ang bawat item sa materials list habang inilalagay mo, parang kusinero na nagche-check ng recipe, para walang kulang na gamit!

statements.text: The finding is just what the test showed, not a grade! A careful test can still show your first idea was wrong.
statements.tl: Ang finding ay kung ano ang ipinakita ng test, hindi grade! Kahit maingat na test, maaari pa ring ipakita na mali ang unang idea mo.

statements.text: If you cannot say what you would measure, your problem is not ready yet! Sharpen it first before listing your materials.
statements.tl: Kung hindi mo masabi kung ano ang susukatin mo, hindi pa handa ang problema! Linawin mo muna ito bago mag-list ng materials.

statements.text: We usually measure mass in grams (g) and kilograms (kg)!
statements.tl: Karaniwan nating sinusukat ang masa sa gramo (g) at kilogramo (kg)!

statements.text: Here is a fun fact: One single gram is equal to a whopping 1,000 milligrams!
statements.tl: Narito ang isang masayang katotohanan: Isang buong gramo ay katumbas ng 1,000 miligramo!

statements.text: A thermometer measures temperature, or how hot or cold something is. We read it by checking where the liquid or number reaches in Celsius!
statements.tl: Ang termometro ay sumusukat ng temperatura o kung gaano kainit o kalamig. Binabasa natin ito sa pamamagitan ng pagtingin kung saan umaabot ang likido o numero sa Celsius!

statements.text:
If a 150g dark chocolate bar is 70% cacao, how much cacao is that?

You eat 105 grams of cacao, because 70 percent of 150 grams is 105 grams!
statements.tl:
Kung ang 150g dark chocolate ay 70% cacao, gaano karaming cacao iyon?

Kumakain ka ng 105 grams ng cacao, dahil ang 70 percent ng 150 grams ay 105 grams!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 16_vWKOKw6tJwTeIBBX0bOpOAZmQb2dzt), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A balance measures the mass of lightweight materials in grams, like salt or sugar.
statements.tl: Ang balance ay sumusukat ng mass ng magagaan na materyales gamit ang grams, tulad ng asin o asukal.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1PXxFmIp28lcIhWUQOYMzeZh2qQ2PJZwS), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Heavy materials like cement are measured in kilograms, the unit we use for large amounts of mass.
statements.tl: Ang mabibigat na materyales tulad ng semento ay sinusukat sa kilograms, ang unit na ginagamit natin para sa malalaking dami ng mass.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1RKD0LsDj8bSYsFSxnu8SJ5r-vC71WhKV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Choose milligrams for very light objects, grams for everyday objects, and kilograms for heavy materials, so the number is easy to understand.
statements.tl: Piliin ang milligrams para sa napakagagaan na bagay, grams para sa pang-araw-araw na bagay, at kilograms para sa mabibigat na materyales, para madaling maintindihan ang numero.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1RKD0LsDj8bSYsFSxnu8SJ5r-vC71WhKV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What could happen if we used the wrong units for measurements?

Other scientists would not understand our results! Using the correct unit, like grams for mass, helps everyone compare measurements accurately.
statements.tl:
Ano ang maaaring mangyari kung mali ang unit na ginamit natin sa pagsukat?

Hindi mauunawaan ng ibang scientists ang ating mga resulta! Ang paggamit ng tamang unit, tulad ng grams para sa mass, ay tumutulong sa lahat na maikumpara nang tama ang mga sukat.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1S1H4MnGylVmBVu6oUXBfUgsshI8DQjou), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: To measure the mass of small objects like mongo seeds, place them on a weighing scale and read the pointer carefully to get the value in grams.
statements.tl: Para sukatin ang mass ng maliliit na bagay tulad ng mongo seeds, ilagay ang mga ito sa weighing scale at basahin nang mabuti ang pointer para makuha ang value sa grams.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Ze3xgTqtC755O4IDvL9lZlblXqES9WUs), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: If you dissolve 20 grams of baking soda in 600 grams of water, the percent by mass is about 3.23%, because the solute is a small part of the whole solution.
statements.tl: Kung magtunaw ka ng 20 gramo ng baking soda sa 600 gramo ng tubig, ang percent by mass ay mga 3.23%, dahil maliit na bahagi lamang ng buong solution ang solute.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1ibYBfwesxhuXWubKIs2Jv3CbUpdijEZG), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why must solute and solvent have the same unit before adding?

Because you cannot add grams and kilograms directly! One unit must be converted first so the mass of solution is correct.
statements.tl:
Bakit dapat magkapareho ang unit ng solute at solvent bago pagdagdagin?

Dahil hindi mo maaaring direktang pagdagdagin ang gramo at kilogramo! Kailangang i-convert muna ang isang unit para tama ang mass ng solution.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1ubQhpZzmC4_n-2ZlvCP0JtV59jKQ3MH2), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How do you find the number of moles from a given mass?

Divide the mass in grams by the molar mass in grams per mole, because molar mass tells you how many grams one mole weighs.
statements.tl:
Paano mo makukuha ang bilang ng moles mula sa binigay na mass?

I-divide ang mass sa grams sa molar mass sa grams per mole, dahil sinasabi ng molar mass kung ilang grams ang bigat ng isang mole.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1brcFRgQfC-AXvdgp7wTDwJD1TO0jDVXb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What's the biggest fruit that grows on a tree?

It's the jackfruit! This giant fruit that grows on trees can weigh up to about 55 kilograms.
statements.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking prutas sa puno?

Ang langka! Itong higanteng prutas na tumutubo sa puno ay maaaring tumimbang ng hanggang 55 kilo.

statements.text:
How heavy can a jackfruit get?

A single jackfruit can weigh up to about 50 kilograms — as heavy as a young child!
statements.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang pinakamalaking langka?

Ang isang langka ay maaaring tumimbang ng hanggang 50 kilo — kasinbigat ng isang batang tao!

statements.text: A single jackfruit can weigh more than 30 kilograms and grow as long as a person's arm!
statements.tl: Ang isang langka ay maaaring tumimbang ng higit sa 30 kilo at lumaking kasinghaba ng braso ng tao!
statements.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica; FAO crop references; encyclopedia-stable

statements.text: Most vaccines must stay between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius to work — the 'cold chain' is the system of fridges and cool containers keeping them right from factory to clinic!
statements.tl: Kailangang itago ang karamihan ng bakuna sa 2-8°C para gumana ito — ang 'cold chain' ang sistema ng mga refrigerator at insulated na sisidlan na nagpapanatili ng tamang temperatura mula sa paggawa hanggang gamitin!
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable; WHO; DOH Philippines; NRC LS1.C; PH context

statements.text:
How heavy can the biggest bat get?

The giant golden-crowned flying fox can weigh up to 1.4 kilograms, making it one of the heaviest bats in the world!
statements.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang pinakamalaking paniki?

Ang giant golden-crowned flying fox ay umaabot ng 1.4 kilo ang bigat, kaya isa ito sa pinakamabigat na paniki sa mundo!

statements.text:
How tiny is the Etruscan shrew?

It weighs about as much as a small coin -- only around two grams!
statements.tl:
Gaano kaliit ang Etruscan shrew?

Ang timbang niya ay halos kasinggaan lang ng isang maliit na barya -- mga dalawang gramo lang!

statements.text:
How do we measure the mass of an object?

We use a special balance to measure the mass of an object!
statements.tl:
Paano natin sinusukat ang masa ng isang bagay?

Ginagamit natin ang isang balance o timbangan upang sukatin ang masa ng isang bagay!

statements.text: Taring means setting the balance to zero with the empty container on it, so only the liquid gets weighed.
statements.tl: Ang taring ay pag-set ng balance sa zero habang nasa ibabaw na ang walang-laman na container, para ang liquid lang ang matimbang.

statements.text: When reading a laboratory thermometer, keep it upright and your eyes level with the top of the liquid inside the glass tube to get an accurate temperature reading.
statements.tl: Kapag nagbabasa ng laboratory thermometer, panatilihin itong patayo at ang iyong mga mata ay naka-level sa tuktok ng liquid sa loob ng glass tube upang makakuha ng tamang temperature reading.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 18JhqAzYFZar9YfM9vODOjZCyyRtDDKnP), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Mass is the amount of matter in an object, and we measure it with a balance or weighing scale.
statements.tl: Ang mass ay ang dami ng matter sa isang bagay, at sinusukat natin ito gamit ang balance o weighing scale.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1RKD0LsDj8bSYsFSxnu8SJ5r-vC71WhKV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: When measuring water temperature, submerge the thermometer without touching the bottom of the glass so it reads only the water.
statements.tl: Kapag sinusukat ang temperatura ng tubig, ilubog ang thermometer nang hindi sumasayad sa ilalim ng baso para mabasa lamang nito ang tubig.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1RKD0LsDj8bSYsFSxnu8SJ5r-vC71WhKV), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What is a triple-beam balance?

It is a mechanical balance with three beams and sliding weights that you move until the object and the weights are balanced!
statements.tl:
Ano ang triple-beam balance?

Ito ay isang mechanical balance na may tatlong beams at sliding weights na ginagalaw mo hanggang mag-balance ang bagay at ang mga weights!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1aM3wMlrxKITYVpGo1SlU8jHV3DHz-gGA), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A balance or scale is the science tool used to measure mass, which is the amount of matter packed inside an object.
statements.tl: Ang balance o scale ang gamit sa science para sukatin ang mass, o ang dami ng matter na nasa loob ng isang bagay.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1jOXO0cQbVUyviIIyPm7bTQceT06l6T9j), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: An analytical balance is a very precise scale that measures tiny differences in mass, so it is used when a measurement must be exact.
statements.tl: Ang analytical balance ay isang napaka-precise na scale na sumusukat ng maliliit na pagkakaiba sa mass, kaya ginagamit ito kapag kailangang eksakto ang sukat.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1jOXO0cQbVUyviIIyPm7bTQceT06l6T9j), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why can't we use just one tool for every measurement?

Different samples need different tools. A thermometer measures temperature, while a balance measures mass, so you must choose the tool that matches what you are testing!
statements.tl:
Bakit hindi puwedeng isang tool lang ang gamitin sa lahat ng sukat?

Iba-ibang sample ang nangangailangan ng iba-ibang tool. Ang thermometer ay sumusukat ng temperature, habang ang balance ay sumusukat ng mass, kaya dapat piliin mo ang tool na tugma sa iyong sinusuri!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1jOXO0cQbVUyviIIyPm7bTQceT06l6T9j), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A thermometer is a science tool used to measure temperature in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit during experiments.
statements.tl: Ang thermometer ay isang science tool na ginagamit upang sukatin ang temperatura sa degrees Celsius o Fahrenheit habang nag-eeksperimento.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1ubQhpZzmC4_n-2ZlvCP0JtV59jKQ3MH2), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Can your fingers always tell if something is hot or cold?

No! Your senses can be fooled. If one hand was in cold water and the other in warm water, the same tap water feels different to each hand. That is why we use a thermometer.
statements.tl:
Laging tama ba ang iyong mga daliri sa pagsasabi kung mainit o malamig ang isang bagay?

Hindi! Maaaring maloko ang iyong pandama. Kung ang isang kamay ay galing sa malamig na tubig at ang isa ay sa maligamgam, magkaiba ang pakiramdam ng parehong tubig sa gripo sa bawat kamay. Kaya gumagamit tayo ng thermometer.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1v1glf3pwWU2zvI-172ShWMosHIxTodTt), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Before using a double-pan balance, make sure the pans are empty, set both riders to zero, and turn the adjustment knob until the pointer reads zero.
statements.tl: Bago gamitin ang double-pan balance, siguraduhing walang laman ang mga pan, ilagay ang parehong riders sa zero, at i-turn ang adjustment knob hanggang ang pointer ay magbasa ng zero.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1yAIpM18HwjcTfD-BRQ6KJsClukbz2yLu), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What are two common types of thermometers?

Some thermometers are digital and show a number on a screen, while others use a rising liquid.
statements.tl:
Ano ang dalawang karaniwang uri ng termometro?

May digital na termometro na nagpapakita ng numero sa screen, at may termometrong gumagamit ng umaakyat na likido.

statements.text:
How can you prove mass stays the same after a change?

Weigh everything before and after inside a sealed container — the weight stays exactly the same!
statements.tl:
Paano mo mapapatunayan na pareho pa rin ang masa pagkatapos ng pagbabago?

Timbangin ang lahat bago at pagkatapos sa loob ng selyadong sisidlan — pareho pa rin ang timbang!

statements.text:
How do we find out an object's mass?

We use a balance to measure mass by comparing the object against known masses!
statements.tl:
Paano natin malalaman ang masa ng isang bagay?

Ginagamit natin ang isang timbangan para sukatin ang masa sa pamamagitan ng paghahambing nito sa mga bagay na alam ang masa!

statements.text:
What instrument do we use to measure temperature?
