statements.tl: Ang Pluto ay isang dwarf planet dahil hindi nito nalinis ang orbit nito! Kaya noong 2006, hindi na ito kabilang sa walong planeta.

statements.text: A meteoroid is a cool rock floating in space that has not yet entered Earth's atmosphere!
statements.tl: Ang meteoroid ay isang bato sa kalawakan na hindi pa pumapasok sa atmospera ng Earth!

statements.text: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and is also considered a dwarf planet!
statements.tl: Ang Ceres ang pinakamalaking bagay sa asteroid belt at itinuturing ding isang dwarf planet!

statements.text: Scientists study asteroids and comets because they barely changed in billions of years, acting like "fossils" that preserve our solar system's formation history!
statements.tl: Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang mga asteroid at kometa dahil halos hindi sila nagbago sa loob ng bilyong taon, parang mga "fossil" ng solar system!
statements.source: NRC ESS1.C (asteroids and meteorites have changed little over billions of years)

statements.text: In the early solar system, microscopic dust and ice collided and stuck together to form planetesimals in a process called accretion!
statements.tl: Sa maagang solar system, nagbanggaan at dumikit ang napakaliit na alikabok at yelo para bumuo ng mga planetesimal sa prosesong tinatawag na accretion!

statements.text: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) classifies solar system objects that are neither planets nor moons into two groups: small solar system bodies and dwarf planets.
statements.tl: Ayon sa International Astronomical Union (IAU), ang mga bagay sa solar system na hindi planeta o buwan ay nahahati sa dalawang grupo: small solar system bodies at dwarf planets.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 14k_x-UuWQTZInxFM5PyhXC1Z0C6tsaH7), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Comets are icy bodies made of dust, rock, frozen water, methane, and ammonia.
statements.tl: Ang mga kometa ay mga nagyeyelong bagay na gawa sa alikabok, bato, frozen water, methane, at ammonia.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 14k_x-UuWQTZInxFM5PyhXC1Z0C6tsaH7), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Other asteroids are scattered throughout the solar system, possibly thrown out of the asteroid belt by Jupiter's gravity.
statements.tl: Ang ibang mga asteroid ay nakakalat sa buong solar system, posibleng itinapon palabas ng asteroid belt ng gravity ng Jupiter.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 14k_x-UuWQTZInxFM5PyhXC1Z0C6tsaH7), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Asteroids are composed mainly of silicate rock and metals such as iron and nickel.
statements.tl: Ang mga asteroid ay pangunahing binubuo ng batong silicate at mga metal tulad ng bakal at nickel.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1hvK3KZUGBy-bNBaW3hzrp6nkhtOldi3a), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Meteoroids are fragments of asteroids and comets, often created when asteroids collide with each other.
statements.tl: Ang mga meteoroid ay mga piraso ng asteroid at kometa, na kadalasang nabubuo kapag nagbanggaan ang mga asteroid.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1hvK3KZUGBy-bNBaW3hzrp6nkhtOldi3a), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Comet orbits are highly elliptical, while asteroid orbits are more rounded and less elliptical.
statements.tl: Ang orbit ng kometa ay napakahaba at elliptical, habang ang orbit ng asteroid ay mas bilugan at hindi gaanong elliptical.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1hvK3KZUGBy-bNBaW3hzrp6nkhtOldi3a), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why do some meteor showers happen at the exact same time every year?

It's because Earth passes through the same comet-debris path during each orbit!
statements.tl:
Bakit nangyayari ang ilang meteor shower sa parehong panahon kada taon?

Dahil dumaraan ang Mundo sa parehong landas ng labi ng kometa sa bawat orbit!

statements.text:
Where do meteor showers like the Perseids and Leonids come from?

Meteor showers happen when Earth passes through a comet's debris trail! The Perseids in August come from Comet Swift-Tuttle, and the Leonids in November come from Comet Tempel-Tuttle.
statements.tl:
Saan nagmumula ang mga meteor shower tulad ng Perseids at Leonids?

Meteor shower ay nangyayari kapag dumadaan ang Earth sa debris trail ng kometa! Ang Perseids tuwing Agosto ay mula sa Comet Swift-Tuttle, at ang Leonids tuwing Nobyembre ay mula sa Comet Tempel-Tuttle.

statements.text: Many annual showers are visible from the Philippines! Some northern radiants sit lower, but a local astronomy club table is a super useful source.
statements.tl: Maraming taunang shower ang nakikita mula sa Pilipinas! Mas mababa ang ilang northern radiants, pero ang table ng lokal na astronomy club ay napaka-useful na source.

statements.text: Meteor showers happen around the same time every year! Earth passes through the same dust trails left by comets or asteroids annually, so astronomers know when to expect the Perseids and Geminids.
statements.tl: Ang mga meteor shower ay nangyayari sa halos parehong oras bawat taon! Dumadaan ang Earth sa parehong mga bakas ng alikabok na iniwan ng kometa o asteroid, kaya alam ng mga astronomo kung kailan ang Perseids at Geminids.

statements.text: Look up at the sky! The Perseid meteor shower happens every August each year.
statements.tl: Tumingala ka sa langit! Ang Perseid meteor shower (ulan ng bulalakaw) ay nangyayari tuwing Agosto bawat taon.

statements.text: When Earth passes through comet Swift-Tuttle's dusty trail, tiny space particles burn up in our atmosphere and create the Perseid meteor shower!
statements.tl: Kapag dumaan ang Earth sa alikabok na bakas ng comet na Swift-Tuttle, nasusunog ang maliliit na space particles sa atmospera natin, kaya lumilikha ng Perseid meteor shower!

statements.text:
Why do meteor showers happen at the same time every year?

Earth passes through a trail of dust left by a comet! As the dust particles burn up in the atmosphere each year, we see a meteor shower!
statements.tl:
Bakit nangyayari ang ulan ng bulalakaw sa parehong panahon taun-taon?

Dumadaan ang Earth sa landas ng alikabok na naiwan ng kometa! Habang nasusunog ang mga butil sa himpapawid taun-taon, nakikita natin ang meteor shower!

statements.text: A meteor shower gets its name from the constellation that holds its radiant. That name stays the same year after year as Earth crosses the stream again.
statements.tl: Ang isang meteor shower ay pinangalanan sa constellation na kinaroroonan ng radiant nito. Ang pangalang iyon ay nananatiling pareho taon-taon habang tinatawid muli ng Earth ang stream.

statements.text: Many annual meteor showers come from a parent comet that still sheds dust along its orbit. Earth meets that dust on a schedule set by both orbits.
statements.tl: Maraming taunang meteor shower ay galing sa isang parent comet na nag-iiwan pa rin ng alikabok sa orbit nito. Nakakasalubong ng Earth ang alikabok na iyon sa oras na nakatakda ng dalawang orbit.

statements.text: The Geminids are a regular December shower whose parent is an asteroid-like body. This shows that not every annual stream comes from a classic comet.
statements.tl: Ang Geminids ay regular na meteor shower tuwing Disyembre na ang pinagmulan ay parang asteroid. Nagpapakita ito na hindi lahat ng taunang stream ay galing sa karaniwang comet.

statements.text: The Quadrantid meteor shower is a regular early-January event. It is another calendar marker listed in yearly meteor-shower tables.
statements.tl: Ang Quadrantid meteor shower ay regular na kaganapan tuwing unang bahagi ng Enero. Ito ay isa pang pananda sa kalendaryo na nakasulat sa taunang listahan ng mga meteor shower.

statements.text: A meteor shower has a peak night and a wider season. Reliable tables list both, so 'regular' does not mean only a single hour each year.
statements.tl: Ang isang meteor shower ay may pinakamalakas na gabi at mas mahabang panahon. Pareho itong nakasulat sa maaasahang listahan, kaya ang 'regular' ay hindi ibig sabihin na isang oras lang bawat taon.

statements.text:
Are all shooting stars the same?

Nope! Random sporadic meteors can appear any night. But a shower is the regular, clustered burst when Earth hits a known dust stream.
statements.tl:
Lahat ba ng shooting stars ay pareho?

Hindi! Ang mga random na sporadic meteor ay maaaring lumitaw kahit anong gabi. Pero ang shower ay ang regular at magkakasamang paglitaw ng mga meteor kapag tumama ang Earth sa kilalang stream ng alikabok.

statements.text: Earth's year-long trip around the Sun is the clock. The same stretch of orbit is where a given shower's dust is waiting each year.
statements.tl: Ang isang taong paglalakbay ng Earth sa paligid ng Araw ang nagsisilbing orasan. Ang parehong bahagi ng orbit ay kung saan naghihintay ang alikabok ng isang shower bawat taon.

statements.text:
Does a bright Moon cancel the meteor shower?

Nope! The shower still arrives on schedule. A bright Moon just hides many meteors from our eyes — the regularity is about the stream, not how many you see.
statements.tl:
Kinakansela ba ng maliwanag na Buwan ang meteor shower?

Hindi! Dumadating pa rin ang shower sa takdang oras. Itinatago lang ng maliwanag na Buwan ang maraming meteor — ang regularity ay tungkol sa stream, hindi sa kung ilan ang nakikita mo.

statements.text: The Lyrids are a regular April shower tied to comet Thatcher, listed on sky calendars alongside the famous Perseids.
statements.tl: Ang Lyrids ay isang regular na April shower na konektado sa comet Thatcher, nakalista sa sky calendar kasama ng sikat na Perseids.

statements.text:
Where do the October Orionids come from?

They return each October from the dust of comet Halley — a regular shower from a parent comet famous in other years too!
statements.tl:
Saan nagmula ang October Orionids?

Bumabalik sila tuwing Oktubre mula sa alikabok ng comet Halley — isang regular na shower mula sa parent comet na sikat din sa ibang taon!

statements.text: The Eta Aquariids are a regular May shower also linked to comet Halley — proving one comet trail can create more than one annual meeting!
statements.tl: Ang Eta Aquariids ay isang regular na May shower na konektado rin sa comet Halley — patunay na ang isang comet trail ay kayang gumawa ng higit sa isang taunang pagkikita!

statements.text: The Cassini probe went on an epic space journey to explore the planet Saturn and its rings!
statements.tl: Naglayag ang Cassini probe sa isang epikong byahe sa kalawakan upang galugarin ang planetang Saturn at ang mga singsing nito!

statements.text: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits above Earth's atmosphere, so it can see space super clearly!
statements.tl: Ang Hubble Space Telescope ay umiikot sa itaas ng atmosphere ng Earth, kaya super malinaw nitong nakikita ang kalawakan!

statements.text: Infrared telescopes detect heat radiation from objects in space, allowing astronomers to see things that are too cool or too dusty for ordinary telescopes.
statements.tl: Nadedetect ng infrared telescopes ang heat radiation mula sa mga bagay sa kalawakan, kaya nakikita ng mga astronomer ang mga bagay na masyadong malamig o masyadong maalikabok para sa ordinaryong mga telescope.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 155iY1mMJh_jPmfUWC7IPFdT-7MGY91jk), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Do only humans make radio waves?

Nope! Stars, galaxies, and the Sun naturally give off radio waves. Astronomers use giant radio telescopes to listen to them and explore distant space!
statements.tl:
Tao lang ba ang gumagawa ng radio waves?

Hindi! Ang mga bituin, galaksiya, at Araw ay natural na naglalabas ng radio waves. Ginagamit ng mga astronomo ang malalaking radio telescope para pakinggan at aralin ang kalawakan!

statements.text:
How do astronomers see deep into the universe?

The Hubble Space Telescope uses large mirrors to collect faint visible light from distant galaxies!
statements.tl:
Paano nakikita ng mga astronomer ang malalim na kalawakan?

Gumagamit ang Hubble Space Telescope ng malalaking salamin para mangolekta ng mahinang visible light mula sa malalayong galaxy!

statements.text:
How do scientists see the invisible universe?

They use different telescopes, like radio and X-ray telescopes, to detect spectrum parts our eyes can't see, learning more about space!
statements.tl:
Paano nakikita ng mga siyentipiko ang di-nakikitang uniberso?

Gumagamit sila ng iba't ibang teleskopyo, tulad ng radio at X-ray telescope, para makita ang spectrum na hindi nakikita ng mata, at mas matuto tungkol sa kalawakan!

statements.text:
Why is the James Webb Space Telescope hard to repair?

Unlike the close Hubble, James Webb sits 1.5 million kilometers away—farther than the Moon! This huge distance makes it very hard to repair if it breaks.
statements.tl:
Bakit mahirap ayusin ang James Webb Space Telescope?

Hindi tulad ng malapit na Hubble, ang James Webb ay nasa layong 1.5 milyong kilometro—mas malayo pa sa Buwan! Kaya napakahirap nitong ayusin kung masira.
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable consensus (NASA JWST orbits Sun-Earth L2, ~1.5 million km)

statements.text:
Why did astronauts have to fix the Hubble telescope in space?

When Hubble first reached space, its pictures were blurry because of a flaw in its mirror! So, astronauts went out into space to fix it.
statements.tl:
Bakit kailangang ayusin ng mga astronaut ang Hubble telescope sa space?

Nang unang umabot ang Hubble sa space, malabo ang mga larawan nito dahil sa flaw sa mirror! Kaya lumabas ang mga astronaut sa space para ayusin ito.

statements.text: Distant stars are so far that the light seen through a telescope left them years to millions of years ago, meaning we are looking into the past!
statements.tl: Napakalayo ng ibang bituin kaya ang light na nakikita sa telescope ay umalis ilang taon hanggang milyong taon na ang nakakalipas—tayo ay nakatingin sa nakaraan!
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable consensus (light travel time / look-back time)

statements.text: To see faint star light, the James Webb telescope must stay extremely cold, so it uses a giant shield to block the Sun's heat!
statements.tl: Para makita ang mahinang light ng mga bituin, kailangang manatiling napakalamig ng James Webb telescope, kaya may giant shield itong pumipigil sa init ng Araw!
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable consensus (JWST five-layer sunshield, cold infrared operation)

statements.text: We sent robotic spacecraft to fly close and study asteroids and comets! Some missions even collected tiny samples and brought them back to Earth for scientists to examine.
statements.tl: Nagpadala na tayo ng mga robotic spacecraft para pag-aralan ang mga asteroid at kometa! May mga misyon na kumuha pa ng maliliit na sampol at ibinalik sa Earth para suriin ng mga siyentista.

statements.text: Scientists use telescopes to watch asteroids near Earth's path! They calculate their routes ahead of time to make sure our planet is safe and to see if any action is needed.
statements.tl: Gumagamit ang mga siyentista ng mga teleskopyo para bantayan ang mga asteroid malapit sa Earth! Kinakalkula nila ang mga landas nang maaga para masigurong ligtas ang ating planeta at kung kailangan ng aksyon.

statements.text: Using powerful telescopes like Hubble, scientists can spot galaxies that are extremely far away!
statements.tl: Gamit ang makapangyarihang teleskopyo tulad ng Hubble, nakikita ng mga siyentipiko ang napakalayong galaksiya!

statements.text:
What is a space probe and why do we use it?

It is a robotic craft with no people aboard! We send it to faraway planets that are too dangerous for astronauts.
statements.tl:
Ano ang space probe at bakit natin ito ginagamit?

Ito ay isang robotikong sasakyan na walang sakay na tao! Ipinapadala ito sa malalayong planeta na delikado para sa astronaut.

statements.text:
Why are telescopes like Hubble placed in space?

To get clearer pictures! There is no atmosphere up there to blur the view.
statements.tl:
Bakit inilalagay sa kalawakan ang mga teleskopyo tulad ng Hubble?

Para makakuha ng mas malinaw na larawan! Walang atmospera doon na nakakalabo sa tanaw.

statements.text:
What kind of light does the James Webb Space Telescope see?

It sees infrared, a kind of heat light, letting it view extremely distant and very old galaxies!
statements.tl:
Anong uri ng liwanag ang nakikita ng James Webb Space Telescope?

Nakakakita ito ng infrared, isang uri ng liwanag na init, kaya nakikita nito ang napakalayo at sinaunang galaksiya!

statements.text:
Why is looking through a telescope like looking back in time?

When we look at a very distant star, we see its old light, so we are really looking back in time!
statements.tl:
Bakit parang tumitingin sa nakaraan kapag gumagamit ng teleskopyo?

Kapag tumitingin tayo sa napakalayong bituin, nakikita natin ang luma nitong liwanag, kaya parang tumitingin tayo sa nakaraan!

statements.text: A telescope reveals way more stars and galaxies than your eyes can see! It gathers faint light from distant objects to show you the hidden universe.
statements.tl: Ang teleskopyo ay nagpapakita ng mas maraming bituin at galaxy kaysa sa nakikita ng mata! Tinitipon nito ang mahinang liwanag mula sa malalayong bagay.

statements.text: Genetic diversity helps a species adapt to change and resist disease — when a small population loses much of it, the species becomes more fragile.
statements.tl: Ang genetic diversity ay nagbibigay sa isang species ng kakayahang mag-angkop sa mga pagbabago at labanan ang mga sakit — kapag nawalan ng marami nito ang isang maliit na populasyon, nagiging mas marupok ang species.

statements.text:
Why is an ecosystem with many species tougher?

When many different species do the same job — like many kinds of insects that pollinate flowers — there's a backup if one disappears. That's why ecosystems with many species are more stable than ones with only a few!
statements.tl:
Bakit mas matatag ang ekosistemang maraming species?

Kapag maraming iba't ibang species ang may parehong trabaho — tulad ng maraming uri ng insektong pollinator — may backup kapag nawala ang isa. Kaya mas matatag ang ekosistemang maraming species kaysa sa iilan lang!

statements.text: A wildlife corridor is a strip of connected habitat that lets animals move between separated forests, helping keep their genetic diversity healthy.
statements.tl: Ang wildlife corridor ay pagdurugtong ng mga kagubatan na nagbibigay-daan sa mga hayop na makakilos sa magkahiwalay na tirahan, tumutulong ito sa kanilang genetic diversity.

statements.text: Species diversity is the variety of different species living in a particular area, like how a coral reef has fish, corals, and sea turtles all together.
statements.tl: Ang species diversity ay ang iba't ibang uri ng species na naninirahan sa isang partikular na lugar, tulad ng coral reef na may isda, corals, at pawikan na magkakasama.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17pRCRb7sVjySGKba39tFdhJGX9UdpEGE), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: High biodiversity means many different species live in one place, so when hard times come, some will likely survive and keep the ecosystem going.
statements.tl: Ang high biodiversity ay nangangahulugang maraming iba't ibang species ang naninirahan sa isang lugar, kaya kapag dumating ang mahihirap na panahon, may ilang makaliligtas at magpapatuloy sa ecosystem.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1MqADgmQoYOF9vyF2Y8ZQizf3zKNbnJev), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Biodiversity is the variety of life on Earth, including all its different forms and all the ways living things interact with each other.
statements.tl: Ang biodiversity ay ang pagkakaiba-iba ng buhay sa mundo, kasama ang lahat ng iba't ibang anyo nito at ang lahat ng paraan ng pakikipag-ugnayan ng mga nabubuhay na bagay sa isa't isa.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1N6EWjU_XOp-qfjwOKupwGbFwxvWcIcgi), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
If two communities both have 50 individuals and 5 species, can one be more diverse?

Yes! Community A with 10 individuals per species has greater evenness, while Community B with 20, 10, 10, 6, and 4 individuals has greater variation in dominance.
statements.tl:
Kung ang dalawang komunidad ay parehong may 50 indibidwal at 5 species, maaari bang mas diverse ang isa?

Oo! Ang Community A na may 10 indibidwal bawat species ay may mas mataas na evenness, habang ang Community B na may 20, 10, 10, 6, at 4 na indibidwal ay may mas malaking variation sa dominance.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1dBQpOszdgrtdRnSc3og-fPATCM_Xi_Ur), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why is an ecosystem with high biodiversity better off?

With many different species, there are more food sources and helpers, so the ecosystem can survive changes and disasters more easily!
statements.tl:
Bakit mas nakakalamang ang ecosystem na may mataas na biodiversity?

Dahil maraming iba't ibang species, mas maraming pagkukunan ng pagkain at katulong, kaya mas madaling makakaya ng ecosystem ang mga pagbabago at sakuna!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1gKpH1xKg4DCvSCVOFe8UEKo_k2WZs3km), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: An ecosystem with low biodiversity contains fewer species, making it more fragile because the loss of even one species can have a big impact.
statements.tl: Ang isang ecosystem na may mababang biodiversity ay naglalaman ng mas kaunting species, kaya mas marupok ito dahil ang pagkawala ng kahit isang species ay maaaring magdulot ng malaking epekto.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1gKpH1xKg4DCvSCVOFe8UEKo_k2WZs3km), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Biodiversity means the variety of living things in a place. The more varied the life, the more stable and healthy the ecosystem -- and the Philippines is one of the richest countries for it!
statements.tl: Ang biodiversity ay ang dami at pagkakaiba-iba ng mga buhay na bagay sa isang lugar. Mas magkakaiba ang buhay, mas matatag at malusog ang kapaligiran -- at isa ang Pilipinas sa pinakamayaman dito!

statements.text: It's a myth that nothing happens when one species disappears. The effect is often slow — things seem fine at first, then the balance suddenly collapses later.
statements.tl: Mali ang akalang walang mangyayari kapag naglaho ang isang species. Kadalasan mabagal ang epekto — tahimik muna ito, pero pagkaraan ng ilang panahon biglang gumuguho ang balanse.

statements.text:
Why is a mixed forest healthier?

A forest is healthier when many kinds of trees grow together, not just one kind like ipil-ipil.
statements.tl:
Bakit mas malusog ang halo-halong gubat?

Mas malusog ang gubat kapag halo-halong uri ng puno ang tumutubo, hindi lang isang klase tulad ng ipil-ipil.
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable; biodiversity vs monoculture reforestation references

statements.text: The Philippines is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots — home to a huge variety of plants and animals!
statements.tl: Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa mga biodiversity hotspot sa mundo — tahanan ng napakaraming iba't ibang halaman at hayop!

statements.text:
Why is having many animal species important?

Every animal has a role in nature -- some eat insects, some spread plant seeds. When there are many kinds and they're all connected, nature stays balanced and healthy.
statements.tl:
Bakit mahalaga ang maraming uri ng hayop?

Bawat hayop ay may papel sa kalikasan -- may kumakain ng insekto, may nagkakalat ng buto ng halaman. Kapag marami at magkakaugnay sila, mas balanse at malusog ang kalikasan.

statements.text: Ecosystems with more kinds of species and more connected food webs recover better from disturbances than ecosystems with only a few species.
statements.tl: Ang mga ekosistema na may mas maraming species at magkakaugnay na food web ay mas matibay at mas mabilis makabawi mula sa mga kaguluhan.

statements.text: In a diverse ecosystem, some species handle heat while others handle cold. So when the climate shifts, at least some of them survive!
statements.tl: Sa isang diverse ecosystem, kaya ng iba ang init at ng iba ang lamig. Kaya kapag nagbago ang klima, may ilan pa ring nabubuhay!

statements.text: The Philippines grows many rice varieties! If a new disease attacks one type, other resistant types can still produce grain for a safe harvest.
statements.tl: Maraming uri ng palay ang itinatanim sa Pilipinas! Kung atakihin ng bagong sakit ang isang uri, ang ibang uri na may resistensya ay maaari pa ring magbigay ng butil para anihin.

statements.text:
How do decomposers keep our soil rich?

Many kinds of decomposers, like different fungi and bacteria, break down dead leaves! If one dies out, the others keep the soil rich.
statements.tl:
Paano pinapanatili ng mga decomposer ang pagiging mayaman ng lupa?

Maraming uri ng decomposer, tulad ng fungi at bacteria, ang sumisira sa patay na dahon! Kung mawala ang isa, pinananatili pa rin ng iba na mayaman ang lupa.

statements.text:
What shape is DNA?

DNA is shaped like a twisted ladder — scientists call it a 'double helix'!
statements.tl:
Anong hugis ang DNA?

Ang DNA ay hugis pilipit na hagdan — tinatawag itong 'double helix'!

statements.text:
How many building blocks make up DNA?

DNA is built from just four bases: adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine — A, T, G, and C!
statements.tl:
Ilang uri ng base ang bumubuo sa DNA?

Binubuo ang DNA ng apat na base lamang: adenine, thymine, guanine, at cytosine — A, T, G, at C!

statements.text: The two sides of the DNA ladder are a sugar-phosphate backbone, made of alternating deoxyribose sugar and phosphate groups linked together.
statements.tl: Ang dalawang gilid ng DNA ladder ay sugar-phosphate backbone, gawa sa salit-salit na deoxyribose sugar at phosphate group na magkakadugtong.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 12xUWs5HUkWVojo9AmQ-jLobs7WCHSTz3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: DNA is a double-stranded molecule shaped like a twisted ladder, with a sugar called deoxyribose and the bases A, T, C, and G.
statements.tl: Ang DNA ay double-stranded na molecule na hugis twisted ladder, na may asukal na tinatawag na deoxyribose at mga base na A, T, C, at G.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1ecolMd0gHbBoHdEs9FdWah3RAKXThzmO), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: DNA has four bases: adenine and guanine are double-ring purines, while cytosine and thymine are single-ring pyrimidines.
statements.tl: May apat na bases ang DNA: ang adenine at guanine ay double-ring purines, habang ang cytosine at thymine ay single-ring pyrimidines.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-17288), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What shape is DNA?

A twisted ladder called a double helix! Two long strands are joined together by rungs, like a spiral staircase.
statements.tl:
Anong hugis ang DNA?

Parang pilipit na hagdan na tinatawag na double helix! May dalawang mahabang strand na pinagdugtong ng mga baitang.

statements.text:
What shape is DNA?

DNA is shaped like a double helix — imagine a ladder that's been twisted round and round!
statements.tl:
Anong hugis ang DNA?

Ang DNA ay may hugis na double helix — parang pilipit na hagdan!

statements.text:
Do all living things share the same kind of DNA?

Yes — from humans and animals to plants and the tiniest bacteria, every living thing shares the same double helix DNA shape, showing all life on Earth is connected.
statements.tl:
May pare-parehong DNA ba ang lahat ng buhay?

Oo — mula sa tao, hayop, halaman, hanggang sa pinakamaliit na bacteria, magkapareho ang hugis ng double helix DNA ng lahat. Ipinapakita nitong konektado ang lahat ng buhay sa Earth.

statements.text:
Which letter always pairs with A in DNA?

There's a pairing rule: A always goes with T, and G always goes with C — so if you know one DNA strand, you can already guess the other.
statements.tl:
Anong letra ang laging kasama ng A sa DNA?

May patakaran sa pagpapares: ang A ay laging kasama ng T, at ang G ay laging kasama ng C — kaya kung alam mo ang isang strand, mahuhulaan mo na ang isa.

statements.text: The two DNA strands are held by weak hydrogen bonds between paired bases, so the ladder can unzip when the cell copies it!
statements.tl: Ang dalawang hibla ng DNA ay pinagdikit ng mahihinang hydrogen bonds sa pagitan ng magkapares na bases, kaya nabubuksan na parang zipper kapag kinokopya ng cell!

statements.text: In the DNA double helix, the sugar-phosphate backbones run along the outside, while the paired bases form the rungs on the inside!
statements.tl: Sa double helix ng DNA, ang sugar-phosphate backbones ay nasa labas, habang ang magkapares na bases ang bumubuo sa mga baitang sa loob!

statements.text: The two strands of DNA run in opposite directions! One goes upward while the other goes downward along the twisted ladder.
statements.tl: Ang dalawang hibla ng DNA ay tumatakbo sa magkasalungat na direksyon! Ang isa ay paakyat habang ang isa ay pababa sa paikot na hagdan.

statements.text: A DNA double helix is only about 2 nanometers wide! About 25,000 of them side by side would fit across a human hair.
statements.tl: Ang double helix ng DNA ay halos 2 nanometers lang ang lapad! Mga 25,000 nito na magkakatabi ang kasya sa isang hibla ng buhok ng tao.

statements.text: Each full turn of the DNA helix is about 3.4 nanometers long and holds about 10 base pairs, like ten steps on a spiral staircase!
statements.tl: Ang bawat buong ikot ng DNA helix ay mga 3.4 nanometers ang haba at may hawak na mga 10 base pairs, parang sampung baitang sa spiral staircase!

statements.text:
How does long DNA fit inside a tiny nucleus?

It wraps around proteins called histones, just like thread winding around tiny spools to stay tidy!
statements.tl:
Paano kasya ang mahabang DNA sa loob ng maliit na nucleus?

Bumabalot ito sa mga protina na tinatawag na histones, parang sinulid na umiikot sa maliliit na spool para manatiling maayos!

statements.text: The order of bases A, T, C, and G along the DNA strand is the code carrying instructions to build your body!
statements.tl: Ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng bases na A, T, C, at G sa DNA strand ay ang code na nagdadala ng instructions para buuin ang katawan mo!

statements.text:
How does DNA build an exact copy of its partner strand?

Since each base has only one perfect partner, each strand acts as a template to build the other exactly!
statements.tl:
Paano gumagawa ang DNA ng eksaktong kopya ng kabilang strand?

Dahil may iisang perpektong kapareha ang bawat base, nagsisilbing template ang bawat strand para buuin nang eksakto ang kabilang strand!

statements.text: The DNA double helix works like a zipper! The bases are the matching teeth, and the backbones are the two tapes.
statements.tl: Ang DNA double helix ay gumagana parang zipper! Ang mga bases ang nagtatagpung mga ngipin, at ang backbones ang dalawang tela.

statements.text:
What ions make up potassium chloride?

Potassium chloride (KCl) is made of potassium (+1) and chloride (-1) ions in a one-to-one ratio!
statements.tl:
Anong ions ang bumubuo ng potassium chloride?

Ang potassium chloride (KCl) ay gawa sa potassium (+1) at chloride (-1) ions sa tig-iisang dami!

statements.text:
What does the formula MgCl2 mean?

It tells you there is one magnesium ion and two chloride ions in the compound!
statements.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng formula na MgCl2?

Sinasabi nito na may isang magnesium ion at dalawang chloride ions sa compound!

statements.text: Magnesium oxide, MgO, forms when magnesium loses two electrons to become Mg2+ and oxygen gains two electrons to become O2-.
statements.tl: Ang magnesium oxide, MgO, ay nabubuo kapag ang magnesium ay naglalabas ng dalawang electrons para maging Mg2+ at ang oxygen ay kumukuha ng dalawang electrons para maging O2-.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1b5kT2v5ORLqOFueiZcRdl--l0-rS2JKp), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A formula unit shows the lowest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound, like NaCl for one sodium ion to one chloride ion.
statements.tl: Ang formula unit ay nagpapakita ng pinakamababang whole-number ratio ng mga ion sa isang ionic compound, tulad ng NaCl para sa isang sodium ion sa isang chloride ion.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-sPFSnUoT76f1lJCbDPqrnwqO-qBcJSb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: To write an ionic formula, use the crisscross method: switch the oxidation numbers of the positive and negative ions to become subscripts.
statements.tl: Para isulat ang ionic formula, gamitin ang crisscross method: pagpalitin ang oxidation numbers ng positive at negative ions para maging subscripts.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Etyuf8FrzuhS9Vf_NrODPWnehq3sQCGi), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Many compounds are used in daily life, such as water for drinking, sodium chloride for flavoring food, and aspirin for relieving pain.
statements.tl: Maraming compound ang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na buhay, tulad ng tubig sa pag-inom, sodium chloride sa pagpapalasa ng pagkain, at aspirin sa pagpapagaan ng sakit.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1TRBVi24YbCDyvZDxvDqzl9k5i6M6gKL4), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Table salt is made of two elements joined together: sodium and chlorine. Scientists call it sodium chloride!
statements.tl: Ang table salt ay gawa sa dalawang elemento na pinagsama: sodium at chlorine. Tinatawag itong sodium chloride ng mga siyentipiko!

statements.text:
How do we name a simple ionic compound?

The metal's name comes first, followed by the nonmetal ending in '-ide'! For example, we call it sodium chloride.
statements.tl:
Paano natin pinangalanan ang isang simpleng ionic compound?

Una ang pangalan ng metal, at sumusunod ang di-metal na nagtatapos sa '-ide'! Halimbawa, tinatawag natin itong sodium chloride.

statements.text: Table salt is actually called sodium chloride, a cool compound made of sodium and chlorine!
statements.tl: Ang asing pangmesa ay tinatawag na sodium chloride, isang sangkap na gawa sa sodium at chlorine!

statements.text:
Is 'NaCl' just one tiny single particle?

Nope! An ionic compound is actually a HUGE network of millions of ions. 'NaCl' just shows the RATIO: one sodium for every one chlorine!
statements.tl:
Isa bang maliit na particle ang 'NaCl'?

Hindi! Ang ionic compound ay isang MALAKING network ng milyon-milyong ion. Ang 'NaCl' ay nagpapakita lang ng RATIO: isang sodium bawat isang chlorine!

statements.text:
Why does MgCl2 need TWO chlorines for one magnesium?

A magnesium ion has a +2 charge, but a chloride ion has only -1. So you need TWO chlorines (-1 and -1) to balance the +2 charge. That makes MgCl2!
statements.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng DALAWANG chlorine sa isang magnesium sa MgCl2?

Ang magnesium ion ay may +2 charge, pero ang chloride ion ay -1 lang. Kaya kailangan ng DALAWANG chlorine (-1 at -1) para tumbasan ang +2. Kaya MgCl2!

statements.text: Unlike sodium ions which are typically +1, transition metals can have more than one charge! Iron can be Fe2+ or Fe3+, so we see iron(II) and iron(III) in compound names.
statements.tl: Hindi tulad ng sodium ion na karaniwang +1, ang transition metals puwedeng magkaroon ng iba't ibang charge! Ang iron puwedeng Fe2+ o Fe3+, kaya may iron(II) at iron(III) sa mga pangalan.

statements.text:
What is the chemical formula for table salt?

It is NaCl, or sodium chloride! It is an ionic compound made of sodium (Na+) and chloride (Cl-) ions held together by opposite electrical charges.
statements.tl:
Ano ang chemical formula ng table salt?

Ito ay NaCl, o sodium chloride! Ito ay isang ionic compound na gawa sa sodium (Na+) at chloride (Cl-) ions na hawak ng magkasalungat na electrical charges.

statements.text:
What is the chemical formula of table salt?

The chemical formula of table salt is NaCl!
statements.tl:
Ano ang chemical formula ng table salt?

Ang chemical formula ng table salt ay NaCl!

statements.text:
What makes up table salt?

In NaCl, Na means sodium and Cl means chlorine. So, salt is made of sodium and chlorine!
statements.tl:
Ano ang bumubuo sa table salt?

Sa NaCl, ang Na ay sodium at ang Cl ay chlorine. Kaya ang salt ay gawa sa sodium at chlorine!

statements.text: The chemical formula of baking soda, also known as sodium bicarbonate, is NaHCO3!
statements.tl: Ang formula ng kemikal ng baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) ay NaHCO3!

statements.text:
What is the chemical formula for iron(III) oxide, a component of rust?

The chemical formula of iron(III) oxide is Fe2O3!
statements.tl:
Ano ang formula ng kemikal ng iron(III) oxide, isang sangkap ng kalawang?

Ang formula ng kemikal ng iron(III) oxide ay Fe2O3!

statements.text: The chemical formula for the table salt you use is NaCl, which stands for sodium and chlorine!
statements.tl: Ang kemikal na formula ng asin sa mesa mo ay NaCl, na nangangahulugang sodium at chlorine!

statements.text: A water molecule (H₂O) has two covalent bonds! This happens because the oxygen shares electrons with each of its two hydrogen atoms.
statements.tl: Ang molekula ng tubig (H₂O) ay may dalawang covalent bonds! Nangyayari ito dahil ang oxygen ay naghahati ng electrons sa bawat isa sa dalawang hydrogen atoms.

statements.text: In carbon dioxide (CO₂), carbon and each oxygen share two pairs of electrons, creating a double bond between them!
statements.tl: Sa carbon dioxide (CO₂), ang carbon at bawat oxygen ay naghahati ng dalawang pares ng elektron, kaya may double bond sa pagitan nila!

statements.text: A single water molecule is made of exactly two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom!
statements.tl: Ang isang water molecule ay binubuo ng eksaktong dalawang hydrogen atoms na nakakabit sa isang oxygen atom!

statements.text: Two fluorine atoms share one electron pair to form fluorine gas, and each fluorine atom is left with three lone pairs of electrons.
statements.tl: Ang dalawang fluorine atom ay nagshe-share ng isang pares ng electron para bumuo ng fluorine gas, at ang bawat fluorine atom ay may natitirang tatlong lone pairs ng electron.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1OqmK9SKhXu8fRm6d_kT5qmM3B7E7p9Wl), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The main difference? In an ionic bond, electrons are transferred! But in a covalent bond, electrons are shared.
statements.tl: Ang pinakamalaking pagkakaiba? Sa ionic bond, inililipat ang elektron! Ngunit sa covalent bond, pinaghahatian o ibinabahagi ang elektron.
statements.source: DepEd Science 9 CG (Matter); AAAS BSL Ch.4

statements.text:
What kind of atoms form covalent bonds?

They usually form between two nonmetals! Like hydrogen and oxygen in water, or carbon and oxygen in carbon dioxide.
statements.tl:
Anong uri ng mga atomo ang bumubuo ng covalent bonds?

Karaniwan silang nabubuo sa pagitan ng dalawang di-metal! Gaya ng hydrogen at oxygen sa tubig, o carbon at oxygen sa carbon dioxide.

statements.text: Two atoms can share electrons! One pair makes a single bond, two pairs make a double bond, and three pairs make a triple bond.
statements.tl: Pwedeng magbahagi ng elektron ang dalawang atomo! Isang pares ang single bond, dalawang pares ang double bond, at tatlong pares ang triple bond.

statements.text:
How do two hydrogen atoms form hydrogen gas (H₂)?

They share one pair of electrons—a simple covalent bond!
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuo ng dalawang hydrogen atom ang hydrogen gas (H₂)?

Nagbabahagi sila ng isang pares ng elektron—isang simpleng covalent bond!

statements.text:
What is a covalent bond?

In a covalent bond, two atoms share their electrons to form a molecule! It's like two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen forming water.
statements.tl:
Ano ang covalent bond?

Sa covalent bond, dalawang atomo ang naghahatian ng kanilang mga elektron upang magbuo ng molekula! Gaya ng dalawang hydrogen at isang oxygen na nagbubuo ng tubig.

statements.text:
Why is a nitrogen molecule (N₂) so hard to break apart?

Nitrogen gas (N₂) has a triple bond — three pairs of shared electrons — making it very strong and hard to break!
statements.tl:
Bakit napakatibay ng molekula ng nitrogen (N₂)?

Ang nitrogen gas (N₂) ay may triple bond — tatlong pares ng pinaghahatiang elektron — kaya napakatibay at mahirap putulin!
statements.source: AAAS 4D/H2 (electron sharing); NRC PS1.A (bond strength / binding energy)

statements.text: In a polar bond, electrons are shared unequally — one end becomes slightly negative and the other slightly positive!
statements.tl: Sa polar bond, hindi pantay ang hatian ng elektron — ang isang dulo ay bahagyang negatibo at ang kabila ay bahagyang positibo!
statements.source: NRC PS1.A; AAAS 4D/H8 (electron distribution determines molecular properties)

statements.text: An oxygen atom needs two more electrons to fill its outer shell, and each hydrogen needs one, so they share to form water!
statements.tl: Kailangan ng oxygen atom ng dalawang electrons para mapuno ang outer shell nito, at isa sa bawat hydrogen, kaya nag-share sila para gumawa ng water!

statements.text: A carbon atom needs four more electrons, and each oxygen needs two, so carbon shares two pairs with each oxygen in CO2!
statements.tl: Kailangan ng carbon atom ng apat na electrons, at dalawa sa bawat oxygen, kaya nag-share ang carbon ng dalawang pares sa bawat oxygen sa CO2!

statements.text: When two atoms share just one pair of electrons, it is called a single bond, like the hydrogen-oxygen links in water!
statements.tl: Kapag ang dalawang atoms ay nag-share ng isang pares ng electrons, tinatawag itong single bond, tulad ng hydrogen-oxygen links sa water!

statements.text:
Why do atoms bond willingly and stay together?

Forming a covalent bond releases energy! This keeps molecules happily stuck together instead of falling apart.
statements.tl:
Bakit kusang nagbo-bond ang mga atoms at nananatiling magkasama?

Naglalabas ng energy ang pagbuo ng covalent bond! Kaya nananatiling magkasama ang molecules imbes na maghiwalay.

statements.text:
Why is a water molecule bent like a V?

Because oxygen has two lone pairs of electrons, pushing the shape into a bent V!
statements.tl:
Bakit ang water molecule ay baluktot na parang V?

Dahil may dalawang lone pairs ng electrons ang oxygen, kaya baluktot ang itsura nito!

statements.text:
Why is carbon dioxide a straight molecule?

Carbon has no lone pairs! So, the two oxygen atoms line up straight on opposite sides.
statements.tl:
Bakit tuwid na molecule ang carbon dioxide?

Walang lone pairs ang carbon! Kaya pumila nang tuwid ang dalawang oxygen atoms sa magkabilang panig.

statements.text:
Why is a water molecule slightly negative on one end and positive on the other?

In water, oxygen pulls shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen! This makes one end slightly negative and the other slightly positive.
statements.tl:
Bakit ang isang dulo ng water molecule ay bahagyang negative at ang kabilang dulo ay positive?

Sa tubig, mas malakas hinila ng oxygen ang shared electrons kaysa sa hydrogen! Kaya ang isang dulo ng molecule ay bahagyang negative, at ang kabilang dulo ay positive.

statements.text:
What is the secret chemical code for water?

H2O!
statements.tl:
Ano ang formula ng kemikal para sa tubig?

H2O!

statements.text: The chemical formula for carbon dioxide is CO2!
statements.tl: Ang chemical formula ng carbon dioxide ay CO2!

statements.text:
What atoms make up the chemical formula for ammonia?

The chemical formula for ammonia is NH3. This means it is made of one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms!
statements.tl:
Anong mga atomo ang bumubuo sa kemikal na formula ng ammonia?

Ang kemikal na formula ng ammonia ay NH3. Ibig sabihin, gawa ito sa isang atomo ng nitrogen at tatlong atomo ng hydrogen!

statements.text: Covalent compounds are named using prefixes like mono-, di-, and tri- to show how many atoms of each element are present, with an -ide ending.
statements.tl: Ang mga covalent compound ay pinapangalanan gamit ang mga prefix tulad ng mono-, di-, at tri- para ipakita kung ilang atom ng bawat elemento ang naroon, na may -ide na dulo.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Etyuf8FrzuhS9Vf_NrODPWnehq3sQCGi), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why is water called H₂O?

Because each of its molecules is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom stuck together!
statements.tl:
Bakit ang tubig ay tinatawag na H₂O?

Dahil ang bawat molecule nito ay gawa sa dalawang hydrogen atom at isang oxygen atom na magkadikit!

statements.text: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a molecule made of one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. It's the gas we breathe out, and plants use it for photosynthesis!
statements.tl: Ang carbon dioxide (CO₂) ay isang molekula na gawa sa isang carbon atom at dalawang oxygen atom. Ito ang gas na ibinubuga natin, at ginagamit ng mga halaman sa photosynthesis!

statements.text: One water (H₂O) molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom joined together!
statements.tl: Ang isang molekula ng tubig (H₂O) ay gawa sa dalawang atomo ng hydrogen at isang atomo ng oksiheno na magkakabit!

statements.text:
How do elements make compounds?

Two or more elements combine to form a compound, like hydrogen and oxygen forming water!
statements.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng compound ang mga elemento?

Dalawa o higit pang elemento ang nagsasama para bumuo ng compound, gaya ng hydrogen at oxygen na gumagawa ng tubig!

statements.text:
What is the chemical formula of water?

It is H2O! This means each water molecule has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom bonded together.
statements.tl:
Ano ang chemical formula ng tubig?

Ito ay H2O! Ibig sabihin, bawat water molecule ay may 2 hydrogen atoms at 1 oxygen atom na nagsasama-sama.

statements.text:
What is CO2 and what does it do?

CO2 is the chemical formula for carbon dioxide! Each molecule has 1 carbon atom bonded to 2 oxygen atoms. It is the gas we breathe out and a key greenhouse gas.
statements.tl:
Ano ang CO2 at ano ang ginagawa nito?

Ang CO2 ay ang chemical formula para sa carbon dioxide! Bawat molecule ay may 1 carbon atom na nakakabit sa 2 oxygen atoms. Ito ang gas na ating hinihinga palabas at isang key greenhouse gas.

statements.text:
What makes organic and inorganic compounds different?

Organic compounds contain carbon, like sugars, proteins, and plastics. Most inorganic compounds don't, like table salt (NaCl) and water (H2O)!
statements.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng organic at inorganic compounds?

Ang organic compounds ay naglalaman ng carbon, tulad ng asukal, protina, at plastic. Karamihan sa inorganic compounds ay wala, tulad ng table salt (NaCl) at tubig (H2O)!

statements.text: In H2O, H2 means 2 hydrogen atoms and O means 1 oxygen atom. So, one water molecule has 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen!
statements.tl: Sa H2O, ang H2 ay 2 hydrogen atoms at ang O ay 1 oxygen atom. Kaya ang isang water molecule ay may 2 hydrogen at 1 oxygen!

statements.text:
What is the chemical formula for carbon dioxide?

The chemical formula of carbon dioxide is CO2!
statements.tl:
Ano ang chemical formula ng carbon dioxide?

Ang chemical formula ng carbon dioxide ay CO2!

statements.text: In CO2, C means 1 carbon atom and O2 means 2 oxygen atoms. So, one carbon dioxide molecule has 1 carbon and 2 oxygen!
statements.tl: Sa CO2, ang C ay 1 carbon atom at ang O2 ay 2 oxygen atoms. Kaya ang isang carbon dioxide molecule ay may 1 carbon at 2 oxygen!

statements.text: The chemical formula of methane is CH4!
statements.tl: Ang chemical formula ng methane ay CH4!

statements.text: In CH4, the C means 1 carbon atom and H4 means 4 hydrogen atoms! So, one methane molecule has exactly 1 carbon and 4 hydrogen.
statements.tl: Sa CH4, ang C ay 1 atomo ng karbon at ang H4 ay 4 atomo ng hidroheno! Kaya ang isang molekula ng methane ay may 1 karbon at 4 hidroheno.

statements.text:
What is the chemical formula for table sugar, also known as sucrose?

The chemical formula of table sugar (sucrose) is C12H22O11!
statements.tl:
Ano ang formula ng kemikal ng asukal na pangkain o table sugar (sucrose)?

Ang formula ng kemikal ng asukal na pangkain (table sugar o sucrose) ay C12H22O11!

statements.text: The chemical formula of glucose, which is a simple sugar, is C6H12O6!
statements.tl: Ang formula ng kemikal ng glucose (isang simpleng asukal) ay C6H12O6!

statements.text:
How are ions arranged in table salt?

In NaCl, sodium and chloride ions form a repeating pattern called a crystal lattice — not separate molecules!
statements.tl:
Paano nakaayos ang mga ion sa table salt?

Sa NaCl, ang sodium at chloride ion ay nakaayos sa paulit-ulit na pattern na tinatawag na crystal lattice — hindi hiwalay na molekula!
statements.source: NRC PS1.A: atoms combine to form extended structures such as crystals; AAAS 4D/H7

statements.text: Sugar is a covalent compound forming separate molecules, while salt is ionic and forms a giant repeating lattice of ions!
statements.tl: Ang asukal ay isang covalent compound na bumubuo ng hiwalay na molecules, habang ang asin ay ionic at bumubuo ng malaking paulit-ulit na lattice ng ions!

statements.text: In an ionic crystal like table salt, the points of the crystal lattice are occupied by ions, which are atoms that have gained or lost electrons to get an electric charge.
statements.tl: Sa ionic crystal tulad ng table salt, ang mga punto ng crystal lattice ay inookupahan ng mga ions, na mga atom na nakakuha o nawalan ng electrons para magkaroon ng electric charge.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-d2_6H1lqaek20CR3b1CmOrCIAZTvVrM), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Ionic compounds form a crystal lattice, a repeating three-dimensional pattern of positive and negative ions held tightly in place.
statements.tl: Ang mga ionic compound ay bumubuo ng crystal lattice, isang paulit-ulit na three-dimensional na pattern ng positive at negative ions na mahigpit na nakahawak sa lugar.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 180vRyn_Gyf9zzY8c4RbsGruCB1R3FzPx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Ball-and-stick models show how individual ions are oriented, while space-filling models show how ions actually pack tightly together in a crystal.
statements.tl: Ang ball-and-stick models ay nagpapakita kung paano nakaharap ang bawat ion, habang ang space-filling models ay nagpapakita kung paano talaga nagsisiksikan ang mga ion sa crystal.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Lz0hLuXZUrsyVa9hfC0jVZ4JMv0BnJN3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Many covalent compounds form individual molecules when nonmetal atoms share electrons with each other.
statements.tl: Maraming covalent compound ang bumubuo ng indibidwal na molecules kapag ang mga nonmetal atoms ay nagbabahagi ng electrons sa isa't isa.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Lz0hLuXZUrsyVa9hfC0jVZ4JMv0BnJN3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Ionic bonds hold ions together in an ionic crystal, while covalent bonds hold atoms within each water molecule and weak intermolecular interactions hold water molecules together.
statements.tl: Ang ionic bonds ang nagdidikit sa mga ions sa ionic crystal, habang ang covalent bonds ang nagdidikit sa mga atoms sa loob ng bawat water molecule at ang weak intermolecular interactions ang nagdidikit sa mga water molecules.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Lz0hLuXZUrsyVa9hfC0jVZ4JMv0BnJN3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Table salt forms tiny, cube-shaped crystals that are super fun to look at under a magnifying glass!
statements.tl: Ang table salt ay bumubuo ng maliliit na mga kristal na hugis-kubo na nakakatuwang tingnan sa ilalim ng magnifying glass!

statements.text:
Why does a grain of salt look like a tiny cube?

Because in an ionic compound, ions arrange in a repeating pattern called a crystal lattice! They aren't scattered randomly, making the salt look like tiny cubes.
statements.tl:
Bakit parang maliliit na kahon ang butil ng asin?

Dahil sa ionic compound, nakaayos ang mga ion sa paulit-ulit na pattern na crystal lattice! Hindi sila nagkalat, kaya parang maliliit na kahon ang asin.

statements.text:
What shape do salt crystals make?

Table salt (sodium chloride) forms cubic crystals—tiny cubes with equal square faces! It belongs to the cubic crystal system, one of seven main crystal systems.
statements.tl:
Anong hugis ang binubuo ng salt crystals?

Ang table salt (sodium chloride) ay bumubuo ng cubic crystals—maliliit na kubo na may pantay na square faces! Ito ay nasa cubic crystal system, isa sa pitong pangunahing crystal systems.

statements.text: Look at salt under a microscope — each grain is a tiny CUBE! That's because sodium and chloride ions line up in a perfect cubic pattern.
statements.tl: Tingnan ang asin sa ilalim ng microscope — ang bawat butil ay isang maliit na CUBE! Ito ay dahil ang sodium at chloride ions ay nakaayos sa cubic pattern.

statements.text:
Why does table salt melt at about 800°C while sugar melts at a much lower temperature?

Table salt melts at 800°C because its ions are locked in a strong crystal lattice, unlike sugar which melts much lower!
statements.tl:
Bakit natutunaw ang table salt sa halos 800°C habang ang asukal ay sa mas mababang temperatura?

Natutunaw ang table salt sa 800°C dahil ang mga ions nito ay nakakandado sa malakas na crystal lattice, iba sa asukal na mas mababa!

statements.text: Tapping an ionic crystal like salt shatters it into smaller cubes! Pushing the layers brings same-charged ions together, which repel each other.
statements.tl: Ang pagtapik sa ionic crystal tulad ng asin ay nagkakabasag nito sa mas maliliit na cubes! Pagtulak sa layers ay nagdadala sa same-charged ions na nagtatabuyan.

statements.text: The formula NaCl means one sodium ion for every chloride ion in the entire crystal, not a single molecule like H2O!
statements.tl: Ang formula na NaCl ay nangangahulugang isang sodium ion para sa bawat chloride ion sa buong crystal, hindi isang solong molecule tulad ng H2O!

statements.text:
Why is carbon dioxide a gas?

It's a covalent compound with weak attractions between its separate CO2 molecules, making it a gas at room temperature!
statements.tl:
Bakit gas ang carbon dioxide?

Isa itong covalent compound na mahina ang atraksyon sa pagitan ng magkakahiwalay nitong CO2 molecules, kaya gas ito sa room temperature!

statements.text:
Why are most ionic compounds solid at room temperature?

Their ions are held tightly in a rigid lattice, unlike many molecular covalent compounds that are gases or liquids!
statements.tl:
Bakit solid sa room temperature ang karamihan sa ionic compounds?

Mahigpit na nakakapit ang kanilang ions sa isang matigas na lattice, hindi tulad ng maraming molecular covalent compound na gas o liquid!

statements.text:
Why do covalent compounds like methane move freely as a gas?

They have individual molecules that move freely with no repeating crystal structure at all!
statements.tl:
Bakit malayang gumagalaw bilang gas ang covalent compounds tulad ng methane?

Mayroon silang mga molecule na malayang gumagalaw na walang paulit-ulit na crystal structure!

statements.text:
Why are ionic crystals hard but molecular covalent solids like wax are soft?

Strong ionic bonds hold the lattice tightly, but covalent molecules are only weakly attracted!
statements.tl:
Bakit matigas ang ionic crystals pero malambot ang molecular covalent solids tulad ng wax?

Hawak ng malalakas na ionic bonds ang lattice, pero mahina lang ang pagkakaakit ng covalent molecules!

statements.text: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires without breaking, such as gold, silver, and copper.
statements.tl: Ang mga ductile na materyales ay maaaring hatakin para maging wire nang hindi napuputol, tulad ng ginto, pilak, at tanso.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17CLJbOf1T9xM25Dcwc80bWFxNloPjFTr), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: In a metallic bond, outer electrons move freely like a sea of electrons! This is why metals conduct electricity and heat so well.
statements.tl: Sa metallic bond, ang outer electrons ay malayang gumagalaw na parang dagat ng mga elektron! Kaya naman ang mga metal ay mahusay maghatid ng kuryente at init.

statements.text: Metals are great conductors because some electrons inside them are free to move easily, letting electric current flow right through!
statements.tl: Magaling ang mga metal na conductor dahil may mga malayang elektron na madaling gumalaw, kaya madaling dumaloy ang kuryente sa mga ito!

statements.text: A sodium-23 atom has 11 protons, 12 neutrons, and 11 electrons, and its one outer valence electron is the one that delocalizes to join the sea of electrons in metallic bonding.
statements.tl: Ang sodium-23 atom ay may 11 protons, 12 neutrons, at 11 electrons, at ang kanyang nag-iisang outer valence electron ang siyang nagde-delocalize para sumali sa sea of electrons sa metallic bonding.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1IIRcY8Mf1r8GQDgkc7YgacvZq5uxNuqj), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The sea of electrons model, which explains how metallic bonding works, was proposed by scientist Paul Drude in the early 1900s.
statements.tl: Ang sea of electrons model, na nagpapaliwanag kung paano gumagana ang metallic bonding, ay iminungkahi ng siyentistang si Paul Drude noong unang bahagi ng 1900s.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1IIRcY8Mf1r8GQDgkc7YgacvZq5uxNuqj), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: In a piece of sodium metal, each sodium atom gives up its one valence electron to the sea of electrons, leaving behind a positive atomic core with 11 protons and 10 electrons.
statements.tl: Sa isang piraso ng sodium metal, ang bawat sodium atom ay nagbibigay ng kanyang nag-iisang valence electron sa sea of electrons, na nag-iiwan ng positive atomic core na may 11 protons at 10 electrons.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1IIRcY8Mf1r8GQDgkc7YgacvZq5uxNuqj), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Metals such as copper, zinc, and iron are electrical conductors, meaning they allow electricity to pass through them.
statements.tl: Ang mga metal tulad ng tanso, zinc, at bakal ay mga electrical conductors, ibig sabihin hinahayaan nilang dumaan ang kuryente.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1tiSsNowPhRjNIgrz9Y53HicbPLVL8ZV5), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Brass and steel are metals that are good heat conductors, often used in kitchenware and tools.
statements.tl: Ang brass at steel ay mga metal na mahuhusay na heat conductors, kadalasang ginagamit sa mga kagamitan sa kusina at tools.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1tiSsNowPhRjNIgrz9Y53HicbPLVL8ZV5), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Atoms of different sizes block the layers of metal atoms from sliding, making an alloy harder to bend or break!
statements.tl: Ang mga atomo na may magkaibang laki ay humaharang sa paggalaw ng mga patong, kaya mas mahirap baluktutin o sirain ang aleasyon!

statements.text: Metals have free electrons that move around easily, which is why they carry electricity so well!
statements.tl: Ang mga metal ay may malalayang elektron na gumagalaw nang madali, kaya magaling silang magdala ng kuryente!

statements.text:
What's really happening inside a metal that lets it carry electricity?

In a metal, atoms share their outer electrons in something like a sea of free electrons!
statements.tl:
Ano ba talaga ang nangyayari sa loob ng metal kaya nakakapagpadaloy ito ng kuryente?

Sa metal, ang mga atomo ay nagbabahaginan ng kanilang panlabas na elektron — parang dagat ng malayang elektron!

statements.text:
What makes metals look so shiny and sparkly?

The free electrons in metals bounce light back, which is why metals look shiny!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nagpapakintab at nagpagniningning sa mga metal?

Ang malalayang elektron sa metal ang nagbabalik ng ilaw, kaya makintab ang mga metal!

statements.text: The same free electrons make metals amazing at carrying both heat and electricity!
statements.tl: Ang parehong mga malalayang elektron ang dahilan kung bakit napakahusay ng metal sa pagpapadaloy ng init at kuryente!

statements.text: Copper is great at carrying electricity because it has lots of 'free electrons' inside. They aren't tightly held, so they drift easily like water in a pipe!
statements.tl: Magaling ang tanso sa pagdadala ng kuryente dahil may maraming 'free electrons' sa loob. Hindi sila nakakabit nang mahigpit, kaya dumadaloy silang parang tubig sa tubo!

statements.text: Inside metal, atoms let go of outer electrons to move freely! Scientists call this a 'sea of electrons' that holds the metal together and carries electricity.
statements.tl: Sa loob ng metal, iniiwan ng mga atomo ang outer electrons para gumalaw! Tinatawag itong 'sea of electrons' na nagbubuklod sa metal at nagdadala ng kuryente.

statements.text: The same free electrons that carry electricity also make metals shiny! When light hits a metal, its electrons catch and bounce it right back, giving that bright, mirror-like gleam.
statements.tl: Ang parehong free electrons na nagdadala ng kuryente ang nagpapakintab sa metal! Kapag tumama ang liwanag, sinalo ng mga electrons at ibinalik agad, kaya may matingkad na kintab na parang salamin.

statements.text:
How does water carry electricity compared to metal?

Metal uses free electrons, but water uses dissolved minerals or salt! That’s why wet hands are dangerous. Metal is a better conductor, but dirty water can still shock you!
statements.tl:
Paano nagdadala ng kuryente ang tubig kumpara sa metal?

Ang metal ay gumagamit ng malayang electron, pero ang tubig ay mga natunaw na ion mula sa mineral o asin! Kaya delikado ang basang kamay. Mas magaling ang metal, pero maruming tubig ay nakakuryente pa rin!

statements.text:
Why are alloys stronger than pure metals?

Foreign atoms in an alloy block the metal layers from sliding past each other, so the metal won't bend or break as easily!
statements.tl:
Bakit mas malakas ang mga alloy kaysa purong metal?

Ang mga dayuhang atom sa alloy ay humahadlang sa mga layer ng metal na mag-slide, kaya hindi ito madaling mabali o mabago ang hugis!

statements.text:
Why are ionic compounds like salt so hard to melt?

They are hard solids with very high melting points because the pull between their opposite ions is super strong!
statements.tl:
Bakit ang mga ionic compound gaya ng asin ay napakahirap tunawin?

Sila ay matigas na solido na may napakataas na melting point dahil napakalakas ng hila ng magkasalungat na ion!
statements.source: NRC PS1.A: properties of materials understood from forces between constituents

statements.text:
Why is diamond the hardest natural material?

In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four other carbons in one giant network, making it super hard!
statements.tl:
Bakit ang diamond ang pinakamatigas na natural na materyal?

Sa diamond, ang bawat carbon atom ay covalent na nakakabit sa apat na ibang carbon sa isang malaking network, kaya ito ang pinakamatigas na natural na materyal!
statements.source: NRC PS1.A: extended structures (crystals) and properties like hardness; AAAS 4D/H7

statements.text: Metals have free electrons that move around easily, which is why they carry electricity so well!
statements.tl: Ang mga metal ay may malalayang elektron na gumagalaw nang madali, kaya magaling silang magdala ng kuryente!

statements.text: Metals are usually shiny and can conduct both heat and electricity, like the copper wires you see at home.
statements.tl: Ang mga metal ay karaniwang makintab at kaya nilang magdala ng init at kuryente, tulad ng copper wires na nakikita mo sa bahay.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17CLJbOf1T9xM25Dcwc80bWFxNloPjFTr), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Covalent compounds often have low melting points because their molecules are held together by weak attractions that need little heat to break.
statements.tl: Ang mga covalent compound ay kadalasang may mababang melting point dahil ang kanilang mga molecule ay pinagdirikit ng mahihinang atraksyon na kaunting init lang ang kailangan para masira.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 180vRyn_Gyf9zzY8c4RbsGruCB1R3FzPx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Ionic compounds are hard but brittle, so a strong hit can shift their crystal lattice and make them crack or break.
statements.tl: Ang mga ionic compound ay matigas ngunit brittle, kaya ang malakas na pagtama ay maaaring maglipat ng kanilang crystal lattice at maging dahilan ng pagkabasag nito.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 180vRyn_Gyf9zzY8c4RbsGruCB1R3FzPx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity in solid or dissolved form because they have no free-moving charged particles.
statements.tl: Ang mga covalent compound ay karaniwang hindi nagpapadaloy ng kuryente sa solid o natunaw na anyo dahil wala silang malayang gumagalaw na charged particles.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 180vRyn_Gyf9zzY8c4RbsGruCB1R3FzPx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Conductors are materials with high thermal conductivity, so heat travels through them quickly and easily.
statements.tl: Ang conductors ay mga materyales na may mataas na thermal conductivity, kaya mabilis at madaling dumaan ang heat sa kanila.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1jCN_WkP_L48clUz6sCRvv36szAxBDd9Q), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why are wires made of metal?

Metals are good conductors of electricity, so it flows easily through them! That's why wires are made of metal.
statements.tl:
Bakit gawa sa metal ang mga alambre?

Maganda ang metal sa pagdaloy ng kuryente, kaya madali itong dumaloy! Kaya gawa sa metal ang mga alambre.

statements.text: Heat moves quickly through metal! That’s why a metal pot gets hot super fast when you put it on the stove.
statements.tl: Mabilis dumaloy ang init sa metal! Kaya mainit agad ang kalderong metal kapag iniinit sa kalan.

statements.text:
Why did people in ancient times use bronze to make their weapons and tools?

Because bronze is harder than pure copper, making it perfect for tough ancient tools and weapons!
statements.tl:
Bakit ginamit ng mga tao noon ang bronze para sa kanilang mga sandata at kasangkapan?

Dahil mas matigas ang bronze kaysa sa purong tanso, kaya maganda ito para sa matitibay na sandata at kasangkapan!

statements.text: Inside a metal, moving electrons quickly carry heat from the hot part to the cooler part!
statements.tl: Sa loob ng metal, ang gumagalaw na mga elektron ay mabilis na nagdadala ng init mula sa mainit patungo sa malamig!

statements.text:
Ever wonder why metals are so good with heat and electricity?

Metals like copper and iron are conductors — they carry heat and electricity really well!
statements.tl:
Napapaisip ka ba kung bakit napakahusay ng mga metal sa init at kuryente?

Ang mga metal tulad ng tanso at bakal ay mga conductor — maganda silang magpadaloy ng init at kuryente!

statements.text:
Did you know most elements are metals?

Yes! Metals are usually shiny and are great at conducting electricity and heat.
statements.tl:
Alam mo ba na karamihan sa mga elemento ay mga metal?

Oo! Ang mga metal ay karaniwang makintab at mahusay magdaloy ng kuryente at init.

statements.text: It takes a LOT of heat to melt salt because the pull between ions is very strong! You need huge heat to break these bonds, giving high melting points.
statements.tl: Kailangan ng SOBRANG init para matunaw ang asin dahil sobrang lakas ng hila ng mga ion! Kailangan ng napakaraming init para basagin ang bonds, kaya mataas ang melting point.

statements.text:
Can salt water carry electricity?

Yes! When salt dissolves in water, the ions move freely and carry the current. But remember, dry solid salt does NOT conduct electricity!
statements.tl:
Nakakadaloy ba ng kuryente ang tubig na may asin?

Oo! Kapag natunaw ang asin sa tubig, malayang gumagalaw ang mga ion at nagdadala ng kuryente. Pero ang tuyong solid na asin ay HINDI nakakadaloy ng kuryente!

statements.text: Salt is hard but shatters easily! When struck, its ions shift, making the same charges (+ and +) line up. They push each other away, cracking the crystal apart!
statements.tl: Matigas ang asin pero madaling mabasag! Kapag hinampas, umuusog ang mga ion, kaya magkatapat ang parehong charge (+ at +). Nagtutulakan sila, kaya nababasag ang crystal!

statements.text: Diamond carries heat really well, but electricity can't flow through it — unlike graphite, which can conduct electricity!
statements.tl: Magaling dalhin ng diamante ang init, pero hindi dumadaloy ang kuryente dito — iba sa grapayt na nakakapadaloy ng kuryente!

statements.text: Your DNA is neatly packed into structures called chromosomes, found inside a cell's nucleus. Each chromosome carries many genes.
statements.tl: Ang DNA ay maayos na nakabalot sa mga istrukturang tinatawag na chromosomes, na matatagpuan sa nucleus ng selula. Ang bawat chromosome ay may dalang maraming gene.
statements.source: AAAS Benchmarks 5B/H3-H4; encyclopedia-stable cell biology (chromosomes in nucleus)

statements.text: Half of your chromosomes come from your mother, and the other half come from your father.
statements.tl: Kalahati ng iyong mga chromosome ay mula sa iyong ina, at kalahati naman ay mula sa iyong ama.

statements.text: DNA replication begins at specific sequences called origins of replication, where proteins bind and open the double helix to form a replication bubble.
statements.tl: Nagsisimula ang DNA replication sa mga partikular na sequence na tinatawag na origins of replication, kung saan kumakabit ang mga protein at binubuksan ang double helix para bumuo ng replication bubble.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 12xUWs5HUkWVojo9AmQ-jLobs7WCHSTz3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How fast can a bacterium copy its whole chromosome?

E. coli can replicate its entire circular chromosome of 4.6 million base pairs in about 42 minutes from a single origin.
statements.tl:
Gaano kabilis makopya ng isang bacterium ang buong chromosome nito?

Kayang i-replicate ng E. coli ang buong circular chromosome nito na may 4.6 million base pairs sa loob ng halos 42 minuto mula sa isang origin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 12xUWs5HUkWVojo9AmQ-jLobs7WCHSTz3), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Homozygous individuals have two identical alleles for a trait, while heterozygous individuals have two dissimilar alleles for that trait.
statements.tl: Ang homozygous na indibidwal ay may dalawang magkaparehong alleles para sa isang katangian, habang ang heterozygous ay may dalawang magkaibang alleles para sa katangiang iyon.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 16DvTOACFxsb4TUvvlzSyNOKbdCeAiMbx), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A human sperm is a tiny haploid cell with a tail for swimming, and it carries half of the father's genetic information to the egg.
statements.tl: Ang human sperm ay isang napakaliit na haploid cell na may buntot para lumangoy, at dala nito ang kalahati ng genetic information ng ama papunta sa egg.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 16a7dmIFwwX-sxKxyF092mTrviO3viAgU), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What are homologous chromosomes?

They are matching pairs of chromosomes that carry alleles - versions of the same genes - at the same positions.
statements.tl:
Ano ang homologous chromosomes?

Ang mga ito ay magkapares na chromosomes na nagdadala ng alleles - mga bersyon ng parehong genes - sa magkatulad na posisyon.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17aVmKg3nvJlvgDxJLfUfayrpBb_u6d0q), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: DNA carries codes passed from parents to offspring, and these codes determine traits like hair type and blood type.
statements.tl: Ang DNA ay nagdadala ng mga code na ipinapasa mula sa magulang papunta sa anak, at ang mga code na ito ang tumutukoy sa mga katangian tulad ng uri ng buhok at blood type.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1E2uYXW9ahZ1W4ili4LAiXLdtheKQtQ8K), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What do the sugar and phosphate parts of DNA do?

They form the backbone, the strong sides of the DNA ladder that hold the bases in place!
statements.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng sugar at phosphate na bahagi ng DNA?

Binubuo nila ang backbone, ang matibay na gilid ng hagdan ng DNA na humahawak sa mga base sa kanilang lugar!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1E2uYXW9ahZ1W4ili4LAiXLdtheKQtQ8K), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Centrioles are small structures that help form spindle fibers, which pull chromosomes apart during cell division.
statements.tl: Ang centrioles ay maliliit na structures na tumutulong bumuo ng spindle fibers, na humihila sa mga chromosomes palayo sa isa't isa habang naghahati ang cell.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1L8maAIbzMHn1uRakLl12fdJEA4xzCWex), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Females have two X chromosomes, so they can be carriers of an X-linked recessive trait without showing it themselves.
statements.tl: Ang mga babae ay may dalawang X chromosome, kaya maaari silang maging carrier ng X-linked recessive trait nang hindi ito lumalabas sa kanila.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1NxMyF3i30J-KE0MWbJhSHF2FrLVoRc-c), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Genes are segments of DNA that code for proteins or RNA, and these segments influence traits like hair color and eye color.
statements.tl: Ang genes ay mga segment ng DNA na nagko-code para sa proteins o RNA, at ang mga segment na ito ang nakakaapekto sa traits tulad ng kulay ng buhok at mata.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1UdYfptS7ORDL9QUbI1bspHXr__SNCuEb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Protein synthesis follows the central dogma of biology, where genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to protein.
statements.tl: Ang protein synthesis ay sumusunod sa central dogma ng biology, kung saan ang genetic information ay dumadaloy mula DNA papuntang RNA papuntang protein.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1UdYfptS7ORDL9QUbI1bspHXr__SNCuEb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What is the difference between haploid and diploid cells?

Haploid cells have one set of chromosomes, while diploid cells have two complete sets!
statements.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng haploid at diploid cells?

Ang haploid cells ay may isang set ng chromosomes, habang ang diploid cells ay may dalawang kumpletong set!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1ZNSEtEe3ihwQZtOQQxkMm35kVTwKsljU), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A replicated chromosome consists of two identical halves called sister chromatids, joined together at a point called the centromere.
statements.tl: Ang replicated chromosome ay binubuo ng dalawang magkaparehong hati na tinatawag na sister chromatids, na pinagdugtong sa isang punto na tinatawag na centromere.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1_W6gIaE8Zij9DTNPVFgBJtJAR1nWLPtR), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: A diploid cell has two sets of chromosomes, one set from each parent, like most body cells in humans.
statements.tl: Ang diploid cell ay may dalawang set ng chromosomes, isang set mula sa bawat magulang, tulad ng karamihan sa mga body cells ng tao.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1eaRSWbyPbQMSO-tJp6RT9NSrXkowqkTl), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Like dogs, cats, and goats, common observable physical traits passed to offspring are the presence of fur, body shape, and number of legs.
statements.tl: Tulad ng aso, pusa, at kambing, ang mga karaniwang nakikitang physical na katangian na ipinapasa sa mga anak ay ang pagkakaroon ng balahibo, hugis ng katawan, at bilang ng mga binti.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1u9v0PXccVRBiBg7TVHSqZe2PXX8dZzmL), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Chromosomes are threadlike DNA-and-protein structures inside the nucleus that carry the cell's genes and pass heredity from parent cells to daughter cells.
statements.tl: Ang chromosomes ay mga threadlike na DNA at protein sa loob ng nucleus na nagdadala ng genes ng cell at nagpapasa ng heredity mula parent cell papunta sa daughter cell.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id lrmds-17288), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Some viruses can insert their own DNA into a host cell's DNA, disrupting genes and causing mutations.
statements.tl: Ang ilang viruses ay maaaring magpasok ng sarili nilang DNA sa DNA ng host cell, na nakakagambala sa mga genes at nagdudulot ng mutations.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1DmCoJIJKHoF-CSXwI-YyTi5jwZDWG0pA), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What is a mutation?

A mutation is a change in DNA — it might do nothing, help, or hurt the living thing that has it!
statements.tl:
Ano ang mutation?

Ang mutation ay pagbabago sa DNA — maaaring walang epekto, makatulong, o makasama sa nabubuhay na bagay!

statements.text:
What causes mutations in DNA?

Mutations can be caused by things like radiation and certain chemicals that damage DNA.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nagiging sanhi ng mutation?

Maaaring magdulot ng mutation ang mga bagay tulad ng radiation at ilang kemikal na nakakasira ng DNA.

statements.text:
Can sunlight change my DNA?

Yes! UV light from the sun is a mutagen, so too much sun can damage DNA and cause mutations.
statements.tl:
Pwede bang baguhin ng sikat ng araw ang DNA ko?

Oo! Ang UV light mula sa araw ay mutagen, kaya ang sobrang araw ay pwedeng makasira ng DNA at magdulot ng mutation.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17iINbPFUWHTZco-w7llCZAvEBQyGjVU5), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: An insertion mutation adds one or more nucleotide bases into the DNA sequence, which can shift the reading frame and change many amino acids.
statements.tl: Ang insertion mutation ay nagdadagdag ng isa o higit pang nucleotide bases sa DNA sequence, na pwedeng maglipat ng reading frame at magbago ng maraming amino acid.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 17iINbPFUWHTZco-w7llCZAvEBQyGjVU5), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How can one tiny DNA change cause a disease?

Sickle cell anemia results from a substitution mutation that swaps one base, placing a different amino acid in hemoglobin and changing the shape of red blood cells.
statements.tl:
Paano nagdudulot ng sakit ang isang maliit na pagbabago sa DNA?

Ang sickle cell anemia ay resulta ng substitution mutation na nagpapalit ng isang base, kaya ibang amino acid ang nailagay sa hemoglobin at nagbago ang hugis ng red blood cells.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1DmCoJIJKHoF-CSXwI-YyTi5jwZDWG0pA), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Mutations can occur spontaneously during normal cellular processes or from exposure to physical and chemical agents called mutagens.
