statements.tl: Ang mutations ay maaaring mangyari nang spontaneous sa normal na proseso ng cells o mula sa exposure sa physical at chemical agents na tinatawag na mutagens.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1DmCoJIJKHoF-CSXwI-YyTi5jwZDWG0pA), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Mutations can alter a protein's structure and function, because changing the amino acid sequence can change how the protein folds and what job it can do.
statements.tl: Maaaring baguhin ng mutation ang structure at function ng isang protein, dahil ang pagbabago sa amino acid sequence ay nakakapagpabago kung paano tumutupi ang protein at kung anong trabaho ang kaya nitong gawin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1XVTW66VvgMxtmqL4hoyg9deHdQZMQ3I8), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Sunburn happens when UV rays from the sun damage the DNA in your skin cells; getting sunburned again and again raises your risk of skin cancer later on.
statements.tl: Nangyayari ang sunburn kapag sinisira ng UV rays ng araw ang DNA ng mga selula ng balat mo; ang paulit-ulit na sunburn ay nagpapataas ng panganib ng skin cancer sa hinaharap.
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable; DOH Philippines; DepEd G5 Health

statements.text:
What causes Down syndrome?

Having three copies of chromosome 21 instead of two — this happens when chromosomes fail to separate properly during meiosis, called nondisjunction.
statements.tl:
Ano ang sanhi ng Down syndrome?

Ang pagkakaroon ng tatlong kopya ng chromosome 21 sa halip na dalawa — nangyayari ito kapag hindi wastong naghiwalay ang mga chromosome sa panahon ng meiosis, tinatawag na nondisjunction.

statements.text:
What makes DNA mutate?

DNA can change from a copying mistake, or from too much sunlight (UV), cigarette smoke, or certain chemicals — that's why sun protection matters!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nagpapabago sa DNA?

Nagbabago ang DNA dahil sa pagkakamali sa pagkopya nito, o dahil sa sobrang sikat ng araw (UV), usok ng sigarilyo, o ilang kemikal — kaya mahalaga ang pag-iingat sa araw!

statements.text:
What causes mutations in DNA?

Things like radiation and certain chemicals, or copying mistakes in DNA — and if it happens in sex cells, it can pass to the next generation.
statements.tl:
Ano ang sanhi ng mutation sa DNA?

Mga bagay tulad ng radiation at ilang kemikal, o pagkakamali sa pagkopya ng DNA — kapag nangyari ito sa sex cells, maipapasa ito sa susunod na henerasyon.
statements.source: AAAS Benchmarks 5B/H5 (mutations caused by radiation and chemicals; passed on if in sex cells)

statements.text:
What is a silent mutation?

Not all mutations show. In a silent mutation, a DNA letter changes but the protein stays the same — like a typo you can still read as the same word.
statements.tl:
Ano ang silent mutation?

Hindi lahat ng mutation ay may epekto. Sa silent mutation, nagbabago ang isang letra ng DNA pero pareho pa rin ang protina — parang typo na naiintindihan mo pa rin.

statements.text:
Does the body fix mistakes in our DNA?

Yes! Special proteins act like a spell-checker, finding and fixing many DNA errors before they become permanent — so we end up with far fewer mutations.
statements.tl:
Inaayos ba ng katawan ang mali sa DNA?

Oo! May espesyal na protina na parang spell-check na naghahanap at nag-aayos ng maraming mali sa DNA bago ito maging permanenteng mutation — kaya mas kaunti ang mutation na natitira sa atin.

statements.text:
What happens when DNA makes a copying mistake?

Sometimes when DNA copies itself, a base gets swapped by mistake — this is called a mutation, like a typo in writing. Some have no effect; others cause changes.
statements.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa pagkakamali sa pagkopya ng DNA?

Minsan kapag kumokopya ang DNA, may napapalitan na base dahil sa pagkakamali — tinatawag itong mutation, parang typo sa pagsulat. May walang epekto, pero may nagdudulot ng pagbabago.

statements.text:
What is a mutation?

A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence — a part might be altered, deleted, or added, and this can change how a gene works.
statements.tl:
Ano ang mutation?

Ang mutation ay pagbabago sa pagkakasunod-sunod ng DNA — maaaring magbago, mawala, o madagdagan ang isang bahagi, at maaari nitong baguhin ang paggana ng isang gene.
statements.source: AAAS Benchmarks 5B/H4 (inserting, deleting, or substituting DNA segments can alter genes)

statements.text: Mutation and variation aren't the same. Variation means differences among individuals, like eye color or height, and can come from genes or the environment. A mutation is a change in DNA — a source of new genetic variation.
statements.tl: Magkaiba ang mutation at variation. Ang variation ay mga pagkakaiba sa mga indibidwal, gaya ng kulay ng mata o taas, na maaaring mula sa genes o kapaligiran. Ang mutation ay pagbabago sa DNA — isang pinagmumulan ng bagong genetic variation.

statements.text:
How can one tiny gene change cause disease?

Cells use instructions in genes to build proteins, the tiny machines that run your body. Change a letter in a gene, and the protein's shape can go wrong — that's how some mutations cause disease.
statements.tl:
Paano nagiging sanhi ng sakit ang mutation?

Ginagamit ng mga selula ang tagubilin sa gene para gumawa ng protina, ang mga maliit na makina na nagpapatakbo sa katawan. Kapag nagbago ang letra sa gene, puwedeng magmali ang hugis ng protina — kaya nagkakasakit.

statements.text: A mutation that lets a bacterium survive an antibiotic is beneficial for the microbe but harmful for a sick person, depending on whose survival!
statements.tl: Ang mutation na nagpapahintulot sa bacterium na mabuhay sa antibiotic ay beneficial para sa microbe pero harmful para sa may sakit, depende sa survival!

statements.text: A mutation that blocks chlorophyll is harmful for a green plant because it can no longer harvest sunlight well!
statements.tl: Ang mutation na pumipigil sa chlorophyll ay harmful para sa berdeng halaman dahil hindi na ito makakakuha ng sikat ng araw nang maayos!

statements.text: Neutral does not mean nothing happened in the DNA! It just means the change did not clearly help or hurt the organism's function or survival.
statements.tl: Ang neutral ay hindi ibig sabihin na walang nangyari sa DNA! Ibig sabihin lang nito, ang pagbabago ay hindi malinaw na nakatulong o nakasama sa function o survival ng organismo.

statements.text: Mutations create genetic diversity, and while some are harmful, others can be beneficial and contribute to evolution.
statements.tl: Ang mutations ay lumilikha ng genetic diversity, at habang ang ilan ay nakakasama, ang iba ay maaaring maging kapaki-pakinabang at makatulong sa evolution.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1DmCoJIJKHoF-CSXwI-YyTi5jwZDWG0pA), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Not all mutations are harmful — some are neutral with no effect, some are harmful like those causing cancer, and some are beneficial and help organisms survive.
statements.tl: Hindi lahat ng mutasyon ay masama — may neutral na walang epekto, may nakakapinsala tulad ng kanser, at may kapaki-pakinabang na tumutulong sa organismo na mabuhay.

statements.text: A mutation can be helpful, harmful, or have no effect at all — most changes to DNA don't hurt or help, they're just neutral.
statements.tl: Ang isang mutation ay pwedeng makatulong, makasama, o walang epekto — karamihan sa pagbabago sa DNA ay wala lang, neutral.
statements.source: AAAS Benchmarks 5B/H1, 5B/H4 (resulting features may help, harm, or have little or no effect)

statements.text:
Is a mutation always bad?

No! A mutation is a change in an organism's DNA, and it can be harmless, harmful, or even helpful for survival.
statements.tl:
Palagi bang masama ang mutation?

Hindi! Ang mutation ay pagbabago sa DNA ng isang nilalang, at maaari itong walang epekto, makasama, o makatulong sa kaligtasan nito.

statements.text:
How can a tiny mutation make someone sick?

Harmful mutations can change a protein's shape so a cell process fails, the usual disease example in secondary biology pages!
statements.tl:
Paano nakakapagkasakit ang isang maliit na mutation?

Ang harmful mutation ay maaaring magbago ng hugis ng protina kaya nabibigo ang cell process, ang karaniwang halimbawa ng sakit sa secondary biology pages!

statements.text:
Can a mutation ever be helpful for our immune system?

Yes! A rare mutation in a human immune receptor reduces HIV risk, a beneficial example in sources, not a reason to seek infection.
statements.tl:
Pwede bang maging helpful ang mutation para sa immune system natin?

Oo! Ang bihirang mutation sa immune receptor ay nagpapababa ng HIV risk, isang beneficial na halimbawa, hindi dahilan para gustuhing magkasakit.

statements.text:
Can a color change be both good and bad?

Yes! A color mutation might hide a moth on dark bark but expose it on pale bark, showing that being helpful or harmful depends on the environment.
statements.tl:
Pwede bang maging mabuti at masama ang pagbabago ng kulay?

Oo! Ang color mutation ay pwedeng magtago sa gamu-gamo sa maitim na balat ng kahoy pero mailantad sa maputlang balat, kaya ang mabuti o masama ay depende sa kapaligiran.

statements.text:
Why are RNA viruses tricky?

RNA viruses mutate quickly! Some changes help the virus spread, which is a benefit for it but harmful to its hosts, showing benefit and harm at two levels.
statements.tl:
Bakit nakakalito ang RNA viruses?

Mabilis mag-mutate ang RNA viruses! Ang ilang pagbabago ay tumutulong sa virus na kumalat (benepisyo) pero masama sa hosts (pinsala), isang halimbawa ng benepisyo at pinsala sa dalawang antas.

statements.text: Some fruit mutations that stop seeds are super useful to farmers and eaters, even if they would be harmful for the plant in the wild!
statements.tl: Ang ilang mutation sa prutas na pumipigil sa buto ay kapaki-pakinabang sa mga magsasaka at kumakain, kahit na masama ito para sa halaman sa ilang!

statements.text:
What does Ultraviolet light do to our cells?

Ultraviolet light can damage DNA and raise the mutation rate! Whether each change helps, hurts, or does nothing is a separate later question.
statements.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng Ultraviolet light sa ating cells?

Ang ultraviolet light ay kayang sirain ang DNA at pataasin ang mutation rate! Kung ang bawat pagbabago ay nakakatulong, nakakasakit, o walang ginagawa ay hiwalay na tanong sa susunod.

statements.text:
Do all DNA copying mistakes become mutations?

Nope! Cells proofread DNA copies, so many mistakes never become mutations. This explains why not every copying error is harmful!
statements.tl:
Lahat ba ng pagkakamali sa pagkopya ng DNA ay nagiging mutations?

Hindi! Pinoproofread ng mga cells ang mga kopya ng DNA, kaya maraming pagkakamali ang hindi nagiging mutations, kaya hindi lahat ng pagkakamali ay nakakasama.

statements.text: Much DNA does not code for protein! Many letter changes there are scored neutral unless a control switch was hit, which is a cool distinction textbooks make.
statements.tl: Maraming DNA ang hindi nagko-code para sa protein! Maraming pagbabago ng letra doon ay tinuturing na neutral maliban na lang kung natamaan ang isang control switch, isang pagkakaiba sa mga textbook.

statements.text: Whole-genome duplications in plants can be beneficial! This large mutation can make bigger fruits or new species, which sources treat as sometimes very helpful.
statements.tl: Ang whole-genome duplications sa mga halaman ay maaaring maging kapaki-pakinabang! Ang malaking mutation na ito ay gumagawa ng mas malalaking prutas o bagong species, na minsan nakakatulong.

statements.text: Plant breeders sometimes keep beneficial mutations for better yield or disease resistance. They write these cool examples in agricultural science sources!
statements.tl: Minsan, pinipili ng mga plant breeders ang beneficial mutations para sa mas maraming ani o panlaban sa sakit, at isinusulat ito sa agricultural science sources!

statements.text:
Is every inherited color-vision change bad?

Not always! Some are harmful for certain tasks but nearly neutral for others. That's why we must name the job when labeling an effect!
statements.tl:
Masama ba ang lahat ng inherited color-vision change?

Hindi laging masama! Minsan harmful ito sa ilang trabaho pero halos neutral sa iba. Kaya dapat sabihin ang trabaho kapag nilalagyan ng label ang epekto!

statements.text: Carbon dioxide is the fizzy gas in soft drinks and the gas we breathe out! You can test for it because it turns limewater cloudy.
statements.tl: Ang carbon dioxide ang bumubulang gas sa softdrinks at ang gas na ibinubuga natin! Matetest ito dahil pinalalabo nito ang limewater.

statements.text: Waiting a few minutes lets the solid settle down, so scientists can see and measure the precipitate clearly!
statements.tl: Kapag naghintay ka ng ilang minuto, lulubog ang solid para makita at masukod ng mga scientist ang precipitate nang malinaw!

statements.text: Repeated trials under comparable conditions help assess reliability. Results need not be exactly identical because measurements vary. Record all trials, compare their spread and check unexpected differences. Repeatability does not prove that the explanation is correct; the method must also test the intended question fairly.
statements.tl: Nakakatulong ang paulit-ulit na trials sa maihahambing na kondisyon upang suriin ang reliability. Hindi kailangang eksaktong pareho ang resulta dahil nag-iiba ang sukat. Itala ang lahat ng trial, ihambing ang pagkalat ng resulta at suriin ang di-inaasahang pagkakaiba. Hindi patunay ng tamang paliwanag ang repeatability; dapat makatarungang sinusubok ng paraan ang nilalayong tanong.

statements.text:
How do we know carbon is in our breath?

Breathe into clear limewater, and it turns cloudy! This shows your breath has carbon dioxide, made from the carbon your body used.
statements.tl:
Paano natin malalaman na may carbon sa hininga natin?

Ihinga mo sa malinaw na limewater, at magiging malabo ito! Ipinapakita nito na may carbon dioxide sa hininga mo.

statements.text: Stalactites in the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River form when dissolved calcium carbonate precipitates out of water as a solid!
statements.tl: Ang mga stalactite sa Puerto Princesa Subterranean River ay nabubuo kapag ang dissolved calcium carbonate ay nag-precipitate mula sa tubig bilang isang solid!

statements.text: For a fair test, scientists change only one thing, like the gas tested, and keep all other conditions exactly the same!
statements.tl: Sa patas na test, isang bagay lang ang binabago ng scientists, gaya ng gas na sinusuri, at pareho ang lahat ng ibang kondisyon!

statements.text: The independent variable in the limewater test is the gas bubbled in, like your breath or plain air!
statements.tl: Ang independent variable sa limewater test ay ang gas na pinabubula, gaya ng hininga mo o plain air!

statements.text:
What is the dependent variable?

It's what scientists watch for: whether the clear limewater turns cloudy or stays clear!
statements.tl:
Ano ang dependent variable?

Ito ang tinitingnan ng scientists: kung ang malinaw na limewater ay magiging malabo o mananatiling malinaw!

statements.text: To keep the test fair, scientists use the exact same amount of limewater and the same size test tube for every trial!
statements.tl: Para maging patas ang test, gumagamit ang scientists ng parehong dami ng limewater at parehong laki ng test tube sa bawat trial!

statements.text: First, pour clear limewater into a test tube, then bubble the gas through it using a clean straw or tube!
statements.tl: Una, ibuhos ang malinaw na limewater sa test tube, tapos pabulain ang gas gamit ang malinis na straw o tube!

statements.text:
Why use fresh limewater?

Because old limewater might already be cloudy from absorbing carbon dioxide in the air!
statements.tl:
Bakit gagamit ng fresh na limewater?

Kasi ang lumang limewater ay maaaring malabo na dahil sa pagsipsip ng carbon dioxide sa hangin!

statements.text: A good record writes down the starting color and the change, using clear words like 'clear' and 'milky white'!
statements.tl: Ang magandang record ay isinusulat ang panimulang kulay at pagbabago, gamit ang malinaw na salita gaya ng 'malinaw' at 'gatas na puti'!

statements.text:
What does milky white limewater tell you?

It means carbon dioxide gas was hiding in your sample! That milky color is the proof.
statements.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng gatas na puting limewater?

Ibig sabihin may carbon dioxide gas sa sample mo! Yung gatas na kulay ang ebidensya.

statements.text:
How do you do a fair test for precipitate?

Keep the same amount of silver nitrate solution and only change the liquid you add to it!
statements.tl:
Paano gumawa ng fair test para sa precipitate?

Panatilihin ang parehong dami ng silver nitrate solution at baguhin lang ang liquid na idinadagdag mo!

statements.text:
How can you compare how much precipitate forms?

Let the mixture sit for the same amount of time, then check the solid that settles at the bottom!
statements.tl:
Paano mo ikukumpara kung gaano karaming precipitate ang nabubuo?

Hayaang nakababad ang mixture sa parehong tagal, tapos tingnan ang solid na nasa ilalim!

statements.text: Regular air contains a small amount of carbon dioxide! Bubbling enough air through limewater can eventually turn it cloudy, though more slowly than exhaled breath.
statements.tl: May kaunting carbon dioxide ang karaniwang hangin! Maaaring magpalabo sa limewater ang sapat na hanging pinabula rito, pero mas mabagal kaysa sa ibinugang hininga.

statements.text:
How do scientists check if river or pond water has chloride?

They add silver nitrate to the water! If a white precipitate appears, chloride may be present!
statements.tl:
Paano sinusuri ng mga scientist kung may chloride ang tubig sa ilog o lawa?

Nagdadagdag sila ng silver nitrate sa tubig! Kapag may puting precipitate na lumabas, maaaring may chloride doon!

statements.text:
How do scientists record observations without using numbers?

They write down qualitative data like 'turned cloudy' or 'white solid formed' in a table!
statements.tl:
Paano inirekord ng mga scientist ang obserbasyon nang walang numbers?

Isinusulat nila ang qualitative data tulad ng 'naging malabo' o 'may puting solid na nabuo' sa isang table!

statements.text: You need energy to break a bond and pull atoms apart! That is why a stronger bond is much harder to break.
statements.tl: Kailangan ng energy para sirain ang bond at ihiwalay ang mga atomo! Kaya ang mas matibay na bond ay mas mahirap buwagin.
statements.source: NRC PS1.A (grade 12): one must provide at least the binding energy to take a molecule apart

statements.text: In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged as chemical bonds break or form, producing substances with different chemical identities. A change in attraction alone is not enough to prove a chemical reaction: melting ice changes how water molecules interact, but they remain H2O molecules. Use evidence for a new substance, not just a change of state.
statements.tl: Sa chemical reaction, muling naaayos ang atoms habang napuputol o nabubuo ang chemical bonds, at nagkakaroon ng mga sangkap na iba ang chemical identity. Hindi sapat ang pagbabago ng pag-akit lamang: nagbabago ang ugnayan ng water molecules kapag natutunaw ang yelo, ngunit H2O pa rin sila. Gumamit ng ebidensiya ng bagong sangkap, hindi pagbabago lamang ng estado.
statements.source: AAAS 4D/M13: substances combine when atoms combine in new ways; NRC PS1.B

statements.text: When new bonds form, no atoms are lost or created! They just rearrange, keeping the same elements before and after.
statements.tl: Kapag gumagawa ng bagong bond, walang nawawala o nadadagdag na atomo! Nag-aayos lang sila, kaya pareho ang mga elemento bago at pagkatapos.

statements.text:
Can a compound be broken apart?

Yes! Passing an electrical current through some compounds can break the chemical bonds and separate them back into their elements.
statements.tl:
Maaari bang paghiwalayin ang isang compound?

Oo! Ang pagdaan ng electrical current sa ilang compound ay kayang putulin ang chemical bonds at paghiwalayin sila pabalik sa kanilang mga element.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1TRBVi24YbCDyvZDxvDqzl9k5i6M6gKL4), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The overall equation for photosynthesis is six carbon dioxide molecules plus six water molecules, using light energy, to produce one glucose molecule and six oxygen molecules.
statements.tl: Ang kabuuang equation ng photosynthesis ay anim na carbon dioxide molecules plus anim na water molecules, gamit ang light energy, para makagawa ng isang glucose molecule at anim na oxygen molecules.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1c_-Ss80KA8VSe47Z4u9MTYZgb9nwo4K-), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How does lightning help plants?

Air is full of nitrogen, but its atoms are stuck too tightly for plants to use. Lightning's heat is strong enough to break them apart into new, usable substances.
statements.tl:
Paano tinutulungan ng kidlat ang halaman?

Puno ng nitrogen ang hangin, pero sobrang higpit ng pagkakadikit ng mga atom nito kaya hindi magamit ng halaman. Ang init ng kidlat ay sapat para hiwalayin ang mga ito at gumawa ng bagong sangkap.

statements.text:
What happens to the air when lightning strikes?

Right along the lightning's path, the air gets extremely hot, making its nitrogen and oxygen combine into nitrogen oxides -- the first step toward helping the soil.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa hangin kapag may kidlat?

Sa mismong daanan ng kidlat, umiinit nang sobra ang hangin kaya nagsasama ang nitrogen at oxygen dito para bumuo ng nitrogen oxides -- ang unang hakbang tungo sa pagtulong sa lupa.

statements.text: Rust is actually called iron oxide — a brand new substance made when iron and oxygen join forces together!
statements.tl: Ang kalawang ay tinatawag na iron oxide — isang bagong sangkap na nabubuo kapag nagkasama ang bakal at oxygen!

statements.text: In a chemical change, a brand new substance forms! It is completely different from the original material you started with.
statements.tl: Sa kemikal na pagbabago, nabubuo ang isang bagong sangkap! Iba na ito sa orihinal na bagay na ginamit mo.

statements.text:
Why is burning wood a chemical change?

Because it turns into ash, smoke, and gas that are very different from the original wood!
statements.tl:
Bakit kemikal na pagbabago ang pagsunog ng kahoy?

Dahil nagiging abo, usok, at gas ito na ibang-iba sa orihinal na kahoy!

statements.text: Iron rusting is a chemical change! The iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a brand new substance called rust.
statements.tl: Ang pagkalawang ng bakal ay kemikal na pagbabago! Nagrereaksyon ito sa oksiheno at tubig para bumuo ng bagong sangkap na kalawang.

statements.text: Signs like a color change are just clues! You still need to check if a truly new substance was actually formed.
statements.tl: Ang mga senyales gaya ng pagbabago ng kulay ay palatandaan lang! Kailangan mo pa ring tiyakin kung talagang may bagong sangkap na nabuo.

statements.text: Rusting of iron is a slow chemical reaction between iron, oxygen, and water. It doesn't fizz like vinegar and baking soda, but it still forms a new substance!
statements.tl: Ang pagkalawang ng bakal ay isang mabagal na chemical reaction sa pagitan ng iron, oxygen, at tubig. Hindi ito bumubula, ngunit chemical reaction pa rin itong bumubuo ng bagong sangkap!

statements.text: The elements in a compound cannot be separated easily! You need a chemical change to break it apart.
statements.tl: Hindi basta-basta mahihiwalay ang mga elemento sa isang compound! Kailangan mo ng chemical change para bungkagin ito.

statements.text:
What happens when atoms bond together?

The new compound has totally different properties! Salt is safe to eat, even though sodium and chlorine alone are dangerous.
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagbond ang mga atomo?

Ang bagong compound ay may kakaibang katangian! Ligtas kainin ang asin, kahit mapanganib ang sodium at chlorine mag-isa.

statements.text: During hydration, water bonds with cement to form tiny crystals that link everything tightly together!
statements.tl: Sa proseso ng hydration, nakikipag-ugnay ang tubig sa semento at bumubuo ng maliliit na crystal na nagdurugtong sa lahat!

statements.text:
How does bleach remove a stain?

Through a chemical change! It breaks apart the color molecules, making the stain's color disappear from the cloth.
statements.tl:
Paano tinatanggal ng bleach ang mantsa?

Sa pamamagitan ng kemikal na pagbabago! Sinisira nito ang molekula ng kulay, kaya nawawala ang kulay ng mantsa sa damit.

statements.text:
How is plastic made from tiny pieces?

Tiny units called monomers join together in a process called polymerization to form plastic!
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang plastic mula sa maliliit na piraso?

Ang maliliit na yunit na tinatawag na monomer ay nagdurugtong-dugtong sa proseso na tinatawag na polymerization para makabuo ng plastic!

statements.text: The outer electrons of atoms act like glue, joining them together to form substances!
statements.tl: Ang mga panlabas na mga elektron ng atomo ang nagdudugtong sa kanila upang bumuo ng mga sangkap!

statements.text: A dot-and-cross diagram uses dots and crosses to show which atom each valence electron in a bond came from!
statements.tl: Ang dot-and-cross diagram ay gumagamit ng mga tuldok at krus para ipakita kung saang atomo galing ang bawat valence electron sa isang bond!

statements.text: Valence electrons are the electrons in an atom's outermost shell! They are the boss that decides how the atom will bond with other atoms.
statements.tl: Ang valence electrons ay ang mga electrons sa pinakalabas na shell ng isang atomo! Sila ang nagpapasya kung paano makikipag-bond ang atomo sa ibang atomo.

statements.text: The Lewis Electron Dot Structure of sodium shows the symbol Na with one dot, because sodium has one valence electron.
statements.tl: Ang Lewis Electron Dot Structure ng sodium ay nagpapakita ng simbolong Na na may isang tuldok, dahil may isang valence electron ang sodium.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1DV-TSFyLqAWydLpiLHMBHRpOdPLe_nDH), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Covalent bonding happens when two nonmetals share pairs of valence electrons instead of transferring them.
statements.tl: Ang covalent bonding ay nangyayari kapag ang dalawang nonmetal ay naghahati ng pares ng valence electrons imbes na ilipat ang mga ito.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1Etyuf8FrzuhS9Vf_NrODPWnehq3sQCGi), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How can I easily see the valence electrons of an atom?

Draw the element's symbol, then place dots around it to represent its valence electrons!
statements.tl:
Paano ko madaling makikita ang mga valence electron ng isang atom?

Iguhit ang simbolo ng elemento, pagkatapos ay lagyan ng mga tuldok sa paligid nito upang kumatawan sa mga valence electron nito!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1JuD1DgG__dcHh86xu0R6B3oLftUvefHc), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: The total number of valence electrons before and after covalent bonding stays the same, following the Law of Conservation of Matter.
statements.tl: Ang kabuuang bilang ng valence electrons bago at pagkatapos ng covalent bonding ay nananatiling pareho, alinsunod sa Law of Conservation of Matter.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1OqmK9SKhXu8fRm6d_kT5qmM3B7E7p9Wl), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Iodine monochloride forms when one iodine atom and one chlorine atom, each with 7 valence electrons, share one electron pair so both reach 8.
statements.tl: Nabubuo ang iodine monochloride kapag ang isang iodine atom at isang chlorine atom, na parehong may 7 valence electrons, ay nagbahagi ng isang electron pair para pareho silang umabot sa 8.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1QQVPx5gTh9yEEAXDkBGgrjBjPXg_itUY), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: In carbon dioxide, one carbon atom with 4 valence electrons shares two electron pairs with each of two oxygen atoms, making 4 bonding pairs and leaving 4 lone pairs on the oxygen atoms.
statements.tl: Sa carbon dioxide, ang isang carbon atom na may 4 valence electrons ay nagbabahagi ng dalawang electron pairs sa bawat isa sa dalawang oxygen atoms, kaya nabubuo ang 4 bonding pairs at natitira ang 4 lone pairs sa mga oxygen atoms.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1QQVPx5gTh9yEEAXDkBGgrjBjPXg_itUY), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: An electron dot diagram uses dots around an element's symbol to show only its valence electrons, making them easy to count.
statements.tl: Ang electron dot diagram ay gumagamit ng mga tuldok sa paligid ng simbolo ng elemento upang ipakita lamang ang valence electrons nito, kaya madali silang bilangin.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1SpiM8PqBpOuknkcmPslgGbG6CKTkHQsZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Hydrogen has the electron configuration 1s1, so it has exactly one valence electron in its only energy level.
statements.tl: Ang hydrogen ay may electron configuration na 1s1, kaya mayroon itong eksaktong isang valence electron sa nag-iisa nitong energy level.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1qUYN0USdQvm1dkGeaiOJnqaHhKmWuEJq), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How do we find carbon's valence electrons from its configuration?

Carbon is 1s2 2s2 2p2, so we look at the highest level, 2, and add its electrons: 2 + 2 = 4 valence electrons!
statements.tl:
Paano makikita ang valence electron ng carbon mula sa configuration nito?

Ang carbon ay 1s2 2s2 2p2, kaya tinitingnan natin ang pinakamataas na level, 2, at pinagsasama ang mga electron nito: 2 + 2 = 4 na valence electron!
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1qUYN0USdQvm1dkGeaiOJnqaHhKmWuEJq), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Carbon has the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p2, with four valence electrons, placing it in group 14 of the periodic table.
statements.tl: Ang carbon ay may electron configuration na 1s2 2s2 2p2, na may apat na valence electrons, kaya ito ay nasa group 14 ng periodic table.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1sxhJG0I1u3GY6CsBxS8c-XUBvBVk_Nwg), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Atoms join together to fill their outer electron shell, because a full shell makes them more stable!
statements.tl: Nag-uugnay ang mga atomo upang maging puno ang panlabas na shell ng electron, dahil mas matatag sila kapag puno na!
statements.source: DepEd Science 9 CG (Matter); AAAS BSL Ch.4 — octet/stable shell

statements.text: In a covalent bond, the shared pair of electrons counts for both atoms! This makes each atom's outer shell seem full.
statements.tl: Sa covalent bond, ang pinaghahatiang pares ng elektron ay para sa parehong atomo! Kaya tila puno ang panlabas na shell ng dalawa.
statements.source: DepEd Science 9 CG (Matter); AAAS BSL Ch.4

statements.text:
How many bonds can an atom form?

The number of valence electrons helps decide! For example, carbon has four valence electrons, so it usually forms four bonds.
statements.tl:
Ilang bond ang kayang buuin ng isang atomo?

Ang bilang ng valence electrons ang tumutulong magtakda! Halimbawa, ang carbon ay may apat na valence electrons, kaya karaniwang bumubuo ito ng apat na bonds.

statements.text: A Lewis dot structure is a cool diagram using dots to show an atom's valence electrons and how they share to form chemical bonds!
statements.tl: Ang Lewis dot structure ay isang kawili-wiling diagram na gumagamit ng tuldok para ipakita ang valence electrons ng atom at kung paano sila nag-share para gumawa ng chemical bonds!
statements.source: encyclopedia-stable consensus; NRC PS1.A (atomic structure and bonding)

statements.text:
Why don't noble gases react with other elements?

Helium, neon, and argon have full outermost electron shells! Since they're already stable, they don't need to form bonds with anything.
statements.tl:
Bakit hindi nagre-react ang mga noble gases?

Ang helium, neon, at argon ay may punong outermost electron shells! Dahil stable na sila, hindi na kailangan ng iba pang bonds.

statements.text: The electron dot diagram for oxygen shows the symbol O with six dots around it, one for each valence electron.
statements.tl: Ang electron dot diagram para sa oxygen ay nagpapakita ng simbolong O na may anim na tuldok sa paligid nito, isa para sa bawat valence electron.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1SpiM8PqBpOuknkcmPslgGbG6CKTkHQsZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why does oxygen have six valence electrons?

Oxygen's atomic number is eight! Two electrons fill the inner shell, leaving six as valence electrons in the outer shell.
statements.tl:
Bakit anim ang valence electrons ng oxygen?

Ang atomic number ng oxygen ay walo! Dalawang electrons ang pumupuno sa inner shell, nag-iiwan ng anim na valence electrons sa outer shell.

statements.text: Sodium has one valence electron from group 1. It does not match oxygen, which has six from group 16!
statements.tl: Ang sodium ay may isang valence electron mula sa grupo 1. Hindi ito tugma sa oxygen na may anim mula sa grupo 16!

statements.text: For main-group elements using the older IA–VIIIA labels, the A-group number usually gives the number of valence electrons in the outermost shell; helium has two.
statements.tl: Sa main-group elements na gumagamit ng lumang label na IA–VIIIA, karaniwang katumbas ng numero ng A-group ang bilang ng valence electron sa pinakalabas na shell; dalawa ang sa helium.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-sPFSnUoT76f1lJCbDPqrnwqO-qBcJSb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: An oxygen atom has six valence electrons in its outermost shell, so it needs two more to become stable.
statements.tl: Ang oxygen atom ay may anim na valence electrons sa pinakalabas nitong shell, kaya kailangan pa nito ng dalawa para maging stable.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1SpiM8PqBpOuknkcmPslgGbG6CKTkHQsZ), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Oxygen, with eight electrons, has the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p4, giving it six valence electrons in its second energy level.
statements.tl: Ang oxygen, na may walong electron, ay may electron configuration na 1s2 2s2 2p4, kaya mayroon itong anim na valence electron sa ikalawang energy level nito.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1qUYN0USdQvm1dkGeaiOJnqaHhKmWuEJq), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
How many valence electrons does oxygen have?

Oxygen sits in group 16 of the periodic table! This means it has six valence electrons, which are the ones in its outer shell.
statements.tl:
Ilang valence electrons ang mayroon sa oxygen?

Nasa group 16 ng periodic table ang oxygen! Kaya mayroon itong anim na valence electrons, ang mga electron na nasa outer shell nito.

statements.text: To find oxygen's valence electrons, just find it on the table and read its main-group number! Group 16 means six outer electrons.
statements.tl: Para mahanap ang valence electrons ng oxygen, hanapin ito sa table at basahin ang main-group number nito! Ang group 16 ay anim na outer electrons.

statements.text: On older tables, oxygen is in group VIA! The Roman six is the exact same count, meaning oxygen has six valence electrons.
statements.tl: Sa mga lumang periodic table, nasa group VIA ang oxygen! Ang Roman six ay parehong bilang, kaya ang oxygen ay may anim na valence electrons.

statements.text: For groups 13 to 18, except helium, just subtract ten from the group number! Oxygen is group 16, and 16 minus 10 is six valence electrons.
statements.tl: Para sa groups 13 hanggang 18, maliban sa helium, ibawas lang ang sampu sa group number! Ang oxygen ay group 16, at 16 minus 10 ay anim na valence electrons.

statements.text:
Which shell holds oxygen's valence electrons?

Oxygen is in period 2! This means its valence shell is the second shell, which holds those six outer electrons.
statements.tl:
Aling shell ang nagtataglay ng valence electrons ng oxygen?

Nasa period 2 ang oxygen! Kaya ang valence shell nito ay ang pangalawang shell, na siyang nagtataglay ng anim na outer electrons.

statements.text: Oxygen's simple shell pattern is two, then six! That six is the valence count you also get from its column on the periodic table.
statements.tl: Ang simpleng shell pattern ng oxygen ay dalawa, tapos anim! Ang anim ay ang valence count na makukuha mo rin mula sa column nito sa table.

statements.text: Six valence electrons means oxygen is two short of a full set of eight! That is exactly why it often forms two bonds.
statements.tl: Ang anim na valence electrons ay nangangahulugang ang oxygen ay kulang ng dalawa para sa buong set na walo! Kaya madalas itong bumubuo ng dalawang bonds.

statements.text: Sulfur sits under oxygen in the same group, so it also has six valence electrons! Remember, the column, not the row, gives that number.
statements.tl: Ang sulfur ay nasa ilalim ng oxygen sa parehong group, kaya mayroon din itong anim na valence electrons! Ang column, hindi ang row, ang nagbibigay ng bilang.

statements.text:
How many valence electrons does fluorine have?

Fluorine sits one column right of oxygen! So fluorine has seven valence electrons, while oxygen in group 16 has six.
statements.tl:
Ilan ang valence electrons ng fluorine?

Ang fluorine ay nasa isang column sa kanan ng oxygen! Kaya ang fluorine ay may pitong valence electrons, habang ang oxygen sa group 16 ay may anim.

statements.text: Nitrogen sits one column left of oxygen, so it has five valence electrons! Stepping right to oxygen adds one, making six.
statements.tl: Ang nitrogen ay nasa isang column sa kaliwa ng oxygen, kaya may limang valence electrons ito! Ang paghakbang pakanan sa oxygen ay nagdadagdag ng isa, kaya naging anim.

statements.text: Carbon in group 14 has four valence electrons! Oxygen is two groups farther right, so oxygen has six.
statements.tl: Ang carbon sa group 14 ay may apat na valence electrons! Ang oxygen ay dalawang grupo sa kanan, kaya ang oxygen ay may anim.

statements.text:
What makes the chalcogen family special?

Oxygen heads the chalcogen family, group 16! Its members share six valence electrons, even though their atoms get heavier down the column.
statements.tl:
Ano ang espesyal sa chalcogen family?

Ang oxygen ang nangunguna sa chalcogen family, group 16! Ang mga miyembro nito ay may anim na valence electrons, kahit bumibigat ang atoms pababa sa column.

statements.text:
What happens when an atom loses or gains an electron?

It becomes charged and is called an ion!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag ang atomo ay nawalan o nadagdagan ng electron?

Ito ay nagiging may kargang elektrikal at tinatawag na ion!

statements.text: When an atom loses electrons, it becomes a positively charged ion called a cation! A great example is the sodium ion, Na⁺.
statements.tl: Kapag nawalan ng electrons ang isang atomo, nagiging ion na may positibong karga ito na tinatawag na cation! Ang sodium ion na Na⁺ ay isang magandang halimbawa.
statements.source: AAAS 4D/H2; NRC PS1.A (electron transfer forms ions)

statements.text: When an atom gains extra electrons, it becomes a negatively charged ion called an anion! A common example is the chloride ion, Cl⁻.
statements.tl: Kapag nakakuha ng dagdag na electrons ang isang atomo, nagiging ion na may negatibong karga ito na tinatawag na anion! Ang chloride ion na Cl⁻ ay isang halimbawa.
statements.source: AAAS 4D/H2; NRC PS1.A (electron transfer forms ions)

statements.text: In an ionic bond, positive and negative ions pull toward each other because opposite electric charges attract!
statements.tl: Sa ionic bond, ang positibo at negatibong ion ay naghihilahan dahil ang magkasalungat na electric charge ay nag-aakitan!
statements.source: NRC PS1.A: electrical attractions between charged particles cause atoms to form molecules and structures

statements.text: To form magnesium nitride, three magnesium atoms each lose two electrons and two nitrogen atoms each gain three electrons, giving the formula Mg3N2.
statements.tl: Upang mabuo ang magnesium nitride, tatlong magnesium atom ang bawat isa ay nawawalan ng dalawang electron at dalawang nitrogen atom ang bawat isa ay nagkakaroon ng tatlong electron, na nagbibigay ng formula na Mg3N2.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-sPFSnUoT76f1lJCbDPqrnwqO-qBcJSb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Calcium loses two electrons to become Ca2+ and sulfur gains two electrons to become S2-, so they combine equally to form CaS.
statements.tl: Ang calcium ay nawawalan ng dalawang electron upang maging Ca2+ at ang sulfur ay nagkakaroon ng dalawang electron upang maging S2-, kaya pantay silang nagsasama upang bumuo ng CaS.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-sPFSnUoT76f1lJCbDPqrnwqO-qBcJSb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
Why is sodium nitride written as Na3N?

One nitrogen atom needs three electrons to fill its outer shell, so three sodium atoms each donate one electron, forming Na3N.
statements.tl:
Bakit isinusulat ang sodium nitride bilang Na3N?

Ang isang nitrogen atom ay nangangailangan ng tatlong electron upang mapuno ang kanyang outer shell, kaya tatlong sodium atom ang bawat isa ay nagdo-donate ng isang electron, na bumubuo ng Na3N.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-sPFSnUoT76f1lJCbDPqrnwqO-qBcJSb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Calcium loses two electrons to become Ca2+ and each bromine atom gains one electron to become Br-, so two bromines are needed, forming CaBr2.
statements.tl: Ang calcium ay nawawalan ng dalawang electron upang maging Ca2+ at ang bawat bromine atom ay nagkakaroon ng isang electron upang maging Br-, kaya dalawang bromine ang kailangan, na bumubuo ng CaBr2.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1-sPFSnUoT76f1lJCbDPqrnwqO-qBcJSb), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text: Magnesium oxide, MgO, forms when magnesium loses two electrons to become Mg2+ and oxygen gains two electrons to become O2-.
statements.tl: Ang magnesium oxide, MgO, ay nabubuo kapag ang magnesium ay naglalabas ng dalawang electrons para maging Mg2+ at ang oxygen ay kumukuha ng dalawang electrons para maging O2-.
statements.source: DepEd self-learning module (Drive id 1b5kT2v5ORLqOFueiZcRdl--l0-rS2JKp), paraphrased in a Hiraia card

statements.text:
What happens to electrons when an ionic bond forms?

Metal atoms tend to lose electrons, while nonmetal atoms tend to gain them!
statements.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa mga elektron kapag nabubuo ang isang ionic bond?

Ang mga metal atom ay madaling nawawalan ng elektron, samantalang ang mga nonmetal atom ay madaling tumatanggap ng mga ito!
statements.source: DepEd Science 9 CG (Matter); AAAS BSL Ch.4

statements.text: When an atom loses an electron, it becomes a positive ion called a cation! If it gains an electron, it becomes a negative ion called an anion.
statements.tl: Kapag nawalan ng elektron ang isang atomo, nagiging positibong ion na cation ito! Kapag nakadagdag naman ng elektron, nagiging negatibong ion na anion ito.

statements.text:
How does a neutral atom become an ion?

It becomes an ion when its number of electrons changes, so the electrons and protons no longer match!
statements.tl:
Paano nagiging ion ang isang neutral na atomo?

Nagiging ion ito kapag nagbago ang bilang ng elektron nito, kaya hindi na magkapantay ang elektron at proton!
statements.source: DepEd Science 9 CG (Matter); AAAS BSL Ch.4

statements.text: Ionic compounds usually form from a metal and a nonmetal! For example, sodium (a metal) and chlorine (a nonmetal) form table salt.
statements.tl: Ang mga ionic compound ay karaniwang nabubuo mula sa isang metal at isang di-metal! Halimbawa, ang sodium (metal) at chlorine (di-metal) ay bumubuo ng table salt.

statements.text: An ionic bond is held together by the pull between a positive ion and a negative ion—opposite charges attract each other!
statements.tl: Ang ionic bond ay hawak ng puwersa ng pagkakaakit sa pagitan ng positibong ion at negatibong ion—magkasalungat na singil, nagkakadikit!

statements.text: When salt forms, sodium gives one electron to chlorine! Sodium becomes a positive ion, and chlorine becomes a negative ion.
statements.tl: Kapag nabubuo ang asin, nagbibigay ang sodium ng isang elektron sa chlorine! Nagiging positibong ion ang sodium, at nagiging negatibong ion ang chlorine.

statements.text:
How do atoms stick together in table salt?

In an ionic bond, one atom gives electrons to another, giving them opposite charges that attract—like sodium and chlorine in sodium chloride!
statements.tl:
Paano nagdidikit ang mga atom sa asin?

Sa ionic bond, nagbibigay ang isang atom ng elektron sa kabilang atom, kaya nagkaroón sila ng magkasalungat na singil na nag-aakit—gaya ng sodium at chlorine sa sodium chloride!

statements.text:
How does an ionic bond form?

When a metal atom GIVES its electron to a nonmetal atom! After this, both become charged and attract each other.
statements.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang ionic bond?

Kapag IBINIGAY ng metal atom ang electron nito sa nonmetal atom! Pagkatapos, nagiging may charge sila at nagkaakit.

statements.text:
Why do ions stick together?

Because positive (+) and negative (-) charges attract each other like magnets! This strong pulling force holds the ionic compound together so it won't fall apart.
statements.tl:
Bakit nagdidikit ang mga ion?

Dahil ang positive (+) at negative (-) ay magkaakit parang magnet! Ang puwersang ito ang humahawak sa ionic compound para hindi ito magkalas-kalas.
